map.segment: Collection: arm to counting verdict (pre-check, fingerprint smoke, NO window, settle, session chain, agent census and pause, session desk, attempt line and email). Checkout labels: jw = scratchpad/jw (main); bytes = scratchpad/wt/bytes (work/2026-10-23-by-slots-draft).
map.summary:
WHERE A SESSION'S MAC TIME GOES. The cycle times below come from RECORD.md timestamps; the arithmetic is mine.
- BYTES pass 1, t0 to t0: s3 to s4 was 575 to 610 min, s4 to s5 was 610 min, s5 to s6 was 521 min.
- Each cycle is three parts:
  - Before t0 (pre-check, arm notice, smoke, smoke desk, ARM_WAIT, launch lead): 88 to 114 min. s2 1 h 33 m after resume, s3 114, s4 113, s5 109, s6 88.
  - Chain: 316 to 388 min (records 118cc6cb:5, abb6de94:5, 4f20ade7:5, 7326d37c:6).
  - Desk on the Mac: 95.6 to 108.9 min, of which the harvest is 88 to 101.4.
- So the chain is about 61 to 64 % of Mac wall time. Before t0 is about 18 to 20 %. The desk is about 17 to 18 %.
- Inside the chain, block 5/6 measured 90.5 min of fixed parts against 265 min of science, a science share of 74.5 % (jw:docs/design/block6_collection_draft.md:249-266). BYTES split per stage was not measured (INFERRED to be similar).
- So science runs are about 45 to 49 % of Mac wall time. Inside each run the idle baseline is 83 of 116 s (design:554), so the measured request itself is only about 13 % of Mac time (INFERRED product).
- Block 6 gives the same picture: start-to-start 7.9 to 9.6 h (mean 8.7 h), chain 4.6 to 5.6 h, harvest plus desk about 1.5 h, smoke about 50 min (jw:docs/process_traces/2026-10-20-magistrate-c634f6f3/RECORD.md:41).

YIELD PER MAC-HOUR.
- Block 6: 9 counting sessions from 10-17 20:51 to 10-21 about 02:45, about 78 h, so about 8.7 h per counting session (RUN_STATE 59; c634f6f3:31-38).
- BYTES pass 1: from 10-25 07:55 to 10-27 12:24, about 52.5 h for 4 counting sessions, 3 of them claim-usable. That is 13 h per counting session and 17.5 h per usable one (items 71-78).
- Lost to process, not to physics of the experiment:
  - s1-p1: 265 min, a sidecar refusal. The smoke passed and the yield alert fired only after the whole chain (8b6b2b12:7-11, 36-40).
  - s6-p1: a 276 min chain, then excluded. A Codex daemon held the census for the full 7,200 s pause limit (item 78; a46602ae:4-7).
  - Block 6 r2-alpha: a wrong smoke hold (item 52) forced an extra alpha session, about 8 h (INFERRED).

PHYSICS-REQUIRED (KEEP):
- Captures, the reference triplets and midpoint, the corpus up to 12 valid runs, idle baselines of at least 60 s, cooldowns, waiting admission, settles.
- Pre-check physics: contention, instrument, agents and HID idle, thermal, power, clock, disk, model hashes.
- Sleep guard, the agent census, the harvest's exclusions and cell minimums, the structure check.

INHERITED CAUTION (cut or move):
1. The 90-min harvest blocks the Mac before the next pre-check (desk_lane.py:185-261 runs synchronously inside loop.py:580-601).
2. A fingerprint-triggered smoke (~50 min) for every new pack id. fingerprint.py:56-60 puts pack_id in the key, so all 12 BYTES packs smoke, including p2 packs whose models and code equal p1's. On record the smoke caught nothing in block 6 or BYTES, made one wrong hold and missed s1-p1's defect.
3. A 30-min NO window that is dead time when no smoke runs (loop.py:489). Ed has not used it on record.
4. Scheduling latency: one state handler per 300 s launchd tick (loop.py:91-101; com.joulewise.b6loop.plist.template:7). That is about 9 transitions per cycle, about 20 to 40 min (INFERRED).
5. The in-chain bound derivation (~12 min) that "decides nothing" (jw registration:319-321).
6. 6 corpus runs (~15 min) beyond the 12 valid ones the analysis uses (bytes reg:103; registration.py corpus_cap 12).
7. A 2 h pause that ran to its stop against an idle launchd daemon.
8. A headless magistrate on the Mac every session, duplicating the loop's mailer.

BIGGEST WIN: MOVE THE HARVEST TO THE MACBOOK AIR.
- On the Mac, the desk shrinks to the ledger resume-finalize and pin advance, a raw-structure preflight, and a hashed transfer (zstd stream or Thunderbolt). That is about 15 min (INFERRED), down from about 100.
- The harvest (unchanged code, a pure function of the bytes; jw registration §4:433-435) then runs on the Air while the next chain measures.
- The Air rather than the cloud: it is the same macOS arm64 toolchain, has single-core speed near the M3 Max (so the frozen 120 s refit deadline is unlikely to fire; ED-RULING:53-67, cadence plan §3), and a harvest fault there is a re-run, not a loss.
- Combined with fingerprint-without-pack, notice-during-desk and draining ticks, the projected cycle is chain + about 60 to 70 min instead of chain + 200 to 220 min (INFERRED). That is about 26 % less Mac time per session.
- The remaining BYTES work is s1-p1 retry, s6-p1 retry and six p2 sessions. At about 540 min per cycle that is about 72 h; projected it is about 53 h. The roughly 19 h saved can go to the block-5 dry run that ED-RULING 6a puts ahead of BYTES, before the 2026-11-02 00:00 PST end (bytes reg:105).

SESSION LENGTH: KEEP ABOUT 6 H.
- Half sessions cost 46 % more machine time and give 1.74x wider intervals (design:268-303).
- With desk and smoke off the Mac the penalty falls to about 31 % (INFERRED), still a loss.
- The observed stop rate, 0.026 per hour, is far below the 0.16 per hour break-even (design:292-296).

ITEM 78 CURE, in order of strength:
1. Ed and every agent (magistrate, Codex CLI, Claude) work on the Air; the measurement Mac runs no agent.
2. A guard on the Mac that refuses `codex` and `claude` while `collection.active` exists (design 6.3 item 1, Ed's file).
3. No Codex app or auto-updater on the measurement Mac (INFERRED setting).
4. A loop-side remedy (loop.py is not number-bearing): when the pause marker shows only no-TTY daemons reparented to launchd, run `codex app-server daemon stop` and SIGTERM the updater after about 10 min instead of waiting 2 h.
5. The same remedy in pre-check next to reap_orphans.

steps.name: Measurement checkout, pin, code_check and 40-min machine test (per collection-code change)
steps.what: Clone at a pinned commit. code_check refuses number-bearing changes that no executing review covered. A ~40 min machine test (agent pause, idle disturbance to the cap, meter unplugged) runs once per collection-code change before arming.
steps.protects: New collection code that silently loses runs or mis-flags them, e.g. a driver that drops the agent.presence flag so agent-overlapping runs count.
steps.cost: ~40 min of Mac time per collection-code change, plus checkout build. Not per session.
steps.caught_real_defects: YES. MT-20261016 caught the smoke.prepare sidecar defect (round 1 could never have armed) and agent.presence built without monotonic_raw_ns (agent-overlap runs could have counted) (RUN_STATE 41). MT-20261017T1735Z led to PR #501's three desk defects: the busy-fraction veto excluded admitted runs, idle-skip stages were read as missing, and cap-skip rc 1 was failed (RUN_STATE 43).
steps.redundant_with: Partly with CI. CI cannot exercise launchd context, the sampler or a real agent pause.
steps.proposal: Keep it as the one machine-level gate per collection-code change. Never run it per session or per pack.
steps.saves: 0 (already lightened from per-pack fault rehearsals plus round 0, ~28.5 h, by design 13/13.1)

steps.name: Loop scheduling: NEXT/ROTATE/state transitions on a 300 s launchd tick
steps.what: tick() runs exactly one state handler and returns. launchd fires every 300 s. NEXT, PRECHECK, SMOKE_RUN, SMOKE_DESK, ARM_WAIT, SESSION_RUN, SESSION_DESK and ROTATE each wait for the next tick.
steps.protects: Lock discipline and crash-safe state.json between steps.
steps.cost: About 9 transitions per cycle at up to 300 s each, about 20-40 min of idle Mac per cycle (INFERRED from code; not measured).
steps.caught_real_defects: Not a check.
steps.redundant_with: n/a
steps.proposal: Inside one tick, keep calling the next handler while the state changed and the new state is not a waiting state (ARM_WAIT before notice+1800, WAIT_PHYSICS, *_RUN polling). Persist state.json after each handler as now. Add a test that a no-smoke cycle reaches SESSION_RUN in one tick after ARM_WAIT clears. loop.py is not on NUMBER_BEARING_PATHS.
steps.saves: ~15-30 min per session (INFERRED)

steps.name: PRECHECK physics readings
steps.what: Measures directly: clock rate over 60 s; AC attached and battery within 200 mA; thermal level 0; contention 180 s clean at ≤0.05 CPU-s/s (cap 600 s), with orphaned fixtures reaped; agent census empty and HID idle ≥600 s; disk ≥ P (+ smoke share); instrument 300 frames at median ≤150 ms; evicted captures restored; model hashes; runtime versions. On a failure: WAIT_PHYSICS and re-measure every 240 s.
steps.protects: Arming into a machine that would produce contaminated or unmeasurable runs: slow sampler, background analysis daemons, an agent, sleep, a full disk.
steps.cost: ~5 min per check (design 3.3, unmeasured in the records). It runs twice per cycle (PRECHECK and ARM_WAIT).
steps.caught_real_defects: YES. mediaanalysisd at 1.86-1.91 CPU-s/s, and a 218-298 ms sampler because the loop job was ProcessType Background; this would have degraded every run (RUN_STATE 46, 47). Agent census refused BY-H2 at t0 with zero runs (RUN_STATE 67). Lead checks found runaway fseventsd and fileproviderd (f18a96e1 tally). The arm census already catches the Codex daemon (a46602ae:5).
steps.redundant_with: The in-run idle admission catches the same contention later, but only after a run is spent.
steps.proposal: Keep it on the Mac. Add the Codex app-server daemon to the reap step: the precheck already reaps parent-pid-1 fixture orphans; do the same for `codex app-server daemon`/`pid-update-loop` with no TTY. precheck.py is not number-bearing.
steps.saves: Prevents waits; protects whole sessions

steps.name: PRECHECK certain_exclusion (acceptance A on a synthetic full session, nominal and margin)
steps.what: Runs the harvest's acceptance function on a synthetic session built from the plan and the median of the last 24 captures. If A refuses, the pack is held before t0 (a hold, not a loss). The margin case only writes 'thin margin'.
steps.protects: Spending ~6 h on a session the registered analysis would certainly exclude, e.g. a stale acceptance (block 5 BETA a4/a5).
steps.cost: ~2 min, inside C2 (design 3.3: 'item 26's acceptance helper takes about 2 min').
steps.caught_real_defects: No certain_exclusion hold appears in RUN_STATE items 41-78 or the 10-1x/10-2x records. The class it targets cost block 5 two attempts (design 3.2 row 'BETA a4 and a5').
steps.redundant_with: The harvest acceptance after the session, which comes too late to save the session.
steps.proposal: Keep it; it is cheap. No change.

steps.name: Fingerprint and smoke decision
steps.what: The fingerprint is code commit, dirty flag, OS build, model hashes, runtime versions, boot session, meter device, powermetrics version and pack {pack_id, tree_id}. A smoke runs when it differs from the last passing smoke of the same pack_id.
steps.protects: An unexercised change in what a session depends on.
steps.cost: Cheap itself, but it triggers C6. Because pack_id is in the key, every one of the 12 BYTES packs smokes once, including p2 packs with identical models and code (smoke_keep.json p1 and p2 rows are the same models).
steps.caught_real_defects: n/a (decision logic).
steps.redundant_with: The CI test test_every_loop_pack_tree_authenticates_through_its_sidecar now covers committed pack trees (8b6b2b12:19, 26).
steps.proposal: Drop pack_id and tree_id from the smoke-trigger comparison. Compare instead the set of (model hash, runtime, workload config) pairs, and treat a pack whose pairs are all covered by a passing smoke since the last code/OS/boot change as smoked. Pack tree integrity stays with CI and the controller's sidecar check. fingerprint.py and loop.py are not number-bearing.
steps.saves: ~50 min per p2 session x 6 = ~5 h of Mac time in BYTES pass 2

steps.name: Arm notice and 30-min owner NO window
steps.what: Mail at PRECHECK pass with t0_not_before = now+1800. ARM_WAIT returns until notice_sent+1800, then checks a NO reply and the remote STOP ref (git ls-remote).
steps.protects: Ed's chance to veto an arm, e.g. when he wants the Mac.
steps.cost: 0 when a smoke runs (it overlaps). 30 min of idle Mac when no smoke is due.
steps.caught_real_defects: No owner NO in items 41-78 (grep of records for owner_no found none; INFERRED from absence). Ed instead stopped H by hand (RUN_STATE 64).
steps.redundant_with: The STOP file and remote stop ref (loop.py:457-469), which Ed can set at any time.
steps.proposal: Send the next session's arm notice when the previous session enters SESSION_DESK, or when a Mac-side desk (C18) finishes, so the 30 min runs during the desk. Keep the NO and STOP checks at ARM_WAIT. The previous session's line follows in the verdict mail. loop.py is not number-bearing.
steps.saves: Up to 30 min per no-smoke session (~3 h over BYTES pass 2 if C4 is adopted)

steps.name: Smoke collection plus smoke desk
steps.what: A reduced chain (opening capture, 1 start ref, 1 run per module, 1 end ref, closing capture) in a staged clone with a copied ledger. The smoke desk runs the shared harvest and acceptance and classifies pass, physics or fail. A fail holds the pack.
steps.protects: A collection or harvest path that fails structurally on a new fingerprint (launch context, code, OS).
steps.cost: About 50 min per smoke cycle in block 6 (c634f6f3:41): 23-28 min collection plus ~20 min harvest fixed cost (design 3.1). In BYTES pass 1 it ran before every session (new pack each time).
steps.caught_real_defects:
None in 9 block-6 or 6 BYTES sessions:
- Item 52: a wrong smoke_hold on alpha (anchor-fallback rc 1), which cost the r2-alpha slot.
- Item 71: it PASSED while the real s1-p1 collected zero, because smoke.py writes its own sidecar into the staged tree.
- Item 48: false yield alerts every smoke.
- 7209d1b0 rounds 4-6 spent audit findings on smoke-only defects (13 BYTES smokes stopping at export; keep-0 stages).
- The one real smoke-code defect was found by the machine test (item 41).
steps.redundant_with: Pre-check instrument and contention readings (launch context); CI pack-tree test; machine test (C0); the first session's structure check (C20). Registration §4 makes the first real session carry the new-code risk.
steps.proposal: Smoke only when code commit, OS build, runtime versions or boot change (C4). Run the smoke harvest on the MacBook Air, so the Mac's settle and second pre-check overlap it. Never hold a pack on a non-physics smoke result that a full session's own path handles (item 52's queued fix).
steps.saves: ~50 min x (sessions without a code/OS/boot change); ~5 h over BYTES pass 2

steps.name: ARM_WAIT second pre-check, launch lead and settle
steps.what: Fresh physics at t0, then the fingerprint re-check. t0 is 420 s ahead (installer needs 300 s). The driver then reserves the ledger and settles 60 s; every stage starts with its own 60 s idle wait.
steps.protects: Physics drift between the first pre-check and t0 (the smoke loads the machine). The installer race.
steps.cost: ~5 min pre-check + 7 min lead + 3-5 min driver start to first stage + 1 min settle ≈ 16-18 min (design 3.1:119; loop.py:531-532).
steps.caught_real_defects: The census at t0 refused BY-H2 (RUN_STATE 67).
steps.redundant_with: First pre-check (C2) when no smoke ran in between.
steps.proposal: Keep it (physics at t0). If no smoke ran since the first pre-check and less than 10 min passed, the second pre-check may reuse its slow readings (clock and contention), but keep the census and HID idle. Low value; optional.
steps.saves: ≤5 min (optional)

steps.name: Opening and closing calibration captures
steps.what: 59-pulse timing captures at the start (~6 min) and end (~4 min). b_op comes from the session's own two captures. The chain stops at the opening capture if b_pre + s_bracket exceeds the line.
steps.protects: The timing bound b_op that enters every phase check and floor (exclusion grounds P1-P3, N1).
steps.cost: ~10 min per session (design 4.1: 6 + 4).
steps.caught_real_defects: Its N1 code excluded s6-p1 after the agent stop (closing capture missing; a46602ae:7). In block 5 the capture-over-screen (BETA a3) was a rule loss, now converted to a flag (registration 3.2 item 5).
steps.redundant_with: None.
steps.proposal: No change (physics).

steps.name: NEG-8 reference corpus (18 planned runs)
steps.what: 18 runs of the 37 J reference workload. The analysis uses the first 12 valid ones (at least 6 required).
steps.protects: The drift allowance A that enters every bound (N2).
steps.cost: ~45 min (design 4.1). About 6 runs, ~15 min, are reserves used only on losses.
steps.caught_real_defects: The NEG-8 span defect was caught by the #416 audit, not by the corpus (RUN_STATE 69). The corpus itself is measurement.
steps.redundant_with: None for the first 12; runs 13-18 are reserves.
steps.proposal: BYTES p2 keeps 18. The pass-1/pass-2 difference is printed (bytes reg:105), and the corpus also preconditions machine temperature before science (design:297-298), so changing it mid-BYTES adds a confound. New packs: chain-side early stop at 12 succeeded runs plus reserves on loss, as design 14 already decided for new packs.
steps.saves: ~15 min per session for new packs only

steps.name: In-chain bound derivation
steps.what: Derives the drift bound inside the chain after the corpus. Registration: it 'decides nothing (the harvest recomputes the deciding bound)'.
steps.protects: Nothing number-bearing. It is an early sight of the bound.
steps.cost: ~12 min of Mac time per session (design 4.1, BETA a6; not measured for BYTES, INFERRED similar).
steps.caught_real_defects: None on record.
steps.redundant_with: The harvest's recomputation of the deciding bound.
steps.proposal: New packs: remove the stage from the chain, or run it at the desk (Air). BYTES p2: keep it, because it sets the gap and thermal state before the start triplet, and pass comparability matters. Check first whether later stages bind its output (a69c5394:23 says bound_derivation pins settled_corpus.json; INFERRED dependency).
steps.saves: ~12 min per session (new packs)

steps.name: Start, midpoint and end reference runs (3+1+3) and drift screen
steps.what: Reference runs bracketing the science. The drift screen (D1) runs on the survivors. A lost reference is a flag.
steps.protects: Instrument drift across the session (ground D). The allowance uses the triplet means and the midpoint.
steps.caught_real_defects: Screen exclusions: s6-p1 lost its end triplet and was excluded with neg8.survivor_screen_undefined (a46602ae:7), a downstream effect of the agent stop. No D1 failure in block 6/BYTES on record.
steps.redundant_with: None.
steps.proposal: No change (physics/D ground).

steps.name: Science runs with idle baseline, cooldown and waiting admission
steps.what: Each run has an 83 s idle baseline (at least 60 s for the clock fit), the request, and a ~23 s post-request tail. Cooldown releases at 2x the previous baseline, capped at 300 s. Waiting admission retries fresh baselines up to 1,500 s per run and 7,200 s per session.
steps.protects: Idle subtraction and the clock fit. Contamination by a disturbance costs minutes, not runs.
steps.cost: About 74.5 % of the chain is science (design 4.1). A run is 2.25-2.5 min for the reference-sized model; the baseline is 83 of 116 s.
steps.caught_real_defects: Waiting admission absorbed disturbances without losses (design 13). s5-p1's thermal exclusions came from post-request level-1 episodes, a science question, not a process one (a46602ae:8).
steps.redundant_with: None.
steps.proposal: No change for registered packs (nothing changes inside a run). New packs: run design 14's test 8 (short-baseline arm) before registering a shorter baseline.
steps.saves: 0 now; future test 8

steps.name: Agent census and pause (every 30 s, pause between runs, 10 min resume, 7,200 s stop)
steps.what: pgrep '[c]odex|[c]laude'. On a sighting the run in flight ends, the chain pauses, and it resumes 10 min after the last sighting. The overlapping unit is excluded. Cumulative pauses of 7,200 s stop the session (P4).
steps.protects: The 8-47 W draw of an agent contaminating runs.
steps.cost: s6-p1: a 09:35 sighting, 2 h paused, the session ended at 11:35. Chain 276 min plus desk 41.5, not counting, plus a retry (~5.3 h + one cycle).
steps.caught_real_defects: YES (real hazard). Block 5 BETA a2. H interactive agents flagged (RUN_STATE 64). s6-p1 Ed's `codex update` and ChatGPT-app Codex. But the 2 h of the stop were spent on an idle launchd-reparented daemon (a46602ae:4).
steps.redundant_with: The arm census (C2) before t0.
steps.proposal:
Keep the census and the unit exclusion unchanged; they are registered.
1. Ed's interactive Codex and Claude, and all headless agents, run on the MacBook Air, not the measurement Mac.
2. Add Ed's ~/.zshrc guard on the Mac: refuse `codex`/`claude`/`codex update` while ~/night-b6/loop*/collection.active exists (design 6.3 item 1).
3. Remove the Codex app and auto-updater from the measurement Mac (INFERRED that a setting or uninstall exists).
4. Loop-side remedy, in loop.py, which is not number-bearing: while SESSION_RUN and the driver's pause marker exists, if every census match is a no-TTY process with ppid 1 named `codex app-server`/`pid-update-loop`, run `codex app-server daemon stop` and SIGTERM the updater, with a journal row. The pause then ends within ~10 min instead of 7,200 s.
Do not change agent_pause.py: it is number-bearing and would need an executing review and re-pin.
steps.saves: One s6-p1-type loss (~5.3 h of Mac time plus a retry cycle) per event

steps.name: Sleep guard (driver no-sleep assertion and per-run sleep reading)
steps.what: The driver holds its own no-sleep assertion; the keep-awake launchd job is a second layer. Sleep-counting minus sleep-blind clock is read at every run's start and end (excludes at >1 ms).
steps.protects: Runs spanning a sleep (block 5 BETA a4).
steps.cost: Negligible.
steps.caught_real_defects: Block 5 BETA a4 (design 3.2). None in block 6/BYTES (the setting has been in force since 10-10).
steps.redundant_with: The keep-awake job (deliberate second layer).
steps.proposal: No change.

steps.name: Yield alerts (watchdog yield.stage_zero / stage_low)
steps.what: The watchdog compares each stage's yield with its plan and queues notices.
steps.protects: Sessions that run but collect nothing.
steps.cost: Cheap; false alarms on every smoke (item 48).
steps.caught_real_defects: YES but late. It flagged s1-p1's zero yield only after the whole 265 min chain had run; every member had refused in about 0.4 s (8b6b2b12:7, 38).
steps.redundant_with: The structure check at the desk.
steps.proposal: Make it an early stop. The loop polls SESSION_RUN every tick. If the first collection stage ends with 0 succeeded of more than 0 planned, and all failures are the same non-physics refusal, the loop writes STOP for the chain and holds the pack with a structure_defect event. Do this in the loop, not in the driver or chain, which are number-bearing. The session is excluded anyway (S1 structural / N4).
steps.saves: Up to ~4 h of Mac time per zero-yield event

steps.name: Controller plan-tree sidecar refusal (per member)
steps.what: Each member authenticates plan_tree.json through plan_tree.sha256 and refuses if it is absent.
steps.protects: Running a plan whose bytes are not the registered ones (provenance).
steps.cost: It cost s1-p1 (265 min). Otherwise negligible.
steps.caught_real_defects: It refused real, correct registered bytes; the sidecar was missing, the bytes were fine. The magistrate called it a pruning candidate (8b6b2b12:28, 40).
steps.redundant_with: The CI test reading every loop pack through _plan_tree (991358f73). Measurement checkouts are cut from CI-green heads.
steps.proposal: Keep it as it is. Converting it to a flag means touching controller.py (number-bearing, executing review, re-pin), and the CI test already makes the failure unrepeatable. C15's early stop caps any recurrence at one stage.

steps.name: Magistrate activation per session (headless Opus on the Mac waiting for the attempt line)
steps.what: The watchdog launches an agent that polls attempts.jsonl through SESSION_DESK, emails Ed the verdict and exits before PRECHECK.
steps.protects: Human-readable verdict mail and interpretation of anomalies (e.g. s5 thermal led to a council).
steps.cost: ~1.5-2 h of agent wall time per session (4f20ade7 18:54-20:45; abb6de94 08:48-10:40). Duplicate verdict email (283e9802: 'the loop wake emailed it too'). An agent process on the measurement Mac. Fetch slips while armed (RUN_STATE 46: sixth slip).
steps.caught_real_defects: The judgement value is real: s5-p1 cell.below_minimum led to the thermal council (7326d37c:7-9); the item 52 wrong hold was resumed. Routine COLLECTED/ACCEPT verdicts (s2, s3, s4) caught nothing (pruning tallies).
steps.redundant_with: The loop's mailer, which already sends verdict and hold mail (desk design 6.4; loop _event).
steps.proposal: The loop's program mailer sends the routine verdict alone. A magistrate wakes only on HOLD_LOOP, structure_defect, harvest_fault, not counting, a cell below minimum, or Ed's mail. It runs on the MacBook Air (or in the cloud), reading loop state over ssh with argv that cannot match the '[c]odex|[c]laude' census (INFERRED risk: ssh command lines containing '.claude' paths would match).
steps.saves: No agent on the measurement Mac; ~1.5 h of agent time and one duplicate email per routine session

steps.name: Session desk part A: ledger resume-finalize and pin advance
steps.what: desk_lane._advance closes any open bracket slot through recover_calibration_ledger resume-finalize (timeouts 120 then 600 s) or aborts it, then advances the ledger pin, so the next session can reserve.
steps.protects: Calibration ledger custody and continuity (the next session's reservation and b_op provenance).
steps.cost: Inside the desk-minus-harvest residual of 6-8 min, together with the structure check and compression (118cc6cb:5 95-88; abb6de94 100-92; 4f20ade7 108.9-101.4; 7326d37c 95.6-89.1). Split not measured.
steps.caught_real_defects: Records flags on stopped chains (desk_lane.py:113-116); none number-affecting on record.
steps.redundant_with: None.
steps.proposal: Stays on the Mac, before PRECHECK. Order the Mac-side desk as: chain exit, then _advance, then a raw-structure preflight (bundle counts per roster stage from the runs roots, no energy), then a hashed transfer of runs roots, custody, ledger and ledger-referenced captures to the Air, then ROTATE.
steps.saves: n/a (enabler for C19)

steps.name: Session harvest (strict validation, re-reduction, bracket evaluation, acceptance, hidden offsets, export)
steps.what: harvest_b6_session.py on the session's bytes, with a 4 h timeout. It writes the archive, b6-acceptance.json, exclusions, hidden-offset pack records and the blinded export.
steps.protects: The registered exclusions and counting decision; data provenance. It is a pure function of the bytes (reg §4).
steps.cost: 88-101.4 min on the Mac, blocking the next PRECHECK: s2 88, s3 92, s4 101.4, s5 89.1; block 6 88-93. About 18 min of it is a fixed cost of opening historical captures (design 3.1).
steps.caught_real_defects:
YES.

The Mac transfers bytes after C18 (zstd -T0 stream, or a raw copy over a Thunderbolt bridge; every file's SHA-256 checked against custody on arrival).

MEASUREMENT MAC (only what touches the instrument or its ledger):
- Pre-check physics and certain-exclusion.
- Smoke and session collection (chain, captures, references, corpus, runs, census, pause, sleep guard).
- Ledger resume-finalize and pin advance.
- Raw-structure preflight, hashed transfer out, and compression of its own copy.
- The loop process itself.
No agent process at any time.

MACBOOK AIR (macOS arm64, same toolchain; INFERRED chip and disk; confirm at least ~60 GB free for one uncompressed session plus compressed history):
- Session and smoke harvests (unchanged program, identical pinned checkout and venv).
- Full structure check, acceptance, export, compression of its copy.
- Per-session blind analysis and independent recompute (cadence plan section 4).
- Headless magistrate wakes and all of Ed's interactive Codex/Claude work.
It suits real-data harvest better than the cloud because its single-core speed keeps the frozen 120 s refit deadline unlikely to fire (ED-RULING item 6). A firing there is a harvest re-run, not a loss (jw registration:433-435). Risk to check: sustained throttling under passive cooling (INFERRED).

CLOUD (Claude 4 vCPU / 15 GB / ~30 GB; Codex 5 vCPU / 17 GB):
- Code changes for the loop, desk and Air runner.
- Executing reviews, councils, CI, synthetic and fixture tests.
Never raw block-5/6/BYTES bytes: there is no room for 43 GiB sessions uncompressed, and the deadline risk is real (jw:docs/design/analysis_cadence_plan.md:41-54).

The redundancy claim does not hold, and the authority is mislabelled.
(1) p2 packs are not identical to p1 except in pack_id. Compared with bytes-s3-p1, bytes-s3-p2 has a different plan_tree_ref, its own member directories (bytes-s3-p2-reference-start/-midpoint/-end, bound-collection), a different collection_plan.json and extraction_spec.json, and reversed module order. Its registration.json is status 'draft' with estimator versions null.
(2) The CI test named as covering this checks only plan-tree sidecar authentication, the s1-p1 defect class. It does not run a p2 tree's stage walk, its harvest, its export or its withheld-store path.
(3) The BYTES registration itself makes the per-sub-pack smoke a prerequisite: '§19 ... then, for each sub-pack's first session, the smoke by fingerprint (block-6 design §13.1; R8 item 8)' (bytes reg:450). The auditor's 'no smoke rule found in bytes_pack_v1.md' is wrong. The p2 draft notes also say 'Cold gate and smoke fingerprints remain before first t0'.
Dropping pack_id from the key is therefore a registration deviation that needs a dated, blind BYTES addendum, not a process rule change.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode:
A defect specific to a p2 tree first meets the real machine in the claim session. Examples: the reversed-order midpoint placement for single-model sub-packs s5 and s6, or a p2 member-directory or extraction_spec error. With s1-p1 and s6-p1 retries and six p2 sessions due before 11-02, that session is lost and may not be repeatable.
Worse, a referee who reads §19 finds a registered pre-collection step skipped without an addendum. That damages the credibility of the whole pass-2 dataset.
It is acceptable only after a dated BYTES amendment made blind, together with a CI or desk dry-walk of every p2 plan tree through compose, chain.stage_plan and a synthetic harvest and export.

judgments.reason:
Early stop on zero yield is good science in principle. The session is excluded anyway, and s1-p1 wasted 265 min. But the stated path does not exist. The loop's STOP file and remote ref only gate arming (loop.py:457-469), and I found no channel from the loop into a running chain or driver (grep of chain.py, driver.py and driver_lane.py for a STOP or stop file found none). So 'the loop writes STOP for the chain' means either an external kill of the driver process tree or a change to the driver or chain, which are number-bearing. An external kill takes the 'lost' path: desk_lane._advance aborts the bracket with records.terminal_record_absent (desk_lane.py:34-46), and the harvest runs with --allow-missing-terminal.

An external SIGKILL during a calibration capture or ledger write can leave the calibration ledger or pin in a state the next session's reservation and b_op provenance depend on (records.pin_ledger). A heuristic that misfires on physics refusals (all members waiting out admission, or thermal) would also end a session that would have counted.
Safe form: implement the stop through a reviewed, cooperative stop between stages, restricted to rc=1 refusals that are byte-identical. That needs an executing review of the driver or chain change, or limit the loop to an immediate alert to Ed.

judgments.reason:
Four premises fail on reading.
(1) 'Pure function of the bytes; a deadline firing is a re-run, not a loss.' Not so. The harvest re-reduces every run through reduce_bundle with an instrument-calibration physics cache (harvest.py:2266-2289). A wall-deadline firing returns registered INVALID evidence (DETECTION_NONCONVERGENT), not a program fault (powermetrics_fiducial.py:84-94, 995-1011), and the code marks it non-reproducible (powermetrics_fiducial.py:1528-1541). A re-reduction that differs from the stored one emits member.reduction_mismatch, which is EXCLUDE_MEMBER in the b6 catalog (harvest.py:4094-4099). So a slower or throttled host produces recorded exclusions that look like a legitimate verdict, and nothing triggers a re-run. ED-RULING 6(c) kept the deadline precisely because the replay 'runs on the quiet Mac, where the same calibration completed at harvest'. The plan breaks that assumption, and makes it worse by co-locating analysis, recompute and agents on a passively cooled Air.
(2) '--pack-records-root is write-only per session' (open question 2). Wrong. It holds the shared 'bytes' group blinding keys and the withheld store. _stored_or_draw draws a new key when none is present (blinding.py:88-133). The registration fixes the path to the Mac's /Users/edr/night-b6/loop-bytes/packs/bytes/... (bytes reg §11:342, 346).
(3) Holding blinding keys on the machine that hosts every agent widens access to the hidden offsets during blinded analysis (INFERRED; there is no per-user separation).
(4) The async verdict defeats loop protections:
- harvest_fault currently forces a smoke before the next arm (loop.py:317-320, 586-589).
- structure_defect holds the loop before the next session (loop.py:579-584).
- block-6 §4 requires 'a structural defect is fixed before the next session of any pack'.
With the harvest pending, session N+1 is already running when N's defect appears.

judgments.concrete_failure_mode:
A defect visible only in acceptance arrives while session N+1 of another pack is already running on the same code. Examples: a whole stage absent while later stages ran, or a pack-tree problem that surfaces in export. A second 6 h session is lost, and the 'same cause twice → consult' rule then fires one session late.
Required: the preflight counts succeeded member statuses per roster stage, and the next arm waits for the Air's full structure verdict. Only the energy-side work (acceptance numbers, export) may overlap the next chain.

(1) The attempt line and the outcomes from queue.outcome (loop.py:556-566) feed rotate, the 5-attempt pause and the 'same cause twice' consult. A pending line has no outcome.
(2) _precision runs on the counting ids at the desk (loop.py:595).
(3) state['harvest_fault'] forces a smoke before the next arm (loop.py:317-320, 586-589).
All three fire late or not at all while the harvest is pending. The auditor covers only same-pack retry deferral.

judgments.reason: Today compression runs only after harvest_rc == 0 with an ACCEPT or EXCLUDE verdict. It uses the harvest archive and structure.json as its 'after' anchor (desk_lane.py:242-247), so the evidence is compressed only once the archive has inventoried and digested it. The proposal compresses the Mac's copy after the transfer but before any harvest. That precondition then rests on an unverified claim: that the custody journal holds per-file SHA-256 for every raw sampler file. If the Air copy is lost or corrupted, the re-harvest must restore from the Mac copy, and reharvest restores from the '.desk' record dir (desk_lane.py:263-273).
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: The transfer verifies against custody hashes that do not cover some file, for example a sampler raw file not listed in custody. The Mac compresses or evicts its copy, the Air copy turns out to be bad, and the re-harvest has no verified source. A session is lost to process, which the registration says must never happen ('harvest problems are not session losses').

It either trips the census and excludes units, or adds unflagged network and wake load below the admission threshold.

The 180 s contention dwell, the instrument check and the census are repeated each time (precheck.py:556-615). Once C5's arm notice is sent during the previous desk, the first PRECHECK only needs the fingerprint and a census to decide the smoke. The physics that protect t0 are the ARM_WAIT ones. Merge them into one full pre-check at ARM_WAIT and save about 5 min per session. Adding the Codex daemon to the reap step is fine (precheck.py is not number-bearing). judgments.reason: It costs about 2 min and runs before the contention dwell, so its CPU use does not contaminate the readings (bytes:joulewise/b6/precheck.py:523-553 runs before the dwell at 595). Its inputs (the plan and the real ledger's last 24 captures) cannot have changed then, so skip the ARM_WAIT re-run when no smoke ran. judgments.reason: The proposal does not go far enough and misidentifies the main trigger. The fingerprint includes code_commit = `git rev-parse HEAD` of the measurement checkout (bytes:joulewise/b6/fingerprint.py:40). The loop compares the whole fingerprint dict with each pack's last_smoke_fingerprint (loop.py:318-319). Every session desk makes a pin-only git commit of configs/calibration/calibration_ledger_head.json in that checkout (bytes:joulewise/b5/plan.py:677-693, called from desk_lane.py:141-144). The driver lane also notes that a smoke may advance that pin (driver_lane.py:200-201). So HEAD changes after every session, and every session smokes whatever its pack_id. judgments.reason: Agreed, and it can go further. The STOP file and the remote ref are checked only at PRECHECK and ARM_WAIT (loop.py:301-330, 487-510). Once a chain starts, stopping it is manual (RUN_STATE 64). So the NO window is the only veto that does not waste a chain, and it should stay. It need not sit on the critical path, though. Send the next arm notice with a scheduled t0 when session N reaches its desk, or even at session N's t0 with a predicted next t0. Also install the driver during the window: today t0 is set to now + 420 s only after ARM_WAIT passes (driver_lane.py:196-199). One addition: the magistrate should not poll the Mac over ssh during SESSION_RUN. An sshd session and its shell add CPU and network activity during measured runs. Idle admission would catch it, but at a cost in minutes. Have the Mac push state (the mailer already does) rather than the Air pulling it during the chain.

Note that _advance ends in a git pin commit (desk_lane.py:141-144; plan.py:692-693), and that commit is the true trigger of the per-session smoke (see C4). The C4 fix must exclude this file from the fingerprint.

judgments.reason:
The direction is right, but four prerequisites are missing.
(1) Blinding custody. BYTES's single group key and its session bindings live at <pack_records_root>/bytes/blinding. The registration names that concrete Mac path, /Users/edr/night-b6/loop-bytes/packs/bytes/blinding, and the withheld store beside it (bytes reg:342, 346). _stored_or_draw silently draws a NEW factor when the key file and its blinding-sessions bindings are absent (bytes:joulewise/b6/blinding.py:25-36, 88-118). An Air harvest pointed at an empty records root would blind p2 with a different factor than p1. So migrate the key, the blinding-sessions sidecars and the withheld p1 rows once, keep a single custody, add a refuse-if-absent guard, and record the path change as a dated note.
(2) Agents and keys on the same machine. The auditor puts every agent on the Air beside the unblinding keys, which is a blinding regression compared with the Mac today, where no agent runs. Run the harvest and keep the keys under a separate macOS user on the Air (0700) that agents cannot read.
(3) Loop mechanics. _append_attempt is idempotent per session id (loop.py:540-544), so appending a 'harvest_pending' line first would discard the real verdict later. harvest_rc not in (0,6) sets harvest_fault, which forces a smoke (loop.py:318, 593-596). The reharvested command refuses while collection.active exists and re-runs the harvest locally (loop.py:646-663). Use the existing pending_sessions and `reharvested` correction path (queue.py:33-37), with a new non-fault pending code and a command that ingests an externally computed line.
(4) Transfer and disk. desk_compress.compress refuses without the archive's harvest.json (desk_compress.py:253-259), so Mac-side compression needs a new pre-harvest path. Compress then transfer over Wi-Fi or Ethernet; about 70x makes this quick. Do not use a Thunderbolt or USB-C bridge during collection: a peer that draws power over USB-C would load the measured DC input (INFERRED).
The projected 10-12 h saving also assumes it lands now. With ED-RULING 6a putting the block-5 dry run on the Mac first, and the build plus executing review taking an estimated 1-2 days, it likely covers only 4-5 of the 8 sessions (INFERRED).
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: The first Air harvest of a p2 session draws a fresh pack factor (no key or binding present). Its export is then blinded inconsistently with p1, and at release stored_factor divides by one key. Alternatively, an agent session on the Air reads the key directory and the blinding is broken.

Corrections already live in state['reharvested'] (queue.py:33-37). Implement the Air verdict as a correction, not a second append.

Mac-side compression must therefore happen in the same desk, before the next PRECHECK, and today's compress() refuses before a harvest exists (desk_compress.py:253-259). That needs a new, non-number-bearing compress-after-verified-transfer path.

missed_items: The per-session smoke has a different root cause than the auditor names. desk_lane._advance makes a pin-only git commit in the measurement checkout every session (bytes:joulewise/b5/plan.py:676-696). code_commit = HEAD is in the fingerprint (bytes:joulewise/b6/fingerprint.py:40), so every session smokes whatever its pack_id. Block 6's repeat-pack sessions still show 'smoke about 50 min' (c634f6f3:41). INFERRED; confirm from smoke-passes.jsonl.

Blinding key custody is a hard prerequisite for any off-Mac harvest. The registration names the BYTES group key path and withheld store as Mac paths (bytes reg:342, 346), and blinding._stored_or_draw draws a new factor silently when keys are absent (blinding.py:88-118). Migrate keys, session bindings and p1 withheld rows once, add a refuse-if-absent guard, and record a dated custody note.

Co-locating all agents with the unblinding keys on the Air weakens blinding compared with today. Use a separate macOS user for the harvest and keys, or keep the export step on a machine no agent runs on.

The biggest missed parallelism, outside this segment: ED-RULING 6a pauses BYTES so the block-5 blind dry run can use the Mac. The dry run reads immutable archives and measures nothing. Running it on the Air (same macOS arm64; a deadline firing is a tooling refusal and a rerun, ED-RULING item 6) would let BYTES keep collecting on the Mac in parallel. This conflicts with ED-RULING item 6's 'the dry run runs on the quiet Mac', so it needs Ed. Feasibility depends on Air disk for about 3 x 43 GiB uncompressed (cadence plan §3).

Sequencing against the 2026-11-02 end (bytes reg:105). Land the cheap loop-only changes first (C15 early stop, C1 tick drain, C4 fingerprint fix excluding the pin file, C5 notice overlap) in one batched landing. The Air harvest (C19) needs the most build and review time and pays off on fewer remaining sessions than projected.

The launch lead can overlap the NO window. t0 is set to now + 420 s only after ARM_WAIT clears (bytes:joulewise/b6/driver_lane.py:196-199). Fixing t0 at notice + 1800 and installing inside the window saves about 7 min per session.

Transfer link hazard: a Thunderbolt or USB-C bridge between the Air and the measurement Mac can carry USB-PD power and add USB devices, contaminating DC-input and rest numbers or the meter_device fingerprint (INFERRED). Compress on the Mac, then transfer over the network, or unplug before t0.

The magistrate and any transfer on the Air must avoid running ssh commands with 'claude' or 'codex' substrings on the Mac. The census is pgrep -lf over full command lines (bytes:joulewise/hazards/arm.py:69), and scratchpad paths contain 'claude-501'.

Corrected projection: inherited-caution item 6 and C9's ~15 min saving do not exist. BYTES already stops the corpus at 12 valid runs (compose.py:115-117; pack registration corpus.stop_after_valid 12). The projected cycle of chain + 60-70 min should be recomputed without it.
Measure before building: read state.json `since` stamps and smoke-passes.jsonl on the Mac. That turns C1's tick latency and C4's smoke trigger from INFERRED to measured in minutes, with no code.

map.segment: Block-5 analysis: plan steps 1-12, dry run, release
map.summary:
Block-5 numbers are slow for three reasons. None of them is that the science needs it.

(1) Steps 1 and 2 of the dry run repeat the same work hundreds of times, one bundle at a time. They are plain serial loops over about 350 kept bundles (dry_run.py:678, :688). Every strict validation refits the same calibration from scratch: 82 identical refits took 594 s of the first 941 s of the joined run, about 8-10 s each on cloud (L9-2.md:20, :139-140). The harvest already did this exact per-bundle work in a process pool with a per-worker physics cache (harvest.py:2418, :2437-2496, :2549-2552). It also checked that each re-reduction is identical to the stored one (harvest.py:4263-4266). Step 2's outputs are read by no later step. The driver's own comment says so: "Re-reduction probes are commitments for the cold gate; later steps never consume them" (dry_run.py:475-479).

(2) The gates after the numbers exist are serial, and two of them repeat each other:
- the cold Fable and Opus passes on L9 before the release (ED-RULING.md:48-49);
- a full second run in release mode (plan §3.2 item 2, :194-195; dry_run.py:1154-1218);
- step 12, where a judge and a refuter re-derive every printed number (plan :172). The independent recompute re-derives the same numbers from raw records with code that shares nothing with L9 (RUN_STATE item 37, line 64). On evidence: the record says no cold judge ever produced a catch that changed a number, and only executing seats did (pruning_list:381, :524). The L9-ruling cold passes ended ACCEPT WITH CHANGES with no refusal (RUN_STATE:184).

(3) The real data live only on the measurement Mac. Analysis there competes with BYTES collection (ED-RULING item 6a, :70-74), and an agent left on that Mac already lost s6-p1 (RUN_STATE item 78).

Measured costs:
- Full-size synthetic test_dry_run: 20,950-24,782 s (jwdata REPORT module table).
- Steps 0-9 in trace 7: 5 h 28 min (06:31 to 11:59).
- Step 9b: ran 17 min before the 120 s deadline fired (REPORT:284).
- J6: 47,231 s (L9-1.md RESULTS TABLE).

None of this is needed to protect the science. What protects it, and what to keep:
- blinding and structure-only output (the record validator and step_record, steps.py:74-91);
- exclusions applied from the sealed catalog (step 3, plan §2.2);
- the independent recompute;
- one determinism check;
- provenance pins (step 0, windows.py:190; registration §11 item 4).

Changes ranked by payoff:
- (a) A shared physics_cache (already ruled) plus a process pool for steps 1-2. Also ALPHA and BETA run side by side in steps 4 and 10. No authority needed; L9 code only.
- (b) Build the missing piece now, blind, in the cloud: the recompute-vs-L9 comparator. git ls-files on all four checkouts shows no tracked comparator (INFERRED absent). Run the recompute at the same time as the L9 dry run, on a second machine. The recompute is standard-library only and has no wall deadline (independent_recompute_b5.py:1-16), so host speed cannot affect it.
- (c) Script 12 of the 13 post-seal FILLs, the S11 index (configs/analysis/b5/analysed_windows.json, still absent on the L9-2 lane), the L9 pin addendum and the release-event draft. They are paths, SHA-256s and commits. Only DISCLOSURE-SITES needs a ruling.
- (d) Let the lead read the dry run's restricted outputs as soon as the release event is recorded, while release mode re-runs. Registration custody map :4900-4901 already lets the lead read them then.
- (e) A blind, dated amendment to the analysis plan, with a lead line and one executing refuter: step 12 becomes one reviewer reading the comparator table. Step 2 becomes a digest comparison with the harvest's withheld re-reduction.
- (f) Ed rules on moving the real-data dry run (or at least the recompute) to the MacBook Air, so BYTES is not held.

Two critiques of today's papers:
- ED-RULING item 4 ("release equality is tested on a reduced fixture") cannot be done as written. L9-2 showed reduced fixtures trip kept_units.py:163 (L9-2.md:131-138). The existing fast tests already cover release equality: ReleaseComparisonPrimitiveTests and ReleaseAcceptanceTests (test_release_equality.py:45-133).
- The "63 % of wall time" figure was measured on the first 941 s only. Its extension to the whole 6 h run is unverified.

A new risk (INFERRED): the dry run censuses the live calibration ledger at the block-5 measurement checkout (dry_run.py:555-558). Release mode re-hashes it (dry_run.py:1104-1105). If anything appends to that ledger between the dry run and the release, the release refuses with release_digest_differs_from_dry_run.

L9 blind dry run (machine A) at the same time as the independent recompute (machine B: Mac and Air, either way round). Comparator after both (independent_recompute_b5.py:2591-2603; RUN_STATE:282).

map.where_to_run:
Cloud (Claude 4 vCPU/15 GB; Codex Cloud 5 vCPU/17 GB): all code (cache, pool, comparator, index generator, FILL and addendum scripts, the 9b fault-injection test), the six short modules (about 14 min), the executing review, the one cold pass and CI. The one cached full-size test_dry_run can also run in the cloud, but use a workspace-backed TMPDIR: /tmp is an 8.8 GiB tmpfs that ran out of space (L9-1). Never real data in the cloud: about 43 GiB per session exceeds the ~30 GB disk, and only automation may read restricted paths.

MacBook Air (24 GB, macOS, Codex CLI): (1) Best use: receive the compressed block-5 archives at a desk window, verify SHA-256s, and run the independent recompute. It has no wall deadline, so host speed is harmless. This frees the Mac. (2) With an Ed ruling amending ED-RULING item 6, run the L9 blind dry run and the release mode on the Air under the same absolute paths. BYTES then keeps collecting through 2026-11-02, and no agent touches the measurement Mac. (3) Fallback host for the full-size synthetic run if cloud executors drop again (L9-1 outage of 10-23), with macOS parity (zsh, Homebrew python). Caveats (INFERRED): it is fanless and may throttle on multi-hour pool runs. Free disk for about 130-260 GiB decompressed is unknown. The Python/numpy lock must match the Mac for byte-identical digests. Run the pipeline as a detached script, never with an agent reading restricted folders.

Measurement Mac: measurement only. Exceptions: the desk-time compression and transfer, and, if Ed keeps item 6 as written, the first blind dry run with BYTES held.
map.amendment_rules:
Governing text, quoted:

- Registration §0.1 (registration_block5.md:564-567): "Cold gate. An independent ruling on a named question by a judge seat with no prior involvement, checked by a refuter seat whose job is to show the ruling wrong. A challenge that survives goes back to the judge once; a disagreement settles in one erratum, not a chain. A cold erratum is a change to a sealed document made this way; it is prospective when it is made before the bytes it governs exist."
- Registration §0.1 (:568-569): "R3. The standing route for a tooling fault: fix it in a reviewed pull request, merge, then re-run the failed desk step ... on identical bytes. R3 never re-collects anything."
- Registration §10 (:5144-5145): "None to §§3–9 for an armed or completed attempt. A rule, threshold, catalog effect, roster or blinding change is a prospective cold erratum (one judge, one refuter), settled in one erratum." And (:5157-5158): "A review finding that concerns only how something is recorded (receipts, naming, schema formality) is dispositioned 'flag, not refuse' and never sent to a fix round."
- Registration §11 item 4 (:5519-5521): "the analysis code (L9) before the release event ... Each addendum names the files and their SHA-256s and the desk checkout's commit, and is written by a seat that has read no claim-window energy."
- Registration §12 (:5680-5687): "After the seal commit this file's bytes do not change ... The analysis plan is read by no program. If a value is filled into it after the seal commit, its SHA-256 changes, and an addendum to the seal record states the new digest."
- Plan §13 (analysis_plan_block5.md:779-783): "a value that becomes known after the seal goes into an addendum to the seal record (registration §12), not into this file. If this file is nevertheless changed to carry one, the same addendum restates this file's SHA-256."
- Plan §3.2 item 3 (:196-199), for repairs after the release: written and reviewed by seats that have read no released number, plus a synthetic fixture reproducing the failure, with every other fixture's output byte-identical; otherwise a cold gate and the outputs labelled post-unblinding.

Later process rule: orchestrator decisions of 2026-10-14 (pruning_list_2026-10-14.md:540-541). Item 2: the release happens when the blind dry run passes and the independent recompute agrees within a tolerance fixed before release, with no separate cold gate. Item 3: cold judges per rule change are replaced by one executing refuter plus a recorded orchestrator line. ED-RULING.md:9-13: amends nothing registered or sealed.

Application to this segment:
- Speed changes inside L9 code (cache, pools, resume) need no authority, provided outputs and digests are byte-identical, which a test shows.
- Changing sealed plan text (step order 6∥9 or 10-after-4, replacing step 2, lightening step 12, moving determinism before the release) is a HOW change. It needs a blind, dated amendment: a lead line plus one executing refuter under 7a item 3, recorded as a seal-record addendum restating the plan's SHA-256, made before the release event.
- Changing what is computed or excluded needs a prospective cold erratum and is not proposed here.
- Moving real-data runs off the Mac, and cutting to one cold pass, change Ed's own binding text (ED-RULING items 3, 6, 6a; RUN_STATE item 77), so they need Ed.
- The 9b deadline fix is a governed estimator-source change with a calibration-acceptance reissue (ED-RULING :60-62).
open_questions: MacBook Air hardware: chip, free disk (does it hold ~130-260 GiB decompressed, or does the analysis need .zst streaming?), and whether the Python/numpy lock can match the measurement Mac so release digests are byte-identical. Not verified.

Does anything still append to the block-5 measurement checkout's runs/calibration_observation_ledger.jsonl? The dry run censuses its live SHA (dry_run.py:555-558) and release mode re-hashes it (:1104-1105). INFERRED risk of a forced release_digest_differs_from_dry_run.

Is there a release cold gate or not? 7a item 2 (pruning_list:540) says none. The scout (:96) says to assemble a 'cold release packet' per the 'user's cold-gate requirement'. Which is the binding text?

Coverage: does the independent recompute compute every plan §9 printed field (floors, 8 R and 4 R_cm, contrast decision intervals, Holm, reported-cell intervals, attribution floors, §7.3 ratios)? No comparator is tracked in any checkout (INFERRED absent).

ED-RULING item 6 condition: L9-2 has not yet confirmed that a deadline firing fails closed at every site. In particular, can an analysis-time firing make the shared strict-invalid predicate drop a NEG-8 reference the harvest kept, and so change an allowance? The answer decides whether option (c) is safe on any host.
Is the '63 % of wall time in refits' figure, measured on the first 941 s (L9-2.md:139-140), representative of the whole 6 h run? The cache's real saving is unmeasured.
DISCLOSURE-SITES depends on the still-open placement question (registration §14 Q4). Should the lead decide it before the release, as recommended, so placement cannot follow the numbers?
The seal record says 'eleven open markers' (SEAL_RECORD.md:300) while plan §13 lists 13 FILLs. Which two are not counted?
Would the dry run on the Air need the measurement checkout itself (AnalysedWindow.measurement_root, windows.py:131; dry_run.py:555), or only a clone at the same commit plus a ledger snapshot?

science.segment: Block-5 analysis: plan steps 1-12, dry run, release
science.lens: SCIENCE-PROTECTION SKEPTIC: for each LIGHTEN/MERGE/AUTOMATE/PARALLELIZE/MOVE_EARLIER/CUT, look for a realistic path to a wrong, unsupported or non-reproducible printed number, or to a reviewer rightly rejecting the paper; check that the check named as making a step redundant really covers the same failure.

judgments.reason: The cache is keyed by the calibration evidence SHA-256. It is read only after the reducer's own manifest, evidence, plist and events hash checks (cli.py:462-468). The per-bundle staleness checks still run before the cache lookup (reduce.py:1514-1523). Only successes are stored, as max(declared, fresh) b_fiducial, which depends only on the artifact (reduce.py:1526-1594). A cache hit therefore returns what a refit of the same bytes would return. A hit also cannot fire the 120 s deadline, so the cache makes the outcome less host-dependent. Threading the cache into the 9b archive replay touches whole_window.py:407-412 (strict_validate_bundles with workers=1 and no cache). That file is on ED-RULING's non-governed list, so no governed edit is needed. I could not construct a wrong-number path, provided the byte-identity test exists.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: Residual risk, not a wrong number: the 'cached vs uncached byte-identical' test can be inconclusive on a cloud VM, because the uncached arm may itself hit the 120 s deadline (this is what happened in L9-1/L9-2). The INFERRED claim that the cache saves most of 9b's 17 min is unverified. The 9b firing was on a NEG-8 reference (neg8-window-end-r1), which may carry a different calibration artifact from the 82 identical bracket refits (L9-2.md:13-16, :139-140).

judgments.reason: The fast tests named as the release-equality gate run on dispatch doubles: the module docstring reads 'Commitment comparison on dispatch doubles and the joined real programs' (test_release_equality.py:1). R1-R5 check the comparison logic, not whether the real programs give byte-identical outputs in two custody roots. Only JoinedReleaseTests J6 checks that (test_release_equality.py:21-30). J6 has never passed past 9b. In L9-1 the full drivers only reached step 10/11, with no completion record (L9-1.md:5,18,467). So cross-custody-root determinism of steps 10-11 has never been executed. The same map also adds new sources of nondeterminism: pools, concurrent packs, and reordered record assembly.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: Suppose step 10 or 11 writes a custody-root-dependent byte (an absolute path or a root-specific name inside a projection or disclosure). Or suppose the new pool assembles a record in a different order. The blind dry run then completes cleanly, and the release-mode run, in a different custody root, refuses with release_digest_differs_from_dry_run (dry_run.py:1207-1217). That happens after the release event, so the cure is a post-unblinding repair under plan §3.2 item 3 (restricted seats, new fixture, or a cold gate and the 'produced after unblinding' label).

judgments.reason: Fault injection is better than waiting for a natural firing. As specified, though, it can pass without testing anything. (1) A global budget of 0 fires at the first refit in step 1, and the run stops with kept_bundle_strict_validation_failed (dry_run.py:676-682). Steps 4, 9, 9b and 10 are never reached. (2) Once P2's shared cache is on, later steps get cache hits and never refit, so injecting the fault there fires nothing. NEG-8 corpus references are not among the kept bundles validated in step 1, so their refits happen first in steps 4/9/9b. (3) The deadline is a default argument bound when the function is defined (powermetrics_fiducial.py:497,918), so patching the constant does nothing; the seam has to patch the clock or the function, or edit a governed file. One site I read fails closed: the archive replay refuses an unlisted strict-invalid reference (whole_window.py:458). The predicate's signature, however, allows unlisted_strict_invalid='read' (whole_window.py:5412, :5606), so every caller has to be listed and checked.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: The injection test passes because the run stops at step 1 or every later refit is a cache hit. Ed's condition is then recorded as met. On the real dry run, a natural firing in a NEG-8 reference replay on a path that uses 'read', or that drops strict-invalid references, removes a survivor. The drift allowance changes and every floor and contrast D changes with it.

judgments.reason: The record does support lightening: there is no cold-judge W catch, and the L9 judges missed defects that were later found by running code (pruning_list:377, OP-3). Two parts of the claim do not hold. First, the 'redundant with recompute + comparator' half rests on a comparator that does not exist. Second, the recompute cannot see L9-only behaviour: blinding and redaction, the disclosure producer, and the fill input. The proposal also leaves open which model does the single pass. Most build and review seats are Sol, so one Sol pass shares the builder's blind spots. The change also overrides the latest binding text: ED-RULING item 3 says 'The release still needs them' (2026-10-27), which is later than 7a item 2.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: A redaction or disclosure-producer defect lets a RESTRICTED code, or a value derived from one, into the step-11 disclosures (plan §8). Or the fill adapter puts an issued value under the wrong label. The comparator compares quantities, not labels or redaction. A single executing pass from the builder's model family misses it the same way the build did, and the paper prints a disclosure or label that is wrong but numerically 'agreeing'.

judgments.reason: Selection is not taken from the index. select_analysed_attempts recomputes first_claim_usable from the archive-opened attempt records. It refuses window_index_disagrees_with_archive when a record differs from its entry, and block_incomplete when no attempt is claim-usable (windows.py:283-299). Pins are checked against governing_pin (windows.py:189-190). History must be contiguous from attempt 1 (windows.py:237-243). no_archive entries need a citation (windows.py:196-200). A generator error therefore refuses; it does not re-select. I could not construct a wrong-number path.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: Residual: the generator could pick one of several archive copies or backups, or produce a weak record_citation for a no_archive attempt. Both are provenance-quality issues that the loader partly catches (harvest_record_sha256 binding). One lead diff of the generated attempt history against the RUN_STATE attempt record closes the gap. The index must be committed before the dry run, because its SHA binds the release (dry_run.py:1173-1174).

judgments.reason: Scripting the paths and SHA-256s is fine. The redundancy claim is too weak, though: 'git tag + dry-run analysis_commit already bind code identity' shows what ran, not that what ran was the reviewed code. The proposal lets FILLs come 'from the L9 tag or from the dry-run record'. Filling from the dry-run record would pin whatever commit the dry run happened to use. Registration §11 item 4 exists to pin the reviewed analysis code before the release event. The seal record's 'eleven open markers' against plan §13's thirteen also has to be reconciled by a person; a script will not settle it.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: The blind dry run is launched from a commit one fix past the reviewed tag (for example an R3 cure that was never reviewed). The script fills the addendum from the record's analysis_commit, and the release-mode run matches it. The published provenance then claims that reviewed code produced the numbers when it did not.

judgments.reason: The registered check stays. Any strict failure stops step 1 with kept_bundle_strict_validation_failed (dry_run.py:678-681), which is a tooling refusal, not a number. Assembling results in registered order and requiring serial and parallel digests to be equal keeps the record identical. I found no path to a wrong number. The only exposure is cost: under ruling (c), CPU contention is the suspected cause of the deadline firings (L9-2.md:129-130). A pool can cause step-1 refusals and reruns on a slow host.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: Cost only. On the fanless Air, or with one worker per logical core, concurrent first refits in every worker each slow down several-fold, and one fires the deadline. Step 1 then refuses, and the whole dry run is cured and restarted in a fresh custody root. Cap the workers at the harvest's count on the Mac and record load.

judgments.reason: I agree that step 2 feeds no estimator: register() gives rereduced_ outputs fixed names, and rehash() excludes them (dry_run.py:439-441, 474-479). The redundancy argument should be corrected, though. Steps 4, 9 and 10 re-reduce under the window bound b, which is a different computation. The real overlap is with step 1: strict validation already requires summary_metrics.json to equal a fresh re-reduction at the analysis commit (cli.py:455-460). Two couplings remain. The code comment calls these probes 'commitments for the cold gate' (dry_run.py:475), so cutting step 2 only makes sense together with R5. And step 2's outputs are among the digests the release compares, so cutting it removes about 350 determinism commitments, though step 1 already covers them against stored values.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: No wrong-number path. The failure is procedural: step 2 is dropped while step 12 keeps its registered form. The cold gate then loses the per-member commitments the driver produced for it and has to re-derive member energies without an analysis-commit anchor.

judgments.reason: Step 4 gives the floor extractor the harvest archive so it can recompute the NEG-8 allowance (plan :164, :744 (b)). That path replays NEG-8 references through the shared strict-invalid predicate, which refits calibrations under the 120 s deadline. Running ALPHA and BETA together raises CPU contention, the suspected cause of the firings (L9-2.md:129-130), while P5 still has not confirmed that every replay site fails closed. The saving is unmeasured (step 4's cost is unknown). The ordering semantics also change: BETA's outputs exist in custody even when ALPHA refuses.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: Concurrent ALPHA and BETA extraction slows a NEG-8 reference refit past 120 s. If any extraction-path caller treats a strict-invalid reference as lost rather than refusing (signature allows 'read', whole_window.py:5412), the reference drops from the survivor set. The drift allowance and floor change, a floor prints wrong, and the release run, without contention, differs, which is caught only if R4 is kept in its registered place.

judgments.reason: The auditor says the saving is 'minutes; low priority', yet the change needs an amendment to the sealed plan (plan §3.1 order) and introduces concurrency into a shared RunState. Every invoke runs rehash() and register(), which renames files and mutates s.outputs (dry_run.py:424-451, 480-494). Step 9 runs analyze-claims with --neg8-harvest-archive, which replays NEG-8 references and so refits under the deadline. Running it beside step 6 adds contention for a few minutes' gain.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: A race on s.outputs or on file renames during concurrent register() leaves an output out of the record, or produces digests whose order differs between dry run and release. The release then refuses with release_digest_differs_from_dry_run after the release event. A contention-induced firing in step 9's NEG-8 replay brings the S4 failure mode with it.

judgments.reason: Step 10 has never completed in a full-size run (L9-1.md:5, 18, 467). Its custody reopen, open_paper_input with a projection replay-equality check (dry_run.py:900-918), has not been characterised for refits or deadline exposure. Making it concurrent, or starting it right after step 4, adds untested ordering to a step that has never run end to end. The plan's rule that 'a refusal stops the steps after it' would also need an amendment for the reorder.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: ALPHA and BETA issuance run concurrently, and both reopens replay their evidence on one host. One replay is slowed past the deadline in the dry run but not in the release. The result is a tooling refusal and a rerun. Or, if a reopen-path predicate drops rather than refuses, it produces a projection mismatch that surfaces only as a post-release digest difference.

judgments.reason: The registered B5-BLIND-DRY-RUN-RECORD remains one complete, clean run from step 0 (plan §3.2 item 1). The release compares against that record only. Resuming during fix rounds cannot put a reused output into the registered record. An incomplete program-closure hash could hide a defect during a fix round, but the final full run exposes it. I found no path to a wrong number.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: Residual cost: the closure key misses an indirect dependency, so fix rounds 'pass' on stale upstream outputs, and the final full run refuses and costs one more round. The garden-of-forking-paths concern (iterating tooling fixes until an outcome-class status changes) is the same with or without resume.

judgments.reason: Ed's ruling (c) rests on the stated basis 'The dry run runs on the quiet Mac, where the same calibration completed at harvest' (ED-RULING:63). L9-2's reason why (c) is safe likewise depends on host behaviour (L9-2.md:174-177). The project's own cadence plan says real-data analysis off the Mac 'should wait for item 2.4 [governed deadline fix], or use a fast dedicated machine' and recommends the first dry run on the Mac (analysis_cadence_plan.md:47-48, 57, 60-61). A fanless 24 GB Air is not such a machine, and its disk is unknown against ~130-260 GiB decompressed. The census also hashes measurement_root's live ledger (dry_run.py:554-558), which on the Air would be a hand-made snapshot, so the 'archived ledger copies are prefixes of the live ledger' provenance check would compare against a copy.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: On the Air, sustained load throttles the CPU, and a NEG-8 reference refit takes more than 120 s. The best case is repeated tooling-refusal rounds; with P5 unconfirmed, a silently dropped survivor changes the allowance. Separately, the reviewer-facing record now says the registered analysis ran on a different host from the one the governing ruling names, with a substituted ledger. That can be defended only with a dated ruling made before the run.

judgments.reason: The recompute is standard-library only, with no wall deadline (independent_recompute_b5.py:1-32). It reads archives and roots given as arguments, so the host cannot change its result, and running it beside the dry run keeps it independent. The redundancy statement needs a correction for R5, though: it takes 'selection, anchors, timing bounds and calibration fits' as input judgments (:4-5). It reads b_fiducial_s from the capture evidence and recorded b_op from withheld/bracket-evaluation.json (:637-679), and the NEG-8 allowance from the harvest's derived/neg8-allowance.json (:697-699). It does not check those inputs independently.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: No wrong-number path from running it in parallel, provided the copy on the second machine is checked against the harvest's SHA256SUMS and no agent reads restricted folders there. The residual is a scope error: treating its agreement as verifying the allowance or calibration inputs, which it does not recompute.

judgments.reason: Building the comparator blind, now, with bars fixed by FIX-571 (independent_recompute_b5.py:8-16), adds protection that does not exist today. 7a item 2 already makes agreement the release condition (pruning_list:540). The coverage map in the proposal is the essential safeguard. One residual failure needs an explicit rule: a field that is missing or null in either source counts as disagree, not as skipped.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: Residual: the comparator is built against synthetic outputs, where every field is populated. On real data the recompute serializes a non-finite value as null (sanitize, :2580-2588) or L9 emits a refusal for a p42 cell. If 'null on one side' is treated as not comparable, the table shows agreement over fewer quantities than plan §9 prints. Release counts must therefore equal the coverage map's counts.

judgments.reason: A script drafting the digest section is fine. The proposal also sets the release condition as 'dry run clean plus comparator agrees, with no separate cold gate', resolving toward 7a item 2 (2026-10-14). ED-RULING item 3 (2026-10-27, binding, later) says the cold Fable and Opus passes move to before the release event and 'The release still needs them'. RUN_STATE item 35 also once said 'release event through a cold gate'. The map cannot settle that conflict itself; Ed has to rule.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: The lead commits the release event on dry run plus comparator alone, as the proposal says. A later audit reads ED-RULING item 3 and finds the release went ahead in breach of the owner's binding ruling. The release event, the dated moment of unblinding, then becomes contestable, which damages the credibility of every number tied to it.

judgments.reason: The argument that ruling (c) is safe is explicitly that a host-dependent firing 'would surface as release_digest_differs_from_dry_run, not as a wrong number' (L9-2.md:174-177). That holds only if numbers are used after release equality is established. Plan §3.2 item 2 says a mismatch 'stops the analysis'. Letting the lead read dry-run outputs while release mode runs reverses that order. And cross-custody-root equality for steps 10-11 has never been executed (see P4). The safer speed-up is the auditor's own option: a second blind run in a different custody root before the release event, after which the post-release step is a hash-verified read.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: The lead reads the dry-run reported energies and contrasts at the release event. Hours later, release mode refuses at step 10 or 11 because of a custody-root-dependent byte or nondeterministic assembly from the new pool. The lead has now seen numbers from a run whose reproducibility failed. Every repair falls under §3.2 item 3, and the choice of which run's numbers stand is made with the outcome in view. A reviewer can rightly question whether the published numbers came from a reproducible computation.

judgments.reason: The 'fully redundant with R1/R2' claim fails in three ways. (1) The recompute shares inputs with L9 (calibration fits, b_op, anchors, timing bounds, harvest NEG-8 allowance: independent_recompute_b5.py:4-5, 637-699), so agreement cannot detect errors in them. (2) Step 12 checks every printed number against the artifacts. That includes the fill-to-text link (rounding, units, labels, placement), and L9 stops at a validated fill input with rendering left open (Q-RENDERER). The comparator does not cover that link. (3) Authority: the post-release reader 'the results cold gate that re-derives every printed number' is named in the registration's custody map (registration :4898-4900). Registration bytes cannot change after the seal (§12), and §10 makes a rule or blinding change a prospective cold erratum (one judge, one refuter). 7a item 3 changed doctrine, not registration §10. Before the release the cold erratum is cheap, so use it.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: A step-11 issued value is printed at the wrong precision, or the BETA-inclusive labelled line is placed under the registered heading. Both pass the comparator, because the quantities agree. A single reviewer who reads only the agreement table lets the wrong printed sentence through. Separately, a referee who checks registration §10 and the custody map against the published process finds the results gate removed by a lead line rather than the registered erratum route.

judgments.reason: The plan registers it as optional and 'never blocking', and it serializes structure only (plan :180-182). All three packs are collected, so the blind dry run covers the same programs on the full bytes. Not running it cannot change any number.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: None found.

missed_items: Every PARALLELIZE proposal (S1 pool, S4, S6_S9, S10, and the recompute on the same host) raises host CPU contention, which L9-2 names as the suspected cause of the 120 s deadline firings (L9-2.md:13-16, 129-130). Ed's ruling (c) leaves the deadline in place. The map does not cap worker counts or say where load is recorded. Recommendation: cap concurrency at the harvest's Mac worker count until the governed fix (cadence 2.4) lands, and keep step 4 and later serial.

The map's own fix list repeatedly assumes ruling (c) is safe. That safety argument (L9-2.md:174-177) depends on release digest equality being checked before any number is used, and proposal R4 removes exactly that ordering. The map does not note this conflict.

Release equality across two custody roots has never been executed past 9b at full size. L9-1's full drivers reached step 10/11 with no completion record (L9-1.md:5, 18, 467). The fast R1-R5 tests run on dispatch doubles (test_release_equality.py:1). Once the pool, cache and concurrency changes land, one determinism check of the real programs before release is needed: J6 once, or a second blind run in a fresh custody root.

The independent recompute is not independent of the calibration fits, b_op, anchors, timing bounds or the harvest's NEG-8 allowance. It reads them as inputs (independent_recompute_b5.py:4-5, 637-699). The only re-check of the NEG-8 survivor physics is L9's own replay with refit (9b, step 4, step 9). Any plan to hash-bind or cache those away (option (b), or P2's extension) leaves those inputs unchecked by anything outside the harvest.

Proposal P5's fault injection can pass without exercising anything. A global budget of 0 stops the run at step 1 (dry_run.py:676-682). With P2's cache on, later sites never refit. Release condition and amendment route conflict. ED-RULING item 3 (2026-10-27) requires the cold passes before release, while 7a item 2 (2026-10-14) says no separate cold gate.
