map.segment: Independent recompute: coverage and overlap (scripts/independent_recompute_b5.py on lane/2026-10-14-independent-recompute @ 9ca87bce, tests/independent_recompute/, S-13, RUN_STATE item 37)
map.summary:
WHAT IT IS. A 2,662-line Python script that uses only the standard library and imports no repository code (wt/recompute/scripts/independent_recompute_b5.py:1-17; the stdlib-only rule is tested at tests/independent_recompute/test_archives.py:122). It re-derives block 5's numbers from each member's raw/powermetrics.plist, events.jsonl and metadata.json. The first commit describes it as computing "the 97 headline quantities of block 5 (H1 reported cells, H2 floors, H3 dominance, H4 GAMMA contrasts, H5 descriptive magnitudes) and the four tier-2 disclosures" (commit ab14e02d). It now also computes: the per-phase whole-machine (meter) line, the PLAN 8.2 request cross-check, the b_sens sensitivity line, the scaled-allowance line (ALPHA, BETA and GAMMA, including GAMMA outcome words), the alternative-allowance line, the BETA a1/a4/a5-inclusive line and the single-step reconstruction diagnostic (script:1859, 1988-2060, 2165, 2219-2262, 2324, 1725; commits bd91198d and 76f45da3). It never refuses: problems are flags, and 13 codes stop the comparison (script:58-63).

TOLERANCES. The script compares its results only to values stored in the archive:
- Per-run phase energy and anchor envelope: 1e-6 relative, or 1e-6 J absolute near zero (script:80-88, 459-470).
- b_op: 1e-6 relative (script:672-679).
- NEG-8 allowance: same 1e-6 rule (script:787-789).
- plist against CSV: exact (script:429).
The release bar is S-13 (block6_replication_DRAFT.md:1154-1160 and :1206): 1 mJ per run phase energy, and half a unit of the last printed digit for every printed quantity, compared unrounded. On synthetic data, round 2 matched L9's eight operative floors to 8.8e-14 relative (commit 42774681; test_reconcile.py:266-296).

WHAT IT DOES NOT COVER. It treats these as inputs, not things it re-derives (header line 4):
- Exclusions. It reads derived/exclusions.json and derived/flags.jsonl (script:544-557). Pruning-list AN-18, which asked it to re-derive exclusions from the raw monitor records, was never built (pruning_list_2026-10-14.md:183, :328).
- The pulse-calibration fit. It reads each capture's b_fiducial_s and recomputes only the bracket arithmetic (script:637-689). So step 9b's refit has no independent check.
- Event timestamps and clock-anchor bounds.
- Strict bundle validation (step 1), custody, digests and determinism.
- The rendered results fills (step 11).
- p42 cells, which it marks expected_unresolvable (script:2406).
- Block 6 entirely. The script is hard-wired to block 5 (MODELS, sizing_b5.json, schema). The scout report says the existing script "alone is not evidence" for block 6 (BLIND-DRY-RUN-SCOUT.md:111), and the B6-AN-1 brief excludes the adaptation from its own scope (2026-10-27-b6-analysis/BRIEF.md:67).
- Any comparison with L9's outputs. No comparator exists on any inspected branch (git ls-files on all five checkouts; scout:194, "no verified runnable B6 §13 blind/release/recompute command").
- An independent check of the labelled sensitivity lines. RUN_STATE item 37 makes the recompute the only producer of the b_sens, scaled-allowance and BETA-inclusive lines (RUN_STATE.md:64), and the single-step diagnostic's only computation is this script, so nothing checks those four lines except its own tests.

COST. The synthetic suite ran 114 tests in 67.4 s, 18 skipped, all OK. I ran it on this MacBook Air (Apple M4, 4 performance and 6 efficiency cores, 24 GB) while another agent's test_dry_run was also running (load average 5). Real-archive run time has never been recorded. My estimate (INFERRED): plistlib parses about 31 MB/s per core on a synthetic powermetrics-shaped frame (bench run here), so a session of roughly 20-43 GiB of plist takes about 11-23 min on one core, or about 3-6 min with 4 workers.

PER SESSION. Possible for each ALPHA or BETA pack on its own: per-run energies, b_op, NEG-8, reported cells, floors, the machine line and the scaled cells. Dominance, GAMMA contrasts and the aggregate floor gate need all three windows (script:2421-2433). The script stops on a compressed plist (script:401-413). Python 3.14's standard library now reads zstd (checked on this Air: compression.zstd 1.5.7), so it could read the desk-compressed archives without breaking the stdlib-only rule.

WHAT IT CAN REPLACE. Once a comparator exists, the recompute plus that comparator does the same job as block-5 plan §3.1 step 12 (a judge and a refuter re-derive every printed number) for every quantity it covers. It also lets the two cold passes on L9 before release (ED-RULING item 3) and block 6 §13's two blind cold passes shrink to one executing pass, limited to what the recompute does not cover. It does not replace the full-size chain tests, step 1 validation, the step 9b refit (so the ruling's option (b) would have left the fit unchecked), or the release's own digest-equality check.

ITS OWN REVIEWS FOUND REAL DEFECTS, ALL IN THE RECOMPUTE ITSELF:
- F4: falling back to the CSV let a planted 1% fault pass (7e322b76).
- F12: a loose bar let a +0.125 change to rho pass (7e322b76).
- B1: the comparison counts changed with the output mode (d701302f).
No document I could read shows it catching an L9 defect. The cross-check notes are in /Users/edr/night-archive/independent-recompute/CROSS-CHECK.md, which is absent on this machine. One known open item before release: the recompute's meter clock-fit bins differ from the pipeline's, giving 0.020 J against a 1.24e-4 J bar, and the fit-method ruling is still owed (commit 7e322b76).

steps.name: Archive inputs, plan-tree seal and harvest-checkout checks
steps.what: Reads harvest.json, derived/roster.json, derived/exclusions.json, derived/flags.jsonl and whole-window-verdict.json. Hashes the archived plan_tree.json against the sealed digest in sizing_b5.json (falls back to the analysis checkout's copy) and checks that the reference slots in the tree agree with the run-id roles. Flags a harvest checkout that is not recorded clean.
steps.protects: Analysing the wrong pack or plan tree, a reference used in a slot it was not planned for, or a harvest run from a dirty tree. These are stop-class flags: roster_plan_tree_not_sealed, reference_slot_disagrees, harvest_checkout_not_clean.
steps.cost: Negligible: a few JSON reads per window.
steps.caught_real_defects: None recorded in the commits read.
steps.redundant_with: Partly with L9 step 0/3 hash ties and the harvest's own provenance checks (harvest.py). It is independent code, which is the point.
steps.proposal: Keep as is. Pin the recompute commit and record it in the release record, as the scout requires (BLIND-DRY-RUN-SCOUT.md:36).

steps.name: Calibration bracket b_op recomputed from the pre/post captures
steps.what: Finds the two calibration captures through derived/bracket-binding.json. Computes b_op = max(pre, post) + max(|post - pre|, 14.531 ms) and compares it with withheld/bracket-evaluation.json at 1e-6 relative. Flags drift over the 15.502 ms budget, and any member whose stored b_fiducial_s differs (exactly) from the pre-capture value.
steps.protects: A wrong operative timing bound, which widens every envelope and allowance, and a capture mix-up between pre and post.
steps.cost: Negligible.
steps.caught_real_defects: None recorded. The capture-name fallback flag was added in round 2 (commit 42774681).
steps.redundant_with: L9 step 3b (prepare_brackets, wt/l9/joulewise/b5_analysis/dry_run.py:700) computes the same arithmetic independently. It does NOT cover the pulse-fit refit that produces each capture's b_fiducial_s (step 9b).
steps.proposal: Keep. State in the release record that b_fiducial_s is an input to the recompute and is not re-derived. The calibration fit's only executed check is L9 step 9b plus the harvest.

steps.name: Independent plist parse; plist vs CSV identity; stop on a missing or compressed plist
steps.what: Parses raw/powermetrics.plist frame by frame with plistlib and places each record from first_sample_end_point_epoch_s plus cumulative elapsed_ns. Sums the cpu, gpu and ane rails. Checks the whole-second plist labels against an affine pad, and requires exact equality with power_trace.csv. A missing or .zst plist makes that run not_compared, which is a stop flag when the run is in the compared set.
steps.protects: A fault that the shared capture code writes into both the CSV and the summary. Audit F4 showed that integrating the CSV let a planted 1% fault pass. With the plist, seven mismatch flags fire.
steps.cost: Dominant runtime cost. plistlib parses about 31 MB/s per core on the M4 Air (synthetic frame benchmark; INFERRED for real frames). A session is about 43 GiB, mostly plist (cadence plan:15; RUN_STATE 37).
steps.caught_real_defects: Yes, in the recompute itself: audit F4 (commit 7e322b76, 'a planted 1% fault in both passed').
steps.redundant_with: Nothing; this is the only plist-based path independent of the capture's CSV writer.
steps.proposal: Add streaming .zst reading through Python 3.14's stdlib compression.zstd, which keeps the stdlib-only test (test_archives.py:122) valid. The recompute can then run on desk-compressed archives on any machine, with no 43 GiB restore. Add a stdlib multiprocessing pool over members with deterministic merge order, so output bytes are unchanged (about 4x on Air performance cores). This is non-governed code with one executing review and a test that serial and parallel outputs are byte-identical.
steps.saves: Removes the decompress-to-scratch step (about 43 GiB of disk per session, which does not fit a 30 GB cloud seat or the Air's 41 GiB free for more than one session). Cuts the parse from roughly 11-23 min to about 3-6 min per session (INFERRED).

steps.name: Per-run phase energy (overlap integral) and anchor-shift envelopes vs stored summary
steps.what: For prefill, decode and request, finds the one start/end event pair, integrates the overlap with the 100 ms records, and computes the shift envelopes at b_pre, b_op and 0. Compares energy and the b_pre envelope with summary_metrics.json at 1e-6 relative (1e-6 J absolute near zero).
steps.protects: Edge-placement errors (S-13 derivation: a 1 ms edge shift is 0.047 J), dropped records (3.4-5.5 J), and stored-summary corruption.
steps.cost: Cheap once records are parsed.
steps.caught_real_defects: No defect found in production data. On the non-claim rehearsals it reproduced 145 phases to 1e-9 J (commit ab14e02d; S-13 cites 154 of 154 within 7e-15 J, a count that does not match). The lead re-ran R18, alpha-1 and gamma-2 with 6 OK (commit 353ec75f).
steps.redundant_with: L9 step 2 re-reduction (dry_run.py:685-694) recomputes the same energies through repository code. The two are complementary, not duplicate, because they share no code. This is the S-13 '1 mJ per run phase energy' term.
steps.proposal: Run this per session, the same day as the harvest and before desk compression. Output is structure-only (count of stored_energy_mismatch and comparison summary; the CLI line already prints only sha256, flag counts and the comparison counts, script:2647-2655). Run it against the harvest's stored values now, and against L9's step-2 outputs once the comparator (R15) exists. A wrong edge or a dropped record then surfaces before the next session of that pack, not at release.
steps.saves: Moves defect discovery from release (days to weeks later) to the session day. Avoids a late recollection.

steps.name: NEG-8 drift bound and allowance recomputed
steps.what: Takes the clean corpus (10-12 members, the desk cap) and the survivors (plan-tree slots, intersected with the verdict basis, minus screen losses). Computes the bound max(envelope, t*s*sqrt(1/n_start + 1/n_end)) and the allowance max(spread, bound). Compares the allowance with withheld/neg8-rescreen-bracket.json, checks survivor counts, and flags an excluded reference in the screen (stop).
steps.protects: A wrong allowance. It enters every floor, every contrast's D, and the scaled lines.
steps.cost: Cheap: about 19 reference/corpus members per window.
steps.caught_real_defects: None recorded. R18 rehearsal value reproduced (test_rehearsals.py:65-78).
steps.redundant_with: L9 steps 4/9 through whole_window.harvest_neg8_allowance_bracket (B5-PLAN:241-242). Independent code.
steps.proposal: Keep. Run per pack as each pack lands (ALPHA and BETA do not need GAMMA).

steps.name: Kept-unit selection and member validity
steps.what: Builds units from the roster. Checks that the declared kept_units equal those implied by members_excluded (kept_units_disagree is a stop flag), that members are within the verdict membership, and the ABBA shape, model and GAMMA tags, at least 3 records per long phase, the token counts 2048/512, and a zero interpolation bound.
steps.protects: Analysing a unit that the exclusions removed, or one that is mis-shaped or mis-labelled.
steps.cost: Cheap.
steps.caught_real_defects: None recorded.
steps.redundant_with: L9 step 3 (exclusions consumer) and kept_units.py. Both consume the SAME derived/exclusions.json, so a wrong exclusion decision upstream (in the harvest) is caught by neither. AN-18's widening, which would re-derive exclusions from raw monitor records, is not implemented.
steps.proposal: Keep. Separately, either build AN-18's exclusion re-derivation for the flag families that can remove a unit (battery, outside CPU, thermal, clock), or record by a blind lead line that the exclusions are checked only by the harvest plus the L9 consumer. Then point the single executing review (G2) at the harvest's exclusion code.
steps.saves: 0 (this is a coverage gap, not a saving)

steps.name: Estimator 1: reported energy per cell (H1)
steps.what: Reported phase energy per model, phase and cell over kept repeats and quads, with a minimum of 5 per stratum. Interval with the B term, attribution floor and J/token. p42 is marked expected_unresolvable.
steps.protects: A wrong headline number in the paper.
steps.cost: Cheap.
steps.caught_real_defects: None recorded.
steps.redundant_with: L9 step 10 (issue_reported_energy). Independent code.
steps.proposal: Compute per pack as soon as that pack's archive exists. ALPHA and BETA run independently and in parallel.
steps.saves: Release-time wall clock: cells are already computed when the pack closes.

steps.name: Floors (absolute and comparative), minted floor and floor gate (H2)
steps.what: Point floor, corner-widened floor, guard, allowance-widened minted floor, and per-cell floor_gate = max(abs, cmp). The comparative form uses the shared width at b_op.
steps.protects: A wrong attribution floor, which decides contrast outcomes and the dominance branch.
steps.cost: Cheap. The corner enumeration is capped by PLAN 5 at 16 units.
steps.caught_real_defects: Not in production data. It agreed with L9's operative floor on all 8 synthetic cells at 8.8e-14 relative (commit 42774681).
steps.redundant_with: L9 steps 4-5 (extract_detection_floors, mint). Independent code.
steps.proposal: Keep. Per pack, as R6.

steps.name: Dominance ratios R and R_cm, branch A/B (H3)
steps.what: For 8 floors, R = corner-widened / point floor >= 2. For comparative floors, R_cm >= 2. Branch B if any fails. Requires all three packs.
steps.protects: A wrong dominance branch, which changes which floor arithmetic is reported.
steps.cost: Cheap.
steps.caught_real_defects: None recorded.
steps.redundant_with: L9 step 6 (dominance close-out). Independent code.
steps.proposal: Keep. Runs only once all three windows exist (script:2421).

steps.name: GAMMA contrasts, Holm, decision interval, outcome words, LOO, descriptive magnitudes (H4/H5)
steps.what: Per GAMMA cell: quad differences, dbar, metrology D (with allowance), t, p, Holm across the two contrasts, decision interval against the aggregate floor gate, outcome word, leave-one-quad-out, decision_vs_floor and cross-window disclosures. A cell below n=5 sets p=1.
steps.protects: A wrong claim word, which is the paper's central inference.
steps.cost: Cheap.
steps.caught_real_defects: None recorded.
steps.redundant_with: L9 steps 8-9 (finalize, analyze-claims). Independent code.
steps.proposal: Keep. Runs after all three windows exist. For block 6, after each GAMMA session and its paired ALPHA and BETA sessions (needs R16).

steps.name: Tier-2 disclosures: load-sensitivity line and battery-assist line
steps.what: Restores units dropped only for the three load-correlated codes and recomputes with the same estimators. Recomputes cells and contrasts without battery-assisted members.
steps.protects: Mis-stated sensitivity disclosures.
steps.cost: Cheap.
steps.caught_real_defects: None recorded.
steps.redundant_with: L9 step 11 disclosure producer. Independent code.
steps.proposal: Keep.

steps.name: Labelled sensitivity lines: b_sens bound, scaled allowance (incl. GAMMA outcomes), alternative allowance, BETA a1/a4/a5-inclusive
steps.what: Computes the item-37 lines, decided blind on 2026-10-14 between 02:57 and 07:53. Scaling factor max(1, E/E_ref, T/T_ref), applied per arm for GAMMA. The pooled BETA floor uses a triangle-inequality upper bound above 16 units. The extra BETA sessions are read through --extra-beta with isolated readers.
steps.protects: Disclosure honesty about an untested allowance transfer and about the sessions that were removed.
steps.cost: Cheap. The BETA-inclusive line needs three extra session archives.
steps.caught_real_defects: None recorded.
steps.redundant_with: NOTHING. RUN_STATE item 37 makes the recompute the only producer of these lines ('computed by the independent recompute after release'). No second implementation exists, so S-13 agreement cannot apply to them.
steps.proposal: Accept a single implementation, because these lines are labelled and never enter a claim. As the cheap independent check, have the one release reviewer re-derive one cell of each line by hand from the recompute's member detail (--member-detail). The hand-checked synthetic worked examples already exist (test_round3.py:259, :333, :535, :611). Do not build a second implementation.
steps.saves: Avoids a second implementation and a cold gate for labelled lines.

steps.name: Whole-machine lines: PLAN 8.2 request cross-check and gross per-phase meter energy
steps.what: Fits the meter clock from stream-*.jsonl, integrates gross DC input over each phase span, reports rho, flags battery activity at request level, and adds four edge-corner sensitivities. No phase line for GAMMA.
steps.protects: A wrong whole-machine line. It is descriptive and never a claim.
steps.cost: Cheap. 50 Hz meter streams.
steps.caught_real_defects: Recompute-side: F12, where a +0.125 change to rho passed the old max(0.5, 0.5%) bar (commit 7e322b76). OPEN: the recompute's clock-fit bins differ from the pipeline's, moving one sample by 1,249 ns and the energy by 0.020 J against a 1.24e-4 J bar. The run is flagged meter_request_mismatch and the fit-method ruling is still owed.
steps.redundant_with: B6-AN-1 S-15 and the block-5 whole-machine producer (B6 brief:62). Independent.
steps.proposal: Before the block-5 release, a blind lead ruling on the meter fit method, or on the printed precision of the machine line. Otherwise S-13's 'half a unit of the last printed digit' fails at 0.02 J whenever the line prints at 0.01 J. Choose the fit, do not widen the bar.
steps.saves: Avoids a release-day refusal over a known 0.02 J method difference.

steps.name: Single-step reconstruction diagnostic (F5)
steps.what: A step-edge reconstruction per member, printed as m ± h with no B term. Labelled diagnostic; replaces nothing.
steps.protects: Nothing in a claim. It is a diagnostic of prefill scatter.
steps.cost: Cheap.
steps.caught_real_defects: n/a
steps.redundant_with: Nothing; the recompute is its only producer.
steps.proposal: Keep as is. Same single-implementation treatment as R11.

steps.name: Comparison report, stop flags, sanitized deterministic output
steps.what: Counts compared and not-compared runs by reason (only runs in the compared set). Marks each flag stops_comparison and STRUCTURE. Writes sorted JSON and prints sha256, flag counts and the comparison summary.
steps.protects: A silently partial comparison being read as agreement.
steps.cost: Negligible.
steps.caught_real_defects: Yes, recompute-side: B1, where the summary counted members loaded only for detail (commit d701302f).
steps.redundant_with: None.
steps.proposal: Keep. The stdout line is already structure-only, so it can be posted from a blind per-session run.

steps.name: MISSING: comparator from recompute to L9 outputs under S-13
steps.what: Does not exist on any inspected branch. It would read L9's restricted outputs (step-2 re-reductions, extraction, mint, claim verdicts, projections, fills) and the recompute JSON. It would check each run phase within 1 mJ and each printed quantity, unrounded, within half its last printed digit, and keep each observed difference (S-13 requires it printed beside the tolerance).
steps.protects: The release condition itself (RUN_STATE item 37 (ii); B6 §12.3 item 4). Without it the condition cannot be evaluated.
steps.cost: Build: small, a quantity map plus bars. Run: seconds.
steps.caught_real_defects: n/a (unbuilt). The 8-floor synthetic match (test_reconcile.py:266) is the only executed recompute-to-L9 comparison.
steps.redundant_with: Would subsume B5-PLAN §3.1 step 12's re-derivation (G1).
steps.proposal: Build it now in the cloud on S10 synthetic outputs, in parallel with L9-2. It emits a pass/fail count and the worst ratio |diff|/bar per family, which is structure-only and runs blind. It withholds the values until the release event. Extend it to the step-11 rendered fills so it also checks the printed text.
steps.saves: Makes G1 and G2 lightenable. Removes a release-day build.

steps.name: MISSING: block-6 adaptation (per session, pairing, counting)
steps.what: The script is block-5 only: MODELS, sizing_b5.json, the v5 schema, and a fixed three-window aggregate. Block 6 needs per-session runs, GAMMA pairing to round-k floors, the item-53 counting consumer (not a block-5 claim_usable veto), and S-13 comparison.
steps.protects: Block 6's release condition (§12.3 item 4).
steps.cost: Build: moderate. It must share no code with L9 or the B6 driver.
steps.caught_real_defects: n/a
steps.redundant_with: None.
steps.proposal: Give a separate cloud seat the adaptation now (B6-AN-1 is told it is 'Not yours'). Interface: a session archive plus pairing manifest in, the same JSON schema out. Run each block-6 session the day it is harvested.
steps.saves: Avoids block 6 waiting on an unbuilt check at close (2026-11-01).

steps.name: Synthetic test suite (E1-E19, S1-S14, round-3, audit-fix)
steps.what: 114 tests: worked examples, closed-form three-pack archives, planted faults, stdlib-only, determinism.
steps.protects: Recompute arithmetic errors. This is the recompute's own 'independent check'.
steps.cost: 67.4 s wall (57.7 s user) on the M4 Air under concurrent load. 18 skipped (real rehearsal archives).
steps.caught_real_defects: The planted-fault tests encode F4, F12 and B1 (test_auditfix.py:33, :222, :123).
steps.redundant_with: None.
steps.proposal: Run in cloud CI on every recompute change. It is cheap and should run anywhere.

steps.name: Real-rehearsal tests (R18, alpha-1, gamma-2; S10/R2 cross-check fixtures)
steps.what: Opt-in tests against non-claim rehearsal archives and the S10/R2 synthetic L9 outputs, at fixed paths under /Users/edr/night-archive. They are skipped off the Mac (absent on this Air).
steps.protects: Real-format parsing and the 8-floor L9 match.
steps.cost: Unmeasured. Run by the lead on the Mac: '6 OK' (commit 353ec75f).
steps.caught_real_defects: None recorded.
steps.redundant_with: None.
steps.proposal: Package the non-claim rehearsal and S10/R2 fixtures as compressed release assets of the private data repo, with SHA-256 manifests (cadence plan §3 mechanism). Make the paths an environment variable so the tests run in cloud CI and on the Air, not only on the measurement Mac.
steps.saves: Takes these tests off the quiet Mac. They run on every change instead of when the Mac is free.

steps.name: Review gate on recompute code changes (PR #571: audit, Fable and Opus cold passes, delta pass)
steps.what: Three review rounds over about 4 h on 2026-10-22 (commits 7e322b76 15:29, 353ec75f 18:53, d701302f 19:27).
steps.protects: Recompute defects that would make it agree falsely.
steps.cost: About 4 h wall, 3 seats plus lead.
steps.caught_real_defects: Yes: F4 (CSV fallback would pass a 1% fault), F12 (loose bars), B1 (counts depend on the output mode). These were caught by the audit and the first cold pass. The delta pass found B1 (medium); B2-B4 were comments and labels.
steps.redundant_with: Each finding was turned into an executed planted-fault test (R17), which now guards it permanently.
steps.proposal: For future recompute changes: one executing review whose brief requires a planted fault for each new comparison (the F4 pattern), plus R17 green. No second cold pass unless the first finds a blocker.
steps.saves: About 2 review rounds per change (roughly 2-3 h each, INFERRED from PR #571 timestamps).

steps.name: Gate it replaces: B5-PLAN §3.1 step 12 results cold gate (judge + refuter re-derive every printed number)
steps.what: After steps 3-11, a judge and a refuter re-derive every printed number from the step artifacts.
steps.protects: A confident wrong printed number.
steps.cost: Cadence plan: 'days per gate round'. #416-style audits took 7 cold rounds over about 2 days (task brief; INFERRED to be comparable here).
steps.caught_real_defects: Never run (block 5 not released). Pruning list: 'no cold judge produced a W catch in three periods' (pruning_list_2026-10-14.md:525).
steps.redundant_with: R3-R10 plus R15. The recompute re-derives every covered printed quantity from raw records, which is stronger than re-deriving from L9's own artifacts. It is executed and compared under registered bars.
steps.proposal: Replace step 12 with: the recompute plus the comparator (R15, extended to step-11 fills) passing S-13, and one reviewer reading the comparator table. That reviewer also hand-checks one cell of each single-implementation line (R11, R13) and the uncovered surface listed under G2. Make the change by a prospective erratum while block 5 is blind.
steps.saves: One multi-day two-seat gate at release (INFERRED 1-2 days).

steps.name: Gate it lightens: cold Fable + Opus passes on L9 before release (ED-RULING item 3)
steps.what: Two executing cold passes on L9 code, moved by Ed from 'at merge' to 'before release'.
steps.protects: L9 code defects.
steps.cost: Two seats, a cold read of a large code line (multi-hour each; INFERRED).
steps.caught_real_defects: Not yet run on L9-2.
steps.redundant_with: For arithmetic, R3-R10 plus R15 on the real data. NOT redundant for what the recompute takes as input: step 1 strict validation, the step 3/kept_units exclusion consumer and the harvest exclusions (R5 gap), step 9b calibration refit (R1 gap), step 10-11 custody and rendering, and determinism.
steps.proposal: One executing cold pass, briefed only on the uncovered surface: exclusion derivation, 9b, validation, rendering and digest determinism. It runs in parallel with the blind dry run in the cloud. The second pass is dropped once the comparator passes.
steps.saves: One cold seat and its fix round (INFERRED about 0.5-1 day).

steps.name: Gate it lightens: block-6 §13 two blind executing cold passes plus full-size synthetic chain before the blind dry run
steps.what: Block 6's analysis code must be 'tested ... on full-size production-shaped synthetic archives ... and given one blind executing cold pass by Fable and one by Opus' before the dry run.
steps.protects: Block-6 driver defects.
steps.cost: Full-size synthetic runs take about 6 h each (ED-RULING) plus two cold seats.
steps.caught_real_defects: Not run yet.
steps.redundant_with: Same as G2 once R16 exists, and the block-6 blind dry run on real archives is the end-to-end test (ED-RULING pattern).
steps.proposal: A §17 entry: the ED-RULING pattern (cached full-size run, one executing review, real blind dry run as the end-to-end test, cold pass before release), with the R16 recompute plus comparator as the arithmetic check. One executing refuter checks the entry.
steps.saves: About 6-13 h of synthetic runs per round, plus one cold seat.

steps.name: Critique of the 9b ruling's option (b): 'arithmetic left to the independent recompute'
steps.what: Option (b) would have hash-bound the harvest's fit and relied on the recompute for verification.
steps.protects: Pulse-calibration correctness.
steps.cost: n/a
steps.caught_real_defects: n/a
steps.redundant_with: The recompute does NOT refit pulses. It reads b_fiducial_s from instrument_evidence.json (script:637-660). Under (b) the fit would have no executed check outside the harvest.
steps.proposal: Keep Ed's (c). When plan item 2.4 (governed deadline fix) lands, do not cite the recompute as covering the fit unless a stdlib pulse-fit recompute is added to it.

steps.name: Not replaceable: full-size synthetic dry-run and release-equality tests; the release digest check
steps.what: These check that the chain runs and is deterministic.
steps.protects: Tooling refusal and non-determinism.
steps.cost: About 6 h and 13 h (L9-1 report).
steps.caught_real_defects: The joined runs found the 9b wall-deadline refusal (l9-joined REPORT.md:13).
steps.redundant_with: Not with the recompute, which checks values, not that L9 executes.
steps.proposal: No change beyond the ED-RULING (already optional diagnostics). The recompute adds nothing here.

parallelism: Members are independent. Member.__init__ (script:370-470) parses one plist and integrates one run, so a stdlib multiprocessing pool over the compared run ids, merged in sorted order, gives byte-identical output and about 4x speed on 4 performance cores (INFERRED).

Packs are independent up to the aggregate. ALPHA and BETA windows (R1, R3-R7, R10-R12) need no GAMMA, and only dominance, contrasts and the floor gate wait for all three (script:2421). Run each pack's recompute the day it is harvested. For block 6, R16 makes this a two-level DAG matching cadence plan item 2.3.

The recompute shares no code with L9, so it can run on a different machine at the same time as the block-5 blind dry run. The dry run uses the Mac (ruled, ED-RULING 6a); the recompute uses the Air from compressed copies. Neither waits on the other, and the comparator joins them afterwards.

Build R15 (comparator) and R16 (block-6 adaptation) now in cloud seats, in parallel with L9-2 and B6-AN-1. They can be built against S10 synthetic L9 outputs (test_reconcile.py:12, :266) and B6-AN-1's synthetic fixtures. Their interfaces are JSON in and JSON out.
Run G2's single cold pass on the uncovered surface in the cloud while the Mac runs the dry run (ED-RULING item 3 already allows this).
map.where_to_run:
Measurement Mac (M3 Max): never the recompute. CPU load contaminates a session, and RUN_STATE item 78 (s6-p1 lost to a leftover Codex daemon) shows the cost. The only Mac-side step is making each harvested archive available: copy it, or let the desk zstd step produce the compressed copy, with SHA-256s from the harvest record.

MacBook Air (Apple M4, 4 performance and 6 efficiency cores, 24 GB, 41 GiB free disk, python3.14 with stdlib compression.zstd, all verified on this machine): the right home for real-data recompute runs.
- Every session's run happens here the same day, as structure-only output.
- At release, the full block-5 run happens here with the comparator.
- Why here: the script needs only the standard library and the archive. Real blinded data stays on Ed's own hardware instead of moving to a shared cloud VM. And streaming .zst (R2) avoids the 43 GiB-per-session restore that its 41 GiB of free disk could not hold for more than one session.
- Expected cost (INFERRED): roughly 11-23 min per session single-core, or about 3-6 min with a 4-worker pool.
- Caveat: another agent's full-size test_dry_run was running on this Air during my measurements (load 5). Do not run heavy cloud-able tests there while it does recompute work.

Cloud (Claude 4 vCPU/15 GB/30 GB; Codex 5 vCPU/17 GB): everything that needs no real data.
- The synthetic suite: 67 s here, fine on 4 vCPU.
- Building R15 and R16, and their reviews and planted-fault tests.
- The G2 and G3 single executing passes.
- R18, once the non-claim rehearsal fixtures are published as compressed release assets.

Real block-5 or block-6 data should go to the cloud only if Ed explicitly approves that custody path (cadence plan §3). The recompute's run time does not need the cloud, so this keeps "as much in the cloud as possible" without moving blinded data there.
map.amendment_rules:
Governing text, quoted:

- Block-6 registration, §12.4 (jw/docs/registrations/block6_replication_DRAFT.md:1170-1173): "No change to registered arithmetic after any block-6 data exists. A rule of §8 found wrong may be changed while block 6 is blinded, by a dated entry in §17 checked by one executing refuter; it then applies to every session, and the result under the original rule is printed beside it. If a registered line proves too strict, the registered result is printed with a labelled alternative beside it."
- Block-6 header (same file, lines 1-30): "A change after that commit is a dated entry in §17 with its reason (§12.4 says what such a change may and may not touch)."
- S-13 (line 1155-1157): "The observed agreement is printed beside the tolerance and is never used as it."
- Block-5 registration (configs/campaigns/v5_claim_25g83/registration_block5.md:564-567): "A cold erratum is a change to a sealed document made this way; it is prospective when it is made before the bytes it governs exist." Here "this way" means a judge seat, checked by a refuter, with one round back to the judge.
- B5-PLAN §3.2 item 3 (analysis_plan_block5.md:195-199), for repairs after release: allowed only if "written and reviewed by seats that have read no released number, adds a synthetic fixture reproducing the failure, and leaves every other registered synthetic fixture's output byte-identical. Any other change goes to a cold gate before it runs, and its outputs are labelled as produced after unblinding."
- ED-RULING 2026-10-27: "It amends nothing registered or sealed: ... blinding, the independent recompute and its agreement bars, and the release record are unchanged."
- Cadence plan:4-6: "Items marked amend change how a number is computed, and need a dated, blind amendment before the data they apply to are opened."

Applied to this segment:
- R2 and R15-R18 change only the non-governed recompute and comparator code. They need a lead ruling and one executing review.
- G1 edits sealed B5-PLAN step 12, so it needs a prospective erratum while block 5 is blind.
- G3 needs a §17 entry with one executing refuter.
- G2 changes Ed's own ruling, so it needs Ed.
open_questions: What tolerance governs the block-5 release comparison? RUN_STATE item 37 says 'a tolerance fixed before release'. S-13 (1 mJ per run, half the last printed digit) is written in the block-6 registration, and the recompute header's own bars are tighter (1e-6 relative, or 1% of the smallest printed half-width). I found no registered text that adopts S-13 for block 5. A blind lead line should adopt it before release.

Meter clock-fit method. The recompute and pipeline fits differ by 0.020 J on synthetic data (commit 7e322b76, 'Lead to rule on the fit method before release'). Whether the per-phase machine line passes S-13 depends on its printed precision, which I could not find fixed.
AN-18 (re-derive member exclusions from raw monitor records) was ruled KEEP and widened on 2026-10-14 but never built. Build it, or formally drop it and put the exclusion code under G2's review?

Real-archive run time of the recompute is unmeasured. The lead's '6 OK' rehearsal run (353ec75f) recorded no timing. My 11-23 min per session figure comes from a synthetic plistlib benchmark (INFERRED).

Custody: may compressed real block-5 and block-6 archives be copied to the MacBook Air, which is not the measurement Mac, before release? The cadence plan §3 proposes this for an analysis machine, but no ruling I read approves it.

Did the recompute ever catch an L9 or pipeline defect? The CROSS-CHECK.md rounds 1-3 under /Users/edr/night-archive/independent-recompute/ are not on this machine. Commit 42774681 says rulings J5, X1 and J8 were 'built in', which suggests disagreements were reconciled (INFERRED, not verified).

The rehearsal phase count is inconsistent. Commit ab14e02d says 145 phases at 1e-9 J. S-13's derivation (block6_replication_DRAFT.md:1158) says 154 of 154 at 7e-15 J. Which archive set and bar does the S-13 derivation rest on?

The single-implementation lines (b_sens, scaled allowance including GAMMA outcome words, alternative allowance, BETA-inclusive, single-step) have no second computation. Is a hand check of one cell each by the release reviewer (R11) enough, given they are labelled and never claims?

science.segment: Independent recompute: coverage and overlap (scripts/independent_recompute_b5.py @ 9ca87bce, tests/independent_recompute/, S-13, RUN_STATE item 37)

judgments.reason: Reading .zst directly is a sound idea, but the proposal as written drops a provenance check that the current path has. Today the only route from a compressed bundle into a reader is restore_run_to_scratch.py. That tool needs a matching compression-journal entry and checks the decompressed size and SHA-256 before the reader starts (restore_run_to_scratch.py:1-9; desk_restore.py:132-140). The proposal names no digest check. The recompute itself records no per-file input digests: it keeps only exclusions_sha256, files_read and program_sha256 (script:2383, 2570). Desk compression also compresses every file of at least 1 MiB, not only the plist (desk_compress.py:250, 298-318). So a reader that handles only the plist would leave power_trace.csv flagged archive_file_missing, which does not stop the run, and would silently lose the exact plist-vs-CSV identity check (script:428-429). The meter streams would also become meter_absent, which is not a stop flag either (script:58-63), so the whole-machine line would vanish from the comparison without anything stopping. That the CSV and meter files exceed 1 MiB is INFERRED. Finally, pyproject.toml:9 allows Python >=3.11, while compression.zstd needs 3.14, and the output does not record the interpreter. The parallel pool is low-risk if the proposed byte-identity test triggers the deduplicated flags: Reader.flag deduplicates against one shared list (script:268-272), and per-worker lists would need the same deduplication at merge.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: The recompute reads a .zst whose decompressed bytes were never tied to the harvest's sources/SHA256SUMS or the desk journal sha256, so the release record cannot show which bytes were compared. Or, if only the plist is taught .zst, the compressed meter streams raise meter_absent without stopping, and the machine-line agreement is missing while comparison_stopped=false. A later run on Python 3.12 cannot reproduce the run at all.
evidence_refs: wt/recompute git 7e322b76 (compressed meter stream raises meter_absent)

judgments.reason: The claim that the output is structure-only holds only for stdout. The --out JSON written at script:2634-2637 holds per-member E_j, envelopes and reported cells, and flag details carry own_j and stored_j (script:466-470). Block-6 §12.2 permits blind runs on arriving sessions only 'with only structure written out'. B5-REG §8 lists the readers of restricted paths before the release: the harvest, the blind dry run and the scheduler. The recompute is not named, and every offload copy is itself restricted (registration_block5.md:4884, 4895). The step is also inconsistent with itself. It says 'before desk compression', yet where_to_run says 'never the Mac' and 'Air from compressed copies'. RUN_STATE item 37 already places the recompute at the desk before compression, so this is not new. The 'avoids a late recollection' benefit is also a hazard. A recompute mismatch is not a flag the block-6 plan names as excluding (item 37 (c)). Re-collecting or re-arming because an energy-derived agreement check failed would be a data-dependent selection decision. The cure for a pipeline-side mismatch is re-reduction from the raw records, not new data.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: A same-day run on the Air writes reported cells and GAMMA outcome words into a JSON in a directory that a Codex CLI agent on the same machine can open. A seat then builds or repairs block-6 analysis code after seeing outcome-bearing values, so the code is no longer written blind. Separately, a stored_energy_mismatch on session k prompts a re-arm of that pack, and a reviewer reads it as optional stopping.

judgments.reason: Accepting a single implementation for labelled lines is defensible. However, a hand check of 'one cell of each line' does not cover the GAMMA scaled-allowance outcome words. There are only two contrasts, so an arm-swap or indexing defect in one of them survives a one-cell check. judgments.reason: The comparator is needed, and building it is right. The failure modes lie in using it to lighten G1 and G2. (1) S-13 is written as a numeric tolerance, but the printed results also include categorical outcomes: the GAMMA outcome words, dominance branch A/B, the p42 registered refusal, and for block 6 the replication word, which needs the same outcome word and the same sign of dbar. These need exact-match families, or a numeric-only comparator passes while a word differs. (2) A quantity map with no exhaustiveness check silently skips any printed fill it does not map. The comparator should refuse unless every step-11 fill placeholder is either mapped or listed as uncovered. (3) Block 5 has no adopted tolerance. Item 37 says only 'a tolerance fixed before release', and S-13 is block-6 text, so encoding S-13 for block 5 needs a blind adoption line first. (4) Emitting 'worst |diff|/bar per family' blind is a value derived from science quantities, so classify it before posting. (5) The comparator itself needs planted-fault tests per family, for example perturbing one L9 value by 2x the bar, in the F4/F12 pattern. Otherwise its 'pass' is vacuous.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: The claim-verdict-to-fill adapter renders 'L2' where analyze-claims gave 'L1'. Every numeric fill agrees within half a digit, the comparator reports pass, and the single reviewer reading its table sees only numbers. The wrong claim word ships.

The block-6 nine-session batch parallelises across members on the Air's 4 performance cores. With 15 GB of RAM, a cloud seat could also take it if Ed approves custody.

map.segment: Block-6 path from close (2026-10-21, 9/9 counting) to printed block-6 numbers
map.summary:
Block 6 has no analysis code yet. The driver is the 16-line stub at wt/bytes/joulewise/b6/analysis_lane.py:13-16, and none of the needed lines are on main: L9 0576a734/8ad47455, the block-6 line 1706257c/f31aca19, the recompute 9ca87bce and B6-2 all return no to `merge-base --is-ancestor origin/main`. Three findings drive the timeline.

(1) Today's B6-AN-1 seat stopped before writing code. It returned NEEDS_SCOPE (origin/lane/2026-10-27-b6-analysis:.codex-report/B6-AN-1.md:3,17-33) because its brief chose the BYTES work line 991358f7 as the base (BRIEF.md:19,55-57). I confirmed by merge-tree that L9 x 991358f7 conflicts in exactly the 9 listed files. Of those, registry.json alone has 717 hunks, whole_window.py 12 and harvest.py 4. L9-2 x 1706257c (the block-6 registered line) conflicts in only 3 files: hazard_refusals.json (1 hunk), registry.json (1 hunk) and whole_window.py (1 hunk, 43 lines). The first two are regenerated by tooling. L9-2 x main conflicts in registry/SEAL_RECORD/digest_pin_census/repin, which is block-5 landing work and not block-6 work. A 1643-line blind design for this driver already exists (origin/lane/2026-10-22-b6-analysis-design, docs/design/b6_analysis_additions.md: 5 passes, 2 executing consults). Its §15.3 (lines 1146-1165) already gives the 3-conflict base and the recipe. The new brief does not cite it (BRIEF.md:6-11) and re-assigns S-9/S-11, which B6-2 already filled with a dated §17 entry and an executing refuter (VERDICT AGREE, 0 of 840 science runs removed; origin/lane/2026-10-22-b6-s9-s11 9715af39), still unmerged. This is pure duplicated work.

(2) Only two things strictly wait on block 5's release:
- the cross-block phase (§10 summary, §11 side-by-side, replication word, flagged-inclusive comparisons with block 5) plus S-16. These read block 5's release record (design :1130-1134; REG :1209). They are minutes of arithmetic.
- the release itself (REG §12.3 item 2, :1151-1152).

Everything per session is permitted blind now (REG §12.2 :1140-1144): floor units, GAMMA units, §9.5 lines, recompute and per-session S-13 comparisons. The scout's critical path (scout :12) serialises the whole block-6 build, blind run, recompute, release and rerun after block 5's release. That puts two full-size block-6 runs (dry run and rerun) plus gating on the critical path after block 5 releases.

(3) By ED-RULING's own logic, §13's ceremony items are:
- the full-size production-shaped synthetic chain (block 5's took 20,950-24,782 s per dry-run module and 47,231 s for J6; block 6 has 15 session-passes against 3, so roughly 3-5x that, INFERRED);
- 'two cold passes at merge' as a gate before the blind run;
- the scout's self-added release cold gate (scout :206). REG §12.3 :1164-1166 says explicitly there is none.

The protections to keep:
- the independent recompute within S-13 (1 mJ per run phase energy; half a unit of the last printed digit);
- counting from loop acceptance (the item-53 r2-gamma fix);
- the blind structure-only record;
- content-addressed outputs with a determinism check;
- one executing review plus executing cold passes, capped in rounds. #416's rounds 4-7 each changed 0 outputs on 25 real archives (commits 6b54a51d, 7a3b585d, 028f8c50, 49884a10), while rounds 1-3 found real defects (bc588a96: a 162->811 J shadow probe went unflagged).

The MacBook Air is the right host for real block-6 data:
- It runs macOS, so the design's APFS transparent-compressed restore works there (design :68-78). A plain GAMMA unit needs about 129 GiB, which no 30 GB cloud seat can hold.
- Copying the archives to it makes a verified second physical copy. That removes the in-place-rewrite-of-the-only-copy risk (design :1187, audit F1).
- It frees the measurement Mac for block 5's dry run and BYTES, whose t0 deadline is 2026-11-02 (ED-RULING :70-74).

The proposed path cuts the post-block-5-release block-6 critical path from about two full block-6 runs plus gate rounds (INFERRED 1-3 days) to the cross-block phase plus a record (INFERRED hours). The amendments needed are one dated §17 entry (on §13 timing and gates, the S-14 definition, the custody-map root for the Air, and the rerun ordering), one S-15 §17 fill, and lead rulings on the base and on the scout's release gate.

Caveat on read-only: I ran `git merge-tree --write-tree` to list the conflicts. That wrote unreferenced tree and blob objects into the shared .git object store. It changed no ref, worktree or tracked file.

map.amendment_rules:
Governing text, quoted:

- Registration header (jw/docs/registrations/block6_replication_DRAFT.md:18-19): "That commit precedes the start of round 1's first session (its t0, §1.6). A change after that commit is a dated entry in §17 with its reason (§12.4 says what such a change may and may not touch)."
- §12.4 (:1170-1173): "No change to registered arithmetic after any block-6 data exists. A rule of §8 found wrong may be changed while block 6 is blinded, by a dated entry in §17 checked by one executing refuter; it then applies to every session, and the result under the original rule is printed beside it. If a registered line proves too strict, the registered result is printed with a labelled alternative beside it."
- §12.3 (:1164-1166): "The release is a dated record tying the digests of this file, the catalog and every block-6 harvest record. There is no separate cold gate (pruning list 7a decision 2, applied to block 6 as to block 5); the code that computes the numbers has had its two executing cold passes at merge (§13)."
- ED-RULING item 7 (jw/docs/process_traces/2026-10-27-l9-restart/ED-RULING.md:75-77): "Block 6 follows the same principle wherever its registration allows. Where the block-6 registration itself requires a synthetic stage chain before its blind run, that requirement stands until amended by a dated entry under its §17 rules."
- Cadence plan (jw/docs/design/analysis_cadence_plan.md:5-6): items that change how a number is computed "need a dated, blind amendment before the data they apply to are opened". Its §5 (:84-87) asks for the §13 change by "a dated §17 entry with one executing refuter".

How these apply here:
- The §13 process changes (B6-07, B6-09, B6-11, B6-13, B6-15) and the custody-root extension (B6-12) change HOW and WHEN, not WHAT. The registration text requires only a dated §17 entry with its reason. The one-executing-refuter requirement in §12.4 is literally for §8 rule changes; the plan adds it for §13 as prudence. I recommend one entry covering all of them, with one executing refuter, made while block 6 is blinded.
- S-15 (B6-06) fills an open slot that defines WHAT is printed: a §17 entry made blind, with an executing refuter, per design :1172-1177.
- S-9/S-11 are already filled by a §17 entry on an unmerged branch, so only a merge is needed.
- Dropping the scout's extra release gate and choosing the merge base are lead rulings: the first restores registered text; the second touches no registered text.
- Nothing proposed changes an estimator, exclusion, counting rule, bar (S-13) or the blinding rule.

science.segment: Block-6 path from close (2026-10-21, 9/9 counting) to printed block-6 numbers

judgments.reason: The design §15.3 recipe is dated 2026-10-21/22. That is before PR #573's block-6 corrections landed on the BYTES line on 2026-10-22..24, and the proposed base 1706257c lacks them. joulewise/desk_restore.py and scripts/restore_run_to_scratch.py are absent there. The recompute's own RESTORE_TOOL_DETAIL points at the second one. Also missing: 903b5a2f (fail-closed compressed reader, restore-first re-reduction, a 410-line whole_window.py change) and db9e8ab3 (block-6 cold-pass corrections F4/F8/F11/F15/F17). Between 1706257c and 991358f7, whole_window.py changes by 601 lines and cli.py, bundle_read.py, authentication_io.py and desk_compress.py by 69-112 lines each. These are the readers that the analysis's own step 1-2 strict validation and re-reduction run. They are not frozen harvest bytes. The auditor's claim 'no evidence the 6 extra conflicts protect any block-6 number' is therefore unverified, and picking the base to minimise conflicts is not a science criterion.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: The analysis is built on 1706257c + L9. Step 1-2 re-reduction then runs whole_window/cli/bundle_read without #573's cold-pass-corrected readers. The design consult showed that, on these code paths, a compressed or partially restored file makes `reduce` exit 0 with different bytes, and a compressed campaign log reads as empty (design :1635). Any number difference would be a 1 mJ recompute mismatch, which blocks rather than prints. Exclusion and kept-unit differences are different: the recompute takes those as input judgments, so they would pass S-13 silently. The block-6 analysis would then run code that differs from the cold-passed block-6 line, with no record of it.

git diff --stat 1706257c 991358f7 -- joulewise/whole_window.py cli.py bundle_read.py (601/107/69 lines)

judgments.reason: The pure layer is arithmetic over records and fixed tables (the pairing, §10/§11, the structure-only record). B6-03's integration tests and B6-08's executing review cover any drift in the stubbed interfaces before any real run. Dropping S-9/S-11 from the brief is safe only because the auditor re-homes the S-9 desk-exclusion application in the counting consumer. S-15 and S-16 code are still owed, under B6-06 and B6-17. I found no path to a wrong printed number.

judgments.reason: The design restores each unit's sessions in place as APFS-compressed files and compresses them again after the unit (design §0 item 8; :1597-1599). A r3 is shared by G r2 and G r3 (BRIEF A2). A DAG that runs those GAMMA units, or the A r3 floor unit, concurrently interleaves one unit's recompress with another's plain-path reads. The auditor's 'floor reuse removes up to 6 restore passes' contradicts consult F2: steps 5, 9 and 11 read two or three sessions' raw files in one call. A GAMMA unit therefore needs its A and B sessions restored whatever floor outputs it reuses. Reusing content-addressed outputs also needs proof that L9 provenance checks are not bypassed. The auditor itself lists that as untested.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: G r2 finishes and recompresses A r3 while G r3 is still in step 5 or 9 reading A r3 by plain path. Per consult F1, a plain reader on compressed bytes can make `reduce` exit 0 with different bytes, or read a campaign log as empty. A wrong kept set or energy is produced without a refusal. If the recompute is fed the same exclusions it does not catch kept-set errors.

judgments.reason: The blind-run record schema in design §14 carries, per session: acceptance counting, analysis counting and its cause, b5_exclusions_claim_usable, b5_reasons and b6_exclusions_claim_usable. So the first per-session blind run reads r2-gamma's real file under automation, which is exactly what scout :104 asks for. The recompute's veto at :560-561 is kept as an adaptation item (B6-10).
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: None found, provided the release record mechanically requires analysis counting == acceptance counting for all 9 sessions rather than relying on a human read of six fields.

judgments.reason: S-9/S-11 were filled by B6-2 by the registered rule, with a dated §17 entry and an executing refuter. The design names the merge as §15 step 2. The brief's re-assignment (BRIEF.md:62-66) duplicates that work. Applying the exclusion per bundle is still owed, and the proposal re-homes it in the counting consumer.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: Only if the new applying code is never cross-checked against B6-2's replay. Add a structure-only test: the consumer's desk-exclusion count on the real sessions must equal B6-2's recorded '0 of 840 removed'.

judgments.reason: Filling S-15 earlier, blind, through a §17 entry with an executing refuter is the design's own §15 step 7 route. It changes WHAT is printed only before any data are opened, so I found no unblinding path.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: None found. The recompute must also implement the adopted per-phase line, so that S-13 covers it (design :1172-1177).

judgments.reason: (1) The auditor overstates the precedent. ED-RULING amended item 1 for L9 still kept 'one full-size test_dry_run run with the cache on' (:45). Only further full-size runs became optional (:51-52). (2) The checks named as making it redundant do not cover the same failure. The real blind run detects refusals only, since it is blind and no value can be checked. The S-13 recompute treats 'selection, anchors, timing bounds and calibration fits' as input judgments (recompute :4-6) and reads the analysis's exclusions.json (:544-561). So a scale-dependent error in the new block-6 kept-unit path (the block-6 rule plus the S-9 desk exclusion) is invisible to both. Only a synthetic archive with planted truth can see it. (3) The proposed 'short traces' fixtures can fall below the 1 MiB desk-compression size (design §0 item 8), which would make the plain==compressed digest test vacuous.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: A kept-unit or exclusion bug that appears only with production-length traces or compressed (>=1 MiB) files passes the short-trace fixtures. It raises no refusal in the real blind run. It passes S-13 because the recompute consumes the same exclusions. A wrong kept set then feeds the printed per-cell energies and the replication word.

judgments.reason: Running the passes in parallel and concurrently with the blind run is fine; ED item 3 set that precedent. The 'at most one delta round' cap rests on misread evidence. The #416 rounds 4-7 commits say '25 real archives byte-identical' as a regression replay, but those same rounds fixed real defects. Round 4 (6b54a51d) took 13 real block-6 smoke stops to 0 and closed a clock-step-test 'sub-150 blind spot'. Round 5 (7a3b585d) changed printed rows ('19 missing -> 23 printed uncollected'). Round 6 (028f8c50) fixed an Opus HIGH. 'Byte-identical on existing archives' therefore does not show that a round found nothing. Also, the S-13 recompute does not cover selection or exclusion code (recompute :4-6), so it is not redundant for that class.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: A delta round finds a blocker in the kept-unit or exclusion path. Under the cap, the fix is 'verified' by a replay showing real outputs unchanged or changed. Nobody checks that the changed output is right: the recompute takes exclusions as input, and no further cold pass is allowed. The paper then prints a number from code whose last fix no independent reviewer checked.

judgments.reason: Starting early is fine, but two parts of the proposal reduce independence. (a) It builds 'against B6-02's index and pairing interface'. If the recompute takes the pairing from the driver, a pairing bug is common-mode. The registered pairing is a fixed table the recompute should hard-code. (b) The recompute takes exclusions and kept units as inputs (:4-6, :544-561). Block 6 recomputes kept units with new code (the block-6 rule plus the S-9 desk exclusion; design §0 item 2). Unless the recompute derives those independently, S-13 cannot catch them. Sharing the restore is acceptable only if the recompute itself checks each restored file's SHA-256 against the compression record. The design names desk_compress.read_bytes as the recompute's reader (:294-295).
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: The driver pairs G r2 with A r1 instead of A r3, or applies the S-9 desk exclusion to the wrong runs. The recompute consumes the driver's pairing index and exclusions and reproduces the same wrong dbar and cell energies within 1 mJ. S-13 passes, and the wrong replication word is printed.

judgments.reason: The redundancy claim is false as stated. dry_run.py:173-178 (`require_release_equality`) compares output digests, not the code commit. Output equality does not make the dry-run L9 commit 'byte-for-byte' the release tag. ED-RULING item 3 moved L9's cold passes to 'before the release event', after block 5's dry run, so L9 can still change after the commit S-14 would pin. The proposal's re-pin trigger covers only 'if block 5's dry run forces an L9 change'. It misses changes from L9's cold passes or the release path.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: L9's post-dry-run cold pass forces a fix, and block 5 is released at a later tag. Block 6's outputs were computed at the earlier pin, and no re-pin fires because the trigger was only block 5's dry run. The paper claims block 6 used 'block 5's programs at their release tag' (REG §13) when it did not, and the cross-block Δ and the replication word compare outputs of different code.

judgments.reason: A hash-verified second copy is good for provenance, but the plan to analyse it on the Air conflicts with the design's executed finding. The design explicitly rejected 'a copy of the sessions elsewhere' because 'the plans and several bindings name the sessions' original absolute roots (whole_window.py line 6553, analysis_engine/inputs.py line 895, mint_floor_artifact.py line 1130)' (design §4.1 Not chosen). The custody map is a list of path patterns enforced by procedure (B5-REG §8; REG :1134-1135; S-2 names Mac paths). On a personal Air that has the Codex CLI, nothing enforces it. Spotlight indexing and iCloud sync are further INFERRED read paths.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: The archives land under different absolute paths on the Air. Step 0 or the bindings then refuse, and someone 'fixes' the absolute-root bindings in code to run there, which is a provenance-binding change made outside review. Or an agent session on the Air, or Spotlight, reads the restricted plists and blinding is broken. Mitigation: reproduce the exact /Users/edr/night-b6/... paths, exclude them from Spotlight and iCloud, run no agent on the Air, and keep the Mac copy as the authority.

judgments.reason: Running blind before block 5's release is permitted (REG §12.2), but moving it onto the Air removes the premise of Ed's ruling. ED item 6(c) keeps the 120 s wall deadline because 'the dry run runs on the quiet Mac, where the same calibration completed at harvest'. It is conditional on L9-2 confirming, with executed evidence, that a firing 'cannot change a kept unit, a lost-reference list or a printed number'. L9-2's report has no such confirmation: grep finds none, and only option (c)'s fail-closed reading is offered. The plan itself says real-data analysis off the Mac should 'use a fast dedicated machine' (plan :47-48). A fanless Air with a parallel pool is the slow host. Also depends on B6-11 being guarded and on the absolute-root issue in B6-12.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: The deadline fires during a reference-run refit on the Air. If, as is unconfirmed, a firing marks a reference lost instead of refusing, the lost-reference list and kept units change. A consistently slow host fires the same way in both runs, so the digests match and the determinism check passes. A changed kept set is then printed.

judgments.reason: Running the recompute concurrently is fine in principle. 'Sharing each unit's restore cycle' creates the same in-place restore and recompress race as B6-03, unless the restore is reference-counted across both processes or the recompute reads through desk_compress.read_bytes as the design says (:294-295). The kept-set coverage limits of B6-10 also apply.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: The driver finishes the unit and recompresses while the recompute is still reading by plain path. The recompute's input is then truncated or compressed. The run is caught only if the recompute refuses on unreadable bytes, which F4's fix (7e322b76) does for the plist but which is not verified for every file it reads.

judgments.reason: Two blind runs before release do test determinism as well as one after it. Combined with B6-09 (fixes after the passes) and B6-11 (re-pins), though, the proposal re-runs 'only affected units (content-addressed)'. It then removes the one registered full re-run from bytes at the final pin. Unless each unit's content address includes the digest of the whole analysis tree, a fix in shared code such as whole_window.py leaves stale units computed under an older pin. design §14 also says the dry run that satisfies §12.3 item 3 is the full run including the cross-block phase, whose digests the release must reproduce.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: After a late fix the lead judges only GAMMA units affected. Floor-unit outputs from the old pin are reused, and the per-unit digests of the two pre-release runs still match each other. The release opens outputs that do not reproduce from bytes at the pinned S-14, and a reviewer re-running at S-14 gets different numbers. Fix: require one full re-run from archive bytes at the final S-14 pin, whenever it happens, with digest equality to the dry run.

judgments.reason: This is a hard registered dependency (REG §12.3 item 2) for opening values and for the cross-block phase. Keeping it is correct.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: None.

judgments.reason: Folding S-16 into the cross-block invocation is fine as process, but 'minutes of arithmetic' and same-invocation-on-the-Air are unverified. S-16 replays new or changed §8 rules on block 5's usable sessions. The S-9 rule needs each bundle's idle-baseline rails (REG §8.3 item 3), which are raw block-5 bytes on the Mac, not values in B5-RELEASE-RECORD. The proposed host lacks them.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: The automated S-16 step runs on the Air with only block 5's release record available. It either counts the rules it can evaluate and silently prints 0 for the rest, such as the S-9 desk exclusion, or skips them. The printed replay counts beside the rules then understate how block-6 rules act on block 5. The step should declare its raw-byte inputs and run where the block-5 archives are.

judgments.reason: Generating the release record automatically is fine. Cutting the extra gate is not a pure restoration of registered text in the context of this map. REG §12.3 justifies 'no separate cold gate' by 'the code ... has had its two executing cold passes at merge'. B6-09 moves those passes after merge and caps their rounds, and B6-11 allows re-pins, so that justification no longer holds. The scout added the gate on 'the current user's release cold-gate requirement' (scout :206). If that user was Ed, a lead ruling cannot drop it; that is unverified.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: The last fix lands after the capped cold-pass round. Because the gate is cut, nothing checks that the S-14 commit the outputs came from is the commit the cold passes reviewed, so the release goes out on unreviewed code. Replace the gate with a mechanical check in the release record: final S-14 pin == the last commit covered by both cold passes and the executing review, else stop.

missed_items: The S-13 independent recompute is not independent for selection. Its docstring makes 'selection, anchors, timing bounds and calibration fits' input judgments, and it reads the analysis's derived/exclusions.json (independent_recompute_b5.py:4-6,544-561). Block 6 recomputes kept units with new code: the block-6 rule plus the S-9 desk exclusion (design §0 item 2). No step in the map independently checks that path, yet several redundancy claims (B6-07, B6-09) assume S-13 catches wrong numbers there.

The design explicitly rejected analysing a copy of the sessions elsewhere, because bindings name the original absolute roots (design §4.1 Not chosen: whole_window.py:6553, analysis_engine/inputs.py:895, mint_floor_artifact.py:1130). The MacBook Air plan does not address this.

The proposed base 1706257c predates PR #573's block-6 corrections on the BYTES line (desk_restore.py, restore_run_to_scratch.py, 903b5a2f, db9e8ab3). Design §15.3's 3-conflict recipe was trial-merged on 2026-10-21/22, before those landed.

The #416 evidence is misread. Rounds 4-6 found real defects: a clock-step blind spot, 19->23 printed rows, a HIGH. '25 real archives byte-identical' was a regression replay, not proof that a round found nothing (git log 6b54a51d, 7a3b585d, 028f8c50).
ED-RULING's L9 substitution still kept one full-size cached test_dry_run (ED-RULING.md:45), so the precedent cited for B6-07 is overstated.

The in-place APFS restore and recompress per unit is not safe under the proposed concurrent DAG. A r3 is shared by G r2 and G r3, and the recompute shares the restore cycle. A reference-counted unit restore is needed.

cadence.lens: CADENCE SKEPTIC: challenge every KEEP (does it protect a printed number; is there a cheaper form), check that proposals go far enough, list missed parallelism and missed steps

judgments.reason: One executing review is worth keeping. It is the only check of how the registration is read (pairing, counting, the word 'replicated'). The independent recompute cannot see these errors because it is built from the same text. Keeping it as a separate round from the two cold passes (B6-09) does not hold up. The auditor's evidence that executing review catches defects partly comes from cold passes: db9e8ab3 is titled 'Block-6 code: cold-pass corrections' and its body credits 'Fable and Opus cold passes (both ADMIT-WITH-CORRECTIONS)', not a separate executing review. The design consult findings F1-F3 (design :1633-1637) were a consult on the design, not a code review. The review and the cold passes are the same kind of check: a non-author model that runs the code. Cheaper form with the same protection: one round of two parallel executing passes, Fable and Opus. Either one counts as REG §13's 'independently reviewed by executing them' (REG :1186). Run it once the driver builds, alongside the first per-session blind run, with at most one delta round. A defect found after the blind run costs a rerun of only the affected units, because outputs are content-addressed. That is hours on the analysis host, against a serial review-then-cold-pass sequence of days (#416 pattern). This needs the same §17 entry as B6-09, since §13 lists the review and the cold passes as separate items.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: As mapped, the work runs in this order: executing review, then fix, then blind run, then two cold passes, then delta round(s). That is three model reviews of the same code in at least two serial rounds. In #416, the extra rounds after round 3 changed no real archive output (6b54a51d, 7a3b585d, 028f8c50, 49884a10: '25 real archives: 0 stops, byte-identical'). The cost is days of wall time and no printed number is protected beyond what one parallel round plus the S-13 recompute gives.
evidence_refs: git log -1 db9e8ab3 (subject 'Block-6 code: cold-pass corrections (PR #573 ...)'; body 'Fable and Opus cold passes (both ADMIT-WITH-CORRECTIONS)')
origin/lane/2026-10-22-b6-analysis-design:docs/design/b6_analysis_additions.md:1167-1168 (§15 step 5: executing review, then two cold passes, serial)

judgments.reason: LIGHTEN is right but does not go far enough. Fold B6-08 into this round, as above, so the whole block-6 code check is one parallel round of two executing passes with at most one delta round. One correction to the evidence: rounds 4-7 of #416 changed no real archive output, but they were not empty. Round 6 (028f8c50) was an Opus HIGH: a BYTES smoke would otherwise have stopped and held its t0. That is an operational defect, not a number defect, so the cap still stands, but the claim should be 'changed no number', not 'caught nothing'. Moving the passes to 'before the release record, concurrent with the blind run' matches ED-RULING item 3 for L9 (:48-49). Under REG :1186 it needs the §17 entry the auditor names.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: If the cold passes stay 'at merge, before S-14 and the blind run', the whole real-data phase waits on serial cold-pass rounds. The #416 audit took about 2 days of rounds (bc588a96 2026-10-24 20:07 to 49884a10 2026-10-25 01:01 for rounds 3-7 alone).
