judgments.reason:
The transfer is worth keeping. A hash-verified copy protects provenance (the bytes analysed are the bytes harvested). It also ends the problem of in-place restores rewriting 'the only physical copy' (design :300-303, :1187-1188), a real data-integrity protection. Cheaper and safer form: AUTOMATE the verification with the desk's existing compression-row and full-inventory after-check (design §4.1 item 3, consult F4) instead of a new sha256 script. Three conditions are missing:
(1) Absolute-path parity. The design rejected 'a copy of the sessions elsewhere' because plans and bindings name the sessions' original absolute roots (whole_window.py:6553, analysis_engine/inputs.py:895, mint_floor_artifact.py:1130; design :289-293, :1466). The Air must reproduce /Users/edr/night-b6/... exactly, or L9 refuses every unit. Nobody has checked this.
(2) Timing on the Mac. The copy-out is heavy disk I/O. It must not overlap block 5's blind dry run on the Mac, whose 120 s wall deadline fires under contention (L9-2.md:149-163). Schedule it before that dry run starts or in a gap with nothing else running, as well as outside any [QUIET-MAC] session.
(3) Agents on the Air. The Air has the Codex CLI. An agent session with filesystem read on the Air is the same custody exposure the plan warns of (plan :52-54). Item 78 shows a leftover Codex daemon can persist unnoticed. Run the analysis under a separate macOS user or volume that no agent session can read, and exclude it from iCloud.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode:
Possible failures:
- Copy to /Users/<other>/... on the Air: every unit refuses at step 0 or at the bindings, and a full Air run is lost.
- Copy during block 5's dry run: the Mac's 9b refit hits the 120 s deadline, and block 5's dry run takes a tooling refusal and a fresh custody root.
- A Codex session on the Air reads the restricted outputs: blinding is broken.

judgments.reason: This is a registered blinding protection, and it is one of the KEEP items under Ed's principle: block-6 values read first would unblind block 5 'in all but name' (REG :1151-1152). There is no cheaper form. The auditor correctly narrows it to a dependency of the cross-block phase and the release only (B6-17/18). Everything per session is allowed blind by REG §12.2 (:1140-1144).
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: If dropped, block-6 GAMMA outcomes become visible before block 5's analysis is frozen, and a choice about block 5 could then be shaped by its replication.

judgments.reason:
Moving it earlier is right. Two checks are missing before an Air run is committed:
(a) A cheap structure-only timing probe on the Air: one real detection refit at the planned pool size, wall seconds only. REG :1132 allows non-phase timing as structure. The cadence plan itself says real-data analysis off the Mac 'should wait for item 2.4 [governed deadline fix], or use a fast dedicated machine' (plan :47-48, :60-61). A fanless Air (INFERRED) is neither. ED-RULING (c) was argued for 'the quiet Mac, where the same calibration completed at harvest' (:63). The synthetic refusal fired at about 5.6x the isolated fit cost (L9-2.md:150-152).
(b) Restore each session once. The Mac copy stays canonical, so the Air copy can stay restored for the whole run instead of 15 restore/recompress cycles (design :1590-1593 'restores and re-compresses ... 15 session cycles'). That makes 10 cycles, A r3 is not restored three times, and the recompress step is skipped. On-disk cost is roughly the compressed size (design :1592-1597, 7.5x, INFERRED about 50 GiB for 10 sessions).
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: The run starts on an Air that throttles under a 4-8 worker pool. Detection deadlines fire in several units, giving tooling refusals, fresh custody roots and reruns. The determinism rerun (B6-15) can also differ from the first run, and that is caught only after hours of compute.

judgments.reason: The rerun's determinism value does not depend on when it runs, given the same bytes and the same pin. One condition the proposal must state: the release record binds the blind outputs' digests before anything is opened. That keeps the protection the post-release rerun gave against outputs being altered after they are seen. Run the second pass serially on the same host, not concurrently with the first. Running both at once on a fanless Air invites deadline firings that show up as false determinism failures (release_digest_differs_from_dry_run, dry_run.py:176-180).
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: If the two runs are concurrent on one Air, contention fires the 120 s deadline in one run only. The digests then differ and a spurious determinism failure blocks release until a rerun.

judgments.reason: PARALLELIZE is right, but one detail weakens independence. The auditor proposes that the recompute share the driver's APFS restore 'instead of adding a zstd dependency'. The design explicitly keeps desk_compress.read_bytes as the recompute's reader (design :295-296, :1191-1195; §23 'the analysis does not use it, and the recompute does'), so the two programs reach the raw plists by different paths. Sharing the restore makes the input path common to both. A restore defect, for example a reader seeing other than the harvested bytes, would then hit both programs and pass S-13. Keep read_bytes (or an equivalent stdlib-plus-zstd stream) in the recompute.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: A restore or after-check defect delivers altered plain bytes. The driver and the recompute both integrate them, agree within 1 mJ, and S-13 passes on the wrong input.

judgments.reason: Agree on filling it now. The proposal stops short on one point: S-15's executing refuter and the refuter for the §13/S-14/custody §17 entry can be one refuter run over both entries. Both are blind §17 entries due before the blind run, and they review adjacent text. That saves a seat round.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: Two serial refuter seats for two §17 entries drafted the same day add one round with no added protection.

judgments.reason: Agree. Do not schedule the 'optional cached full-size diagnostic on the Air': the Air is the real-data host, and a diagnostic competes with it for CPU and deadline margin. Fixtures with full member counts and short traces (kept_units.py:163-164 requires the counts, not the trace lengths), plus serial==parallel and plain==compressed digest tests, give the coverage.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: A diagnostic synthetic run on the Air overlaps the real blind run and raises deadline-firing risk on real units.

judgments.reason: The scout's own text says it added the release cold gate on its operator's instruction, while noting REG says there is none (scout :202-206). Ed's 2026-10-27 principle and REG :1164-1166 both point to cutting it. Generating the record automatically is right.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: An extra review round on the post-block-5-release critical path that repeats the cold passes and S-13.

missed_items: Absolute-root bindings block an off-Mac copy unless paths are identical. The design rejected 'a copy of the sessions elsewhere' because whole_window.py:6553, analysis_engine/inputs.py:895 and mint_floor_artifact.py:1130 name the original absolute roots (design :289-293, :1466). The Air plan must reproduce /Users/edr/night-b6/... exactly (and any bound measurement-checkout path), or amend the design. Check this first; it is unverified.

The cadence plan's own caveat is not cited. Real-data analysis off the Mac 'should wait for item 2.4 [the governed deadline fix], or use a fast dedicated machine' (plan :47-48, :60-61). Before committing the Air, add a structure-only timing probe there: one real refit at the planned pool size, wall seconds only (REG :1132). Or decide explicitly whether the block-6 blind run waits for 2.4. If 2.4 lands after block 5's first dry run (plan :100), it changes L9 and moves S-14, which could force a full block-6 rerun.

The copy-out conflicts with block 5's dry run on the Mac. ED-RULING 6a gives the Mac to block 5's dry run first (:70-74), and that run keeps the 120 s deadline (:63). The bulk copy must run before it or in a separate gap, not during it.

Custody on the Air is not addressed. The Air has the Codex CLI, so an agent session there could read restricted outputs. Use a separate macOS user or volume closed to agent sessions, with no iCloud sync, and run a check for leftover daemons like the one in item 78 (RUN_STATE.md:284).
Restore on the Air once per session and leave the copy restored: 10 cycles instead of 15, with no per-unit recompress (design :1590-1597). The Mac copy is the canonical one.
Use one executing refuter for both blind §17 entries (S-15 and the §13/S-14/custody/rerun-ordering entry) instead of two serial refuter seats.

The recompute must keep desk_compress.read_bytes as its reader (design :1191-1195), not share the driver's APFS restore. Otherwise the input path is common to both programs and S-13 cannot catch a restore defect.

Some evidence is mis-cited. db9e8ab3 (#573) records cold-pass corrections, not an executing review. #416 round 6 (028f8c50) caught an Opus HIGH, an operational defect that changed no number. The cap on rounds still holds, but the stated rationale should be 'changed no number'.

Moving the release rerun earlier (B6-15) needs the release record to bind the blind outputs' digests before opening. This keeps the protection the post-release rerun gave against changes to outputs after they are seen.

Ed's request was to keep as much as possible in the cloud. The map does this for all code and judgment work. The real-data runs (B6-13/14/15/17) cannot go to the cloud under the design's custody rule (design :1182, 'blinded data never goes to a cloud seat'), so the Air or the Mac is the only option. State this so the cloud preference does not reopen the question.

map.segment: BYTES: registration to released result (pass-1 status, known-bytes test, blinded stage, stage-1 fit, commitment, held-out agreement, stage-2 release, coverage, Bonferroni, pass 2, end date 2026-11-02)
map.summary:
All paths are relative to the scratchpad (/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-edr-code-CapstoneProject-JouleWise/48676f58-1e29-402b-8dfd-f8c6899f3ebf/scratchpad/). Note: the known-bytes reading-rule draft is in jw/ (main), not in wt/bytes/.

WHERE BYTES STANDS (RUN_STATE items 71-78)
- s1-p1 collected zero data. All 143 members refused on a missing plan_tree.sha256, and the smoke did not catch it (jw/docs/process_traces/2026-10-25-magistrate-8b6b2b12/RECORD.md:5-10). The packs are fixed now.
- s2-p1, s3-p1 and s4-p1 count, 125/125 each (items 72, 73, 75).
- s5-p1 (70B) counts but its decode cell is unavailable: 2 of 10 quads kept, because of thermal hits in the post-request tail (item 76). A round-2 council is working on it.
- s6-p1 (122B) was aborted by a leftover Codex daemon. It kept 10/10 repeats and quads b01-b04, with no thermal loss. A retry is pending (item 78).
- Pass-2 packs are still `draft`: estimator versions are null and they have no sizing rows (wt/bytes/configs/b6/packs/bytes-s*-p2/registration.json; sizing_b5.json holds only p1 rows).
- The pinned module matches the registered digest: `shasum` of joulewise/bytes_analysis.py = 18582818…, as registered.

WHAT THE CODE FORCES (read, not executed)
- H1 cannot exist without s1. `freeze_lines` raises unless there are exactly 3 fit models (wt/bytes/joulewise/bytes_analysis.py:89-90).
- The active-or-resident answer prints `missing` without 122B (bytes_analysis.py:1564-1576).
- **Probable gap.** If a sub-pack never counts in either pass, that model has no records at all. Stage 2 then raises "held-out analysis requires all manifest model records" (bytes_analysis.py:1530-1531), and stage 1 refuses on fewer than 3 fit points.
  - Registered D9(b) says H2 should still fit on the remaining models.
  - Only withheld-file loss and a never-collected second pass are tested (tests/test_bytes_agreement.py:1924-1960). A never-counted sub-pack is not.
  - INFERRED: needs one executed synthetic check now.

THE DATE
- 2026-11-02T00:00-08:00 is the last-t0 cutoff in every pack (registration.json `stopping.end_t0_before`; registration §5 line 105). No t0 is allowed in the DST window, 10-31 16:30 PDT to 11-01 02:00 PST (item 69(e)).
- About 132 h remain from about 13:00 PDT on 10-27.
- Measured cycle is about 9.5-10.5 h t0-to-t0: chain 313-388 min, harvest 88-101 min, desk about 95 min, plus arm (items 75, 76; 7326d37c RECORD:6).
- Still needed: 2 pass-1 retries plus 6 pass-2 sessions, about 80 h with zero losses. At the observed 2-in-6 attempt loss rate, about 110-120 h, plus block-5 dry-run Mac time (Ed's rule 6a gives it precedence) and the DST blackout.
- So full pass 2 is marginal. s1-p2 is last in the loop's base order (configs/b6/loop_bytes.json), so the fit set's backup sits in the riskiest slot.

IS THE s1 FIT SET STRICTLY NEEDED IN PASS 1? No.
- Each pack is 1/1, and D9(a) makes a surviving single pass the model's point (registration §7 line 271).
- R5 puts stage 1 "after collection closes" (wt/bytes/docs/design/bytes_pack_design.md:105-110), so s1 data from pass 2 serve equally.
- But s1 must count in some pass, or H1 is void. Its only backup is the last pass-2 slot.
- So run s1-p1 next, before the s6-p1 retry. s6's backup, s6-p2, is first in pass-2 order.

PASS 2 BUYS REPRODUCIBILITY, NOT PRECISION
- The two-pass half-width is the mean of the passes' (h+B), with h not pooled, "because B dominates and does not shrink with passes" (§7 line 271).
- Scientifically essential remaining sessions: s1 (fit set), s6 (third MoE model) and s5-p2 (70B's only possible point). s2-s4 pass 2 are replication.

FASTEST DEFENSIBLE ROUTE TO A BYTES RESULT
1. Order the Mac: s1-p1, then s6-p1, then pass 2. Flip pass 2 to registered today by a mechanical generator plus one executing check (not a two-seat cold gate). Pre-declare, blind, a priority order for use if the date binds: s5-p2 first, then s1/s6 backups, then s2-s4.
2. Move all agent and Codex use off the measurement Mac onto the MacBook Air. Two windows were lost to agents on the Mac (items 67, 78).
3. In parallel, without touching the Mac:
   - fix the no-records gap and the partial-fit-set refusal in non-governed CLI code (scripts/bytes_analyze.py:72);
   - run the blinded stage and the twin on each session's export as it lands, on the Air;
   - time the re-reduction path and the 120 s deadline on the Air using non-claim H/BY-H2 archives;
   - add a per-session process pool in the CLI;
   - build the known-bytes v2 probe, chain extension and Δ code in the cloud;
   - bind the known-bytes reading rule now from the reconciler revision (option a).
4. Decouple the known-bytes measurement from stage 1. The reading rule must bind before stage 1; the hour of measurement does not have to come first. This needs a dated, blind §19 amendment.
5. At close: blinded agreement (minutes), stage-1 fit on the Air, commit, held-out agreement (export-only, cheap), stage-2 release, stage 2. With the code rehearsed, plausibly 1-2 days after the last desk (INFERRED: stage-1/2 wall time is unmeasured).
- The registered science gates stay: estimators fixed; blinding with withheld held-out rows; the stage-1 commitment before held-out unblinding; one independent twin; coverage and Bonferroni already fixed.
- No results-level cold gate is registered for BYTES. None should be added.

CEREMONY
- A third cold pass on the known-bytes rule: two passes plus a reconciler are done.
- Known-bytes timing as a hard gate before stage 1.
- A two-seat cold gate plus a measurement-Mac whole-suite run for a pass-2 registration that mirrors pass 1.
- Smoking pass-2 packs: §19 smokes only "each sub-pack's first session", and the smoke missed the one config defect so far.
- The controller's sidecar refusal (it cost s1-p1, per the 8b6b2b12 pruning tally) is ceremony, but it has no remaining cost now that the sidecars exist.

NOT CEREMONY
- The #416 audits caught a number-changing defect: the NEG-8 reference span was the `measured_run` stage, 6.5-6.9x the request, so B was too small (item 69).
- FIX-416-A found a 28 s meter dropout costing −184.96 J (FIX416A-REPORT.md:66).
- The twin surfaced the ten D1-D10 method differences (bytes_pack_design.md:276-302).
- But the twin did not catch the span defect (19 campaigns showed 0 above the bar before the audit; item 68), so the independence it provides is not complete.

WHAT 2026-11-02 FORCES
- A pass-2 registration flip within about 20 h.
- s1-p1 next.
- A time-boxed 70B thermal ruling before s5-p2.
- Mac time for the block-5 dry run fitted into gaps, or the dry run moved to the Air.
- Either a blind decision that pass 2 is best-effort with a pre-declared priority, or a prospective blind extension of the end date. Ed's ruling 6a explicitly allows the extension (jw/docs/process_traces/2026-10-27-l9-restart/ED-RULING.md:70-74).

steps.name: Zero-yield detection during a session

Implement only if it is a small, tested change to the loop; otherwise defer to after BYTES, because mid-collection loop changes carry their own risk.

steps.name: Retry order: s1-p1 before the s6-p1 retry

Reason: s6's backup (s6-p2) is first in pass-2 order, but s1's backup (s1-p2) is last (configs/b6/loop_bytes.json base_order), the slot most exposed to the 11-02 cutoff. s1-p1 is not strictly required (D9(a), 1/1 packs, stage 1 after collection closes per R5), but s1 must count in at least one pass, and running it now gives it two remaining chances.

parallelism: While the Mac collects (now to 11-02), all off-Mac: C9 pass-2 flip (cloud), C11 known-bytes rule binding (lead), C12 known-bytes v2 probe, chain extension and Δ code (cloud), A1 missing-sub-pack synthetic check (cloud), A2 CLI fix plus per-session blinded runs (Air), A4 re-reduction timing on H/BY-H2 (Air), the A5 process-pool change with its byte-identity test (cloud), and C8 council round 2 (cloud). Per-session pipeline: when a desk ends, rsync the compressed archive to the Air during the desk window (C5). The Air then runs the analysis blinded stage and the twin on that session (A2) while the Mac arms the next session. Evidence: bytes_analyze.py:68-85 (CSV-only blinded stage); bytes_analysis.py:991 (reads .zst through compression.jsonl).

Session-level fan-out in stage 1 and stage 2: load_records iterates sessions serially (bytes_analysis.py:1117-1158), and each archive_records call owns its own physics_cache (bytes_analysis.py:965). A process pool over sessions in scripts/bytes_analyze.py (not digest-pinned; only bytes_analysis.py is, registration §11 line 361) gives up to 12-way independence, bounded by the Air's cores.

Analysis and twin always run concurrently at each stage (blinded, fit, held-out blinded, stage 2): they share no code or state (bytes_twin.py:10). The twin reads the export plus meter streams only (bytes_twin.py:1044-1058), so it finishes long before the analysis's re-reduction.
At close: the known-bytes measured hour on the Mac (needs quiet) runs concurrently with stage 1 on the Air (a different machine, so the Mac's quiet is unaffected), once C13's decoupling is amended.

Block-5 dry run versus BYTES: if A4 shows the Air reproduces the calibration-leaf timing (24 s isolated on the Mac), the block-5 dry run could run on the Air concurrently with BYTES sessions instead of pre-empting the Mac under ED-RULING 6a. map.where_to_run:
Measurement Mac (M3 Max) does only what physically requires it:
- the session chains;
- harvest and desk (custody);
- the stage-1 and stage-2 key releases (keys live at /Users/edr/night-b6/loop-bytes/packs/bytes/blinding), done outside sessions;
- the known-bytes knee scan and measured hour.
No interactive agents, no Codex app or CLI, no auto-updaters on it (items 67, 78).

MacBook Air (24 GB):
- Every step that reads real BYTES files: blinded stage and twin per session (A2/A3), the stage-1 fit (A5), DC/rest agreements (A6), the held-out blinded agreement (A8), stage 2 (A11), the comparer.
- The A4 timing rehearsal on non-claim H/BY-H2 archives.
- The whole-suite run that §19 asks of "the laptop" (macOS arm64 without disturbing the measurement Mac).
- All interactive Codex CLI and Claude Code work, moved off the Mac.
Why the Air rather than cloud:
- The raw archives hold unblinded powermetrics and meter streams; blinding is applied only to export columns (registration §11, Addendum 3 item 4). So they belong on Ed's machines, not agent VMs.
- Compressed archives are a few GiB per session (INFERRED from the block-6 figure of about 1.8 GiB in item 70(d)) and fit easily.
- The Air is Apple Silicon like the Mac, so the macOS-only suite and readers behave the same.
- Caveat: the Air's chip and fanless throttling against the 120 s deadline are unmeasured; A4 measures them first.

Cloud (Claude 4 vCPU/15 GB; Codex 5 vCPU/17 GB): code and synthetic work only.
- The pass-2 registration flip and its executing check (C9).
- Known-bytes v2 probe, chain extension and Δ code (C12).
- The A1 missing-sub-pack campaign; the A5 pool with its byte-identity test.
- The thermal council (C8); the known-bytes rule worked example.
- Any coverage rerun, if A9 triggers.
- The existing synthetic agreement suite: test_bytes_analysis 5049 s (FIX416A-REPORT.md:208).
Never real BYTES archives or exports (INFERRED policy; the registration's blinding relies on code discipline over raw files).
map.amendment_rules:
QUOTED FROM THE GOVERNING TEXTS

Registration status and precedence:
- Status: "where the two differ, the ruling's later addendum is what this text writes down" (wt/bytes/docs/registrations/bytes_pack_v1.md:3).
- Authority order: BAT-2, then Addendum 9, then 8…1, then R1-R8, then the block-6 registration and block 5's arithmetic, "which wins on arithmetic" (line 14).
- Registration time: "The commit that flips the six pass-1 packs to `registered` is the registration time, and it must precede the first BYTES session's start" (line 3).

Specific rules:
- One-pass fallback: "(Addendum 7 D9, decided before any data so that it is not a choice made after seeing them)" (line 271).
- Coverage: "If HC3's plain-95% coverage is below 0.93 in any world, the method is not changed here; the lead rules (Addendum 4 item 5)" (line 327).
- Held-out agreement: "If the attributed difference is a defect in `joulewise/bytes_analysis.py` … the fix restores the registered arithmetic and does not change it … The stage-1 commitment is not withdrawn, re-signed or edited" (line 362).
- Estimators: "If `joulewise/bytes_analysis.py` changes after the stage-1 commitment …, this version is not re-registered: every stage-2 record prints the evaluating digest beside the committed one under the flag `bytes.module_changed_after_commitment`"; "Pass-2 versions remain null pending their agreement; pass-2 packs remain draft until their registration gate" (line 384).
- Stopping: "a pack stops after its one counting session, or when no t0 can start before **2026-11-02T00:00:00-08:00**" (line 105).
- Order before collection: "every pre-collection slot of §18 filled …; the whole test suite run on the laptop …; this registration's cold gate (R8 item 8) …; its commit before the first t0; then, for each sub-pack's first session, the smoke by fingerprint" (line 450).
- Known-bytes test: "runs **after pass-1 collection and before stage-1 unblinding** … It changes no number collected in a pass-1 session" (line 452; P0 ruling 9, BYTES-P0-RULINGS.md:13).

Known-bytes reading rule: "It binds once a cold pass (Fable 5.1 and Opus 5.5, blind, executing) admits it, and it must bind **before the test runs**" (jw/docs/registrations/bytes_known_bytes_reading_rule_DRAFT.md:7-8).

Ed's ruling 6a: "BYTES's registered end (no t0 after 2026-11-02 00:00 PDT) still binds. If the dry run would push s1-p1 past it, the lead tells Ed before holding the loop, so he can choose between the fit set and the date, or amend the end date prospectively while BYTES is still blinded" (jw/docs/process_traces/2026-10-27-l9-restart/ED-RULING.md:70-74).

Ed's standing principle (2026-10-27, as relayed in the task): "the only real rule is good science at a speedy cadence".

HOW THESE RULES SORT THE PROPOSALS ABOVE

Changes to HOW a number is computed are allowed if made blind and dated, with registered numbers unchanged. These need no registration amendment because they touch only non-pinned code (scripts/bytes_analyze.py is not hash-bound; bytes_analysis.py at 18582818… is):
- A2: the partial-fit-set blinded run.
- A5/A11: the session pool.
- A1: census placeholders implementing registered D9(b).
- C5: the rsync to the Air.

Changes to WHAT is collected, excluded or ordered, or to a registered gate, need a blind, dated registration amendment:
- C8: the s5-p1 thermal alternative and the s5-p2 procedure.
- C9: the pass-2 gate form and the suite location.
- C10: the pass-2 priority or scope, or a date extension (Ed).
- C13: the known-bytes ordering.

Lead rulings within the existing text:
- C1: agent tooling off the Mac.
- C3: no smoke for pass-2 non-first sessions, per §19's own wording.
- C7: retry order within pass 1.
- C11: binding the reconciled known-bytes rule.

Code-level:
- Any change to bytes_analysis.py before the commitment re-binds the pass-1 estimator versions in the six pack registrations.
- Any change after the commitment follows the §11 post-agreement-fix route.
open_questions: Why 2026-11-02? R5 mentions 'the 2026-11-01 date' (bytes_pack_design.md:105-106) without saying what it is. If no external deadline depends on it, a prospective blind extension (ED-RULING 6a) removes the risk to pass 2 at no scientific cost. Ed to decide.

Does the analysis refuse stage 1 or stage 2 outright when a sub-pack never counts in either pass? Read from code (bytes_analysis.py:89-90, 1342, 1530-1531), not executed. Needs one synthetic campaign with s1 or s6 absent from both passes, through the CLI and the twin (A1).

What state is seat BY-KB's chain extension in (P0 ruling 9 says the native chain cannot run the known-bytes probe)? Does any v2 probe code exist? Only the v1 probe was found on the bytes branch (scripts/bytes_stream_test.py:36).
How long do the stage-1 and stage-2 re-reductions take per bundle, and does the 120 s calibration deadline fire on the MacBook Air? Unmeasured. Also unknown: the Air's chip, core count and free disk.
Does the BYTES loop smoke pass-2 packs, given §19 says 'for each sub-pack's first session'?

Policy: may blinded BYTES export CSVs, or raw archives (which carry unblinded powermetrics and meter streams), be processed in cloud agent VMs? This map assumes no and puts all real-file analysis on the Air.
Known-bytes reading rule, open item 'Fable 1': adopt option (a) (disclose ε_flip, recommended by the reconciler), (b) a new dispatch-fixed kernel, or (c) a leverage factor? Lead to decide.
Pass 2: should Ed pre-declare, blind, either a priority order (s5-p2 first; s2-s4 pass 2 as replication last) or a reduced scope, given pass 2 adds reproducibility but no precision (§7 line 271)?

The cadence plan (analysis_cadence_plan.md:77) says BYTES stage 1 runs 'as soon as the fit set exists'. R5 says after collection closes (bytes_pack_design.md:107-110). Committing early would freeze one-pass fit points, which is a WHAT change needing a registration amendment. Confirm R5 governs.
Is the council's 70B thermal ruling for s5-p2 achievable before about 10-30? Without it, s5-p2 (70B's only possible point, since its pass-1 cell is unavailable) may miss the cutoff.

science.segment: BYTES: registration to released result (pass-1 status, known-bytes test, blinded stage, stage-1 fit, commitment, held-out agreement, stage-2 release, coverage, Bonferroni, pass 2, end date 2026-11-02)

judgments.reason: The pool is a sound idea, but the check offered as its safeguard (byte-identity against the serial run on one synthetic campaign) does not cover the failure the pool makes more likely. Stage 1 re-reduces every fit bundle through _rederive_summary_for_authenticated_fiducial_bound (bytes_analysis.py:596-599). That calibration carries a frozen 120 s wall deadline (powermetrics_fiducial.py:91-94, 545-551), and the code itself marks a firing non-reproducible (powermetrics_fiducial.py:1531-1541). In archive_records, a non-succeeded re-reduction raises AnalysisError (bytes_analysis.py:1001-1002). AnalysisError subclasses ValueError (bytes_analysis.py:46), so the broad except at bytes_analysis.py:1016-1017 catches it and turns the row into status=unusable. The unit is dropped quietly, with no refusal. Before the commitment, real-data agreement covers only export-based blinded rails, which involve no re-reduction (registration:348, 359, 380). The twin uses the exported phase_decode_j and never re-reduces (bytes_twin.py:1298, 1321). So nothing compares the analysis's re-reduced fit-set unit counts before predictions.json is frozen. Running 4+ processes on a fanless Air raises per-process wall time exactly where the deadline lives. Synthetic campaigns use labelled timing fixtures (bytes_analysis.py:603-608), so a synthetic byte-identity test never exercises the deadline. INFERRED, not executed: that a deadline firing produces summary status != succeeded. Two further gaps. (1) A pool that re-implements session enumeration may drop the sidecar-census path (bytes_analysis.py:1106-1109), so a vanished CSV disappears silently instead of being flagged. (2) where_to_run puts every session's raw archive on the Air, which C1 also makes the home of all interactive agents. The raw powermetrics and meter streams are unblinded, and stage 1 reads every session's archive for references. Agents would then sit next to unblinded held-out energies before the commitment, which contradicts the map's own reason for keeping raw files out of cloud seats.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: The stage-1 pool runs on the Air under load. The calibration's 120 s wall deadline fires on a few fit-set bundles. Each one becomes status=unusable through the ValueError catch, so a 1.7B or 4B cell loses units: its m and h shift, or it drops below minimum. The changed fit points are committed into predictions.json. The twin, working from export values, keeps those units, but the n difference shows only in the stage-2 comparer, after the commitment. The registered result then rests on a host-load-dependent fit point and has to go through the post-agreement-fix route.

judgments.reason: Unlike stage 1, stage 2 does have an executed cross-check that catches the pool-induced silent unit drop. The twin's stage-2 comparison requires exact matches on n, k, labels and refusals (registration:367-368), and the twin keeps every exported unit (bytes_twin.py:1298). A deadline drop in the analysis would therefore show as an above-bar difference that must be attributed before the result stands (registration:378). No results-level cold gate is registered, and leaving one out removes nothing the registration requires. The proposal is safe only if the comparer table is treated as blocking (any exact-field mismatch is attributed, and the stage is rerun serially if it is host-caused), not as a read-only report. The pool must also reuse the module's own session enumeration (bytes_analysis.py:1106-1112). Residual risk not created by this proposal: the twin shares spec misreadings with the analysis (the span defect, RUN_STATE item 68-69), so the 'one reviewer' should check the stage-2 outputs against registration text, not only the counts.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: Only if the comparer is not blocking: a held-out unit dropped by a deadline firing differs in n from the twin, the reviewer reads it as tooling noise, and a held-out point prints with the wrong kept-unit count.

judgments.reason: The map leaves 'before the commitment' as optional ('ideally'). Given the A5 finding, it should be mandatory. The DC-input/rest agreement on released fit configurations is the only real-data executed comparison that can see a re-reduction-driven difference in the fit set's kept units before predictions.json is frozen. The registration says only 'after each release' (registration:380), so placing it between the fit release and the commit is within the text. Add one non-governed CLI guard: before writing predictions, compare the analysis's kept-unit set for each fit cell with the harvest acceptance's kept set, and refuse on any re-reduction-caused 'unusable' row.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: If A6 runs after the commitment, a fit-set unit count changed by a host deadline (A5) is first seen after predictions are frozen, which forces the post-agreement-fix route and a labelled alternative.

judgments.reason: A timing rehearsal on non-claim H/BY-H2 archives touches no keys and no claim data. It only turns an unknown into a measurement, so I cannot build a path from it to a wrong number. Caveat: a rehearsal with no firing does not show that the real run will have none, especially under the A5 pool. A4 should also measure with the intended pool width and record headroom against 120 s per calibration, not just whether the deadline fired.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: None from A4 itself. The risk is reading 'no firing on a serial sample' as permission to run a parallel pool (see A5).

judgments.reason: The diagnosis is verified. In the blinded branch the CLI calls frozen_predictions unconditionally (bytes_analyze.py:72). freeze_lines raises unless there are exactly 3 points (bytes_analysis.py:89-90). frozen_predictions calls it for every non-empty, all-available group (bytes_analysis.py:1506-1510). The fit set is 1.7B, 4B and 8B (roster.json:8, 22, 36, with role fit at :16, :30, :44), so per-session runs refuse until s1 counts. Two gaps remain. (1) The same blinded branch, with --stage1-commit, is the registered post-commit held-out blinded agreement (bytes_analyze.py:68-78; registration:362). A patch that sets frozen to None or skips evaluate with fewer than 3 fit points could change that path. The proposal adds no regression run, but the CLI is half of the agreeing pair (registration:367), so the synthetic agreement suite (test_bytes_agreement) must rerun after the patch. (2) Per-session blinded outputs (fit-set rails, ratios visible to about ±6%, NEG-8 drift) would be visible while pass-2 scope, the end date and the s5-p2 procedure (C8, C10) are still undecided. A scope cut chosen after viewing blinded per-pass results is data-dependent stopping. Either decide C8 and C10 first, or limit what decision-makers see to comparer counts only. Also, the blinded path never checks acceptance.counting (compare bytes_analysis.py:940-941 with 1123-1158). An export left by a non-counting attempt (s1-p1 zero-yield, s6-p1 aborted) in the export directory could be ingested if its session_id is in the manifest. INFERRED: depends on whether the desk exports non-counting attempts.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: A CLI patch for the partial fit set breaks the post-commit held-out blinded branch, and no suite rerun catches it before real use. Separately, the lead sees per-session blinded fit-set rails and NEG-8 before ruling C10(ii), and a reviewer can rightly call the pass-2 cut outcome-informed.

judgments.reason: The gap is real by reading. evaluate requires the subset to equal 3 + H1_checks/3 and raises otherwise (bytes_analysis.py:1530-1531). Census placeholders exist only for sessions whose withheld sidecar exists (bytes_analysis.py:793-805, 1106-1109). The only executed missing-data case covers withheld files missing and an uncollected pass 2 with pass 1 present (test_bytes_agreement.py:1924-1960). A sub-pack absent from both passes is not tested, yet registered D9(b) requires H2 to fit on the remaining models (registration:271). Running the check now only adds protection. A CLI-only placeholder fix, plus agreement with an independently written twin, gives the executed check. Two corrections. (a) Step 4, 'if bytes_analysis.py must change, rebind before stage 1', is not a lead ruling. It changes the registered estimator version after pass-1 sessions ran under 18582818 (registration:384). It needs a blind, dated amendment, the full synthetic agreement rerun, and a coverage rerun if the change touches cell or interval code. (b) Placeholders are also needed at stage 1, where a missing s1 must give lines=None (bytes_analysis.py:1510) rather than a 1-point freeze_lines refusal.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: Not from running the check. If step 4 were done as a lead ruling, the estimator module would change after collection without the agreement and coverage reruns, and the printed numbers would come from code that is not the registered version, without the disclosure §13 requires.

judgments.reason: The proposal lets the known-bytes measurement run after stage 1, or even after stage 2 ('result is added after as a dated record'). The ordering 'after pass-1 collection and before stage-1 unblinding' (registration:452; P0 ruling 9) protects more than the reading rule does. The rule fixes the classes, but the measurement keeps real researcher freedom: knee refusal ('knee not found'), meter-gap UNDETERMINED, stack-check mismatch, and whether and when to rerun. Exercised after the fit lines or H1 words are known, those choices become outcome-informed. The binding reading-rule draft already handles a late test: if the test is not run before stage-1 unblinding, it prints 'Known-bytes check: not measured' (reading rule DRAFT:167). Filling the result in later contradicts the rule's own text. The saving is about 1.5-2 h. A cheaper option keeps the protection: run the measured hour on the Mac at the same time as the stage-1 computation on the Air, keep stage-1 outputs unopened until the known-bytes receipt and class are committed, and declare that a missed test stays 'not measured' with no post-hoc fill.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: Stage 2 shows rails H1 words against the bytes hypothesis. The team then runs the known-bytes test, sees a knee refusal, reruns it, and gets NOT RESOLVED, which now reads as an explanation for the result. A reviewer cannot tell whether the caveat was shaped by the result.

judgments.reason: The 'two passes plus reconciler done' claim does not hold. The rule binds only once 'a cold pass (Fable 5.1 and Opus 5.5, blind, executing) admits it' (DRAFT:7-8). Both passes admitted the earlier text only with corrections. The reconciler then wrote a 406-line revision with new arithmetic, and no cold pass has seen it. The new content includes the repeatability term rep_a, the residual r from a third cache size, a knee rule rewritten to a 'derived one-sided threshold', class precedence, and conflicts resolved by the reconciler's own choice (CHANGES.md:40, 42, 73). The proposed executed check, kb_worked_example.py, was written by the same reconciler (CHANGES.md outputs), so it checks self-consistency, not independence. The reconciler also documents a known false-RESOLVED case under option (a) (Δ_rails = 0.00111 ± 0.00076 'RESOLVED both times, where the truth is not'), and a RESOLVED boundary prints nothing beside its claim lines (DRAFT:169). This is off the critical path: the test cannot run before pass-1 collection closes. So a single delta pass costs no calendar time: one cold executing seat limited to the CHANGES.md rows and the Conflicts section, reproducing §5 from its own script rather than the reconciler's. A full third pass is not needed.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: A defect in the reconciler's new knee threshold or rep_a propagation misclassifies the rails boundary as RESOLVED. The rails claim lines then print with no caveat, implying a memory-traffic attribution the test did not establish. Its only check was the author's own script.

judgments.reason: Option (i), a prospective blind extension of end_t0_before, is clean and explicitly allowed (ED-RULING:70-74). The priority order is acceptable if declared before anyone views per-session outputs (see A2). Option (ii) and the priority order misstate what pass 2 buys. Pass 2 does more than replicate: it 'reverses the module order within each sub-pack' (registration:105; design R6:120). In s2 that is the 'cleanest dense/MoE pair' (8B then 30B-A3B), and in s3 and s4 too. With one pass, each model sits in a fixed session position (first or second module, pre- or post-midpoint reference). INFERRED: the reversal's purpose is order counterbalancing, which the texts do not state outright. The priority also puts s1-p2 behind everything when s1-p1 counts, yet the fit set (1.7B, 4B and 8B; roster.json role fit) carries the committed lines. A pass difference on the fit set guards the predictions more than one on any held-out model. If the date binds, the order should be s5-p2, then the fit-set p2s (s1-p2, s2-p2), then the rest. Option (ii) should be chosen only with explicit disclosure that 7 models lack their order-reversed pass.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: Under (ii), the 30B-A3B point comes only from second-in-session position after 8B. A position or thermal drift effect partly absorbed by B but never checked by a reversed pass shifts the MoE point. The active-or-resident answer rests on it, and a reviewer notes that the registered counterbalance was dropped.

judgments.reason: Verified: the p1-to-p2 registration difference (s2 shown) is bytes_pass, null estimator versions, reversed module order with slightly different est_minutes (121.78 vs 121.47), sizing pointers back to the p1 rows, and stale draft_notes. The generator builds both passes in one loop (bytes_plan_trees.py:333-345). The synthetic agreement campaigns already cover a two-pass layout with pass-2 failure cases at the agreeing digest (test_bytes_agreement.py:1924-1960). §13's 'pending their agreement' is therefore already met by the existing evidence for 18582818. No collected number depends on the gate's form. Conditions for a mechanical flip to be safe: (1) the generator drops the stale p2 draft_notes, which read 'a draft ... not registered or armable'; (2) CI runs the every-loop-pack sidecar-authentication test and the pass-2 tree-selection test (design:250); (3) the cherry-pick into the measurement checkout is verified by tree equality, as was done for 991358f73 (RUN_STATE item 71). If the flip commit changes only JSON and sidecars, the laptop-suite rerun is redundant, because the code is the pass-1 tree already run.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: None to a number, given the conditions. Without condition (3), a p2 sidecar or registration mismatch on the measurement checkout repeats the s1-p1 zero-yield loss of a session; it does not produce a wrong number.

judgments.reason: Time-boxing and the labelled alternative for s5-p1 are fine. The gap is 'a prospective procedure both seats agree on goes straight to the arm' without saying how the s5-p2 data are reported. The round-2 brief's Q3 options include a 'prospective exclusion window' (a46602ae RECORD:10). That is a WHAT-is-excluded change applied to one model, chosen after seeing that model's exclusion pattern. INFERRED: implementing it also changes harvest or acceptance code mid-collection, off the reviewed pass-1 lane pin (registration:450; P0 ruling 11). With s5-p1 unavailable, s5-p2 becomes 70B's only point (one_pass, D9(a)). If it carried the new exclusion rule as primary, the H2 regression would mix one model reduced under a different rule. The requirement should be: s5-p2 is always reduced under the registered rule as the registered cell, and any new exclusion window prints beside it as a labelled alternative. A collection-only change (headroom hold) is acceptable, disclosed as a per-model protocol difference, together with an H2 sensitivity line excluding 70B.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: The seats agree on a post-request thermal exclusion window for s5-p2 only. The 70B one_pass point prints as primary under a rule no other model was reduced with, and enters H2 and the tier deviations. A reviewer flags a model-specific, post-hoc exclusion rule.

judgments.reason: Verified: freeze_lines requires exactly 3 fit models (bytes_analysis.py:89-90). The fit set is 1.7B, 4B and 8B (roster.json), so s1 holds two of the three. s1-p2 is last in base_order (loop_bytes.json:4-17). This is an order change between two pending pass-1 attempts that are both already lost. It changes nothing that is measured, excluded or estimated, so I cannot build a path to a wrong number. Unverified: the map's claim that item 78 places s6-p1 before s1-p1. Item 78 says only that s6-p1 'stays open for its retry; loop ROTATE'.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: None found.

judgments.reason: Skipping a smoke cannot by itself produce a wrong number: a defective session is non-counting, and C4 pins plus the roster/config model check catch a wrong model (bytes_analysis.py:993-994). But the proposal's premise and route are wrong. The loop smokes per pack fingerprint: every pack starts with last_smoke_fingerprint None (loop.py:88), and a smoke is forced whenever any pack's fingerprint differs (loop.py:318-319, 520-524). The fingerprint includes pack_id and its tree (fingerprint.py:54-60). So every p2 pack will smoke, and skipping that needs a loop code change mid-collection, off the reviewed pass-1 lane pin (registration:450), not a lead ruling. The p2 trees are new, never-run trees, so the smoke is the only pre-session execution of them. The CI sidecar test covers only the s1-p1 defect class. With the 11-02 cutoff, a lost p2 session costs more than the about 1 h smoke (INFERRED duration).
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: No number path. The risk is time: a p2-tree defect the smoke would have caught consumes a full session slot near the cutoff, possibly s1-p2 or s5-p2.

judgments.reason: A zero-yield abort only ends a session that cannot count. An aborted session is non-counting and its retry is outcome-blind, so I cannot build a path to a wrong or selectively chosen number. The auditor's own condition (only if small and tested, otherwise defer) is right. Note that it is a loop change off the reviewed pass-1 pin (registration:450), and that the cause it guards against (sidecars) is now covered by CI, so deferring to after BYTES costs little.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: None to a number. A buggy abort would cost sessions, not change values.

judgments.reason: Building the code in the cloud on synthetic receipts touches no data. One condition: the alternative of 'a non-claim H-style session runner' must integrate rails, DC and rest over stamped spans with the same reducers pass 1 uses (P0 ruling 9 requires the chain extension, and the README requires mapping and integrating over the receipt's exact span). Otherwise the known-bytes Δ describes a different integration than the claim lines it annotates. The reading rule's stack check would print UNDETERMINED only for stack-field differences, not for integration-method differences (INFERRED).
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: Only if the H-style runner integrates differently: the caveat class printed beside the claim lines would describe a different measurement path.

judgments.reason: Keeping the census and moving agents off the measurement Mac is right. But the destination clashes with where_to_run, which copies every session's raw archive to the Air before the commitment. Stage 1 reads every session's archive for references (bytes_analysis.py:1155-1157 calls archive_records for each export path). Raw powermetrics and meter streams carry no hidden offset (registration:359), and the map itself keeps raw files out of agent VMs because 'blinding relies on code discipline over raw files'. Making the Air the home of all interactive Claude and Codex work puts agents with file access next to unblinded held-out energies. Needed: a separate macOS account, or a no-agent rule on the Air, for the analysis files until the stage-2 release.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: An interactive agent debugging the A2 or A5 tooling on the Air opens a held-out bundle's raw powermetrics, and the 30B-A3B decode energy is seen before predictions.json is committed. The claim 'predictions were committed before the held-out energies were unblinded' (registration:363) then fails.

missed_items: Silent load-dependent unit loss in the re-reduction path. bytes_analysis.py:1001-1002 raises AnalysisError on a non-succeeded re-reduction. AnalysisError subclasses ValueError (:46), so the except at :1016-1017 turns the row into status=unusable instead of refusing. The 120 s wall deadline (powermetrics_fiducial.py:94, 545-551, marked non-reproducible at :1531-1541) can therefore change kept units and printed numbers depending on host load. The same class Ed's ruling 6 required executed evidence against for block 5; none exists for BYTES. INFERRED: that a firing gives status != succeeded. Needs an executed synthetic check and a CLI guard that compares analysis kept units with acceptance before the commitment.

Before the stage-1 commit there is no real-data agreement on re-reduced fit-set rails: the blinded stage and the twin both use exported phase_decode_j (bytes_analysis.py:1146; bytes_twin.py:1321). The first real-data check of the re-reduced fit cells is A6 (DC/rest after release) or the stage-2 comparer. A6 should run before the commitment.

The blinded load_records path never checks acceptance.counting, unlike archive_records (bytes_analysis.py:940-941 vs 1123-1158). An export of a non-counting attempt (s1-p1 zero-yield, s6-p1 aborted) in the export directory could enter the blinded agreement if the manifest lists its session. INFERRED: depends on desk export behaviour and how the manifest is built.

The p2 pack registrations carry stale draft_notes ('a draft with Mac and B2 slots open; not registered or armable'; configs/b6/packs/bytes-s2-p2/registration.json). A mechanical flip must regenerate or remove them, or the registered record contradicts itself.
The known-bytes reading rule already says what prints if the test misses its slot: 'Known-bytes check: not measured' (reading rule DRAFT:167). C13's later fill-in contradicts the rule's own text.
Fit-set pass 2 (s1-p2, s2-p2) protects the committed lines more than any held-out pass 2, yet the map's priority order puts s1-p2 last unless s1-p1 fails.

The A2 per-session blinded outputs, and the C8 and C10 rulings on what to collect, should be sequenced so that the decisions are made before decision-makers see any per-session numeric output beyond comparer counts. Otherwise the scope or date choice is not blind in the sense the amendment rules require.

cadence.segment: BYTES: registration to released result (pass-1 status, known-bytes test, blinded stage, stage-1 fit, commitment, held-out agreement, stage-2 release, coverage, Bonferroni, pass 2, end date 2026-11-02)
cadence.lens: CADENCE SKEPTIC: challenge every KEEP (does it protect a printed number; is there a cheaper form); check that proposals go far enough; find missed parallelism and missed steps

judgments.reason: The cost is already spent and the step protects real numbers. Registration §3 says the pass-1 flip is the registration time. The NEG-8 span defect was number-changing (item 69). The estimator digest 18582818… is what later stages authenticate against (registration §13, line 384). There is nothing left to lighten. Reopening it for pass 2 would be the waste, and C9 covers that.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: Reopening a B0-style cold gate for pass 2 would add about a day of latency and protect no new number.

judgments.reason: The census is automated and costs nothing per arm. It caught two real contamination sources: in item 67 an interactive session was still open at t0; in item 78 a `codex update` run interactively at 09:35, during the s6-p1 session (t0 06:47), left a daemon running. The losses come from people and agents using the Mac during sessions, not from the gate. The proposal to move all interactive work to the Air is right. It could go further. The headless magistrate activations are themselves agent processes on the Mac. The pointer already makes them exit in PRECHECK..SESSION_RUN, but an activation that overruns into ARM_WAIT is the same hazard. Running them from the Air or the cloud, with only short ssh actions in SESSION_DESK/NEXT, removes the last agent tooling from the Mac (whether the census counts sshd: INFERRED, untested).
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: Someone runs an agent or updater on the Mac mid-session, the 2 h fence pauses the session and then aborts it, and about 10 h of the shrinking window before 11-02 is lost (item 78).
evidence_refs: jw/RUN_STATE.md item 78 pointer (1): exit at once if loop in PRECHECK, ARM_WAIT, SMOKE_* or SESSION_RUN

judgments.reason: These are automated predicates evaluated at arm, with zero analyst time. The thermal exclusion demonstrably touches a number: the 70B cell went to 2/10 quads (7326d37c RECORD). The clock, disk and C4 gates have caught nothing (4f20ade7 RECORD:9), but they cost nothing unless they hold. No cheaper form exists. Disk is the one with a real cost, in operator time (item 70). A pre-computed disk budget for all remaining sessions, checked once on the Air against the Mac's free space, would avoid an arm-time surprise. That is a minor item.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: None from keeping them. Removing the thermal or clock gate would let confounded decode energies into kept cells.

judgments.reason: The direction is right but the mechanism and authority are wrong. (1) The smoke is not decided by §19's wording. It is decided in code, per pack_id: smoke_required() returns True when there is no prior pass for that pack_id, or when any fingerprint field differs (code_commit, boot_session_uuid, pack tree_id, model hashes, powermetrics hash) (joulewise/b6/fingerprint.py:75-99; loop.py:318-320, 520-524). Every p2 pack is a new pack_id, so the loop will smoke all six whatever a lead ruling says. Skipping them needs a loop code change (process_rule_change), and that commit itself changes code_commit and so forces re-smoking anyway. (2) Overlapping the 30-minute notice with the smoke is already done: the notice is enqueued and then the state goes straight to SMOKE_RUN, and ARM_WAIT only waits out what is left of notice_sent+1800 (loop.py:321-328, 489). So the claimed 'overlap' saving is zero, and the roughly 1-1.5 h is smoke plus smoke desk. Realistic lightening: either accept roughly 1 h per session, or bundle a one-line rule into the C9 commit, for example 'a p2 pack whose p1 sibling smoked on the same commit and boot needs no smoke'. Even then a reboot or a new commit forces a smoke. Expected saving is at most about 6 h, and it adds the risk of changing a loop mid-collection.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: The lead rules 'no p2 smoke', the loop smokes anyway because fingerprint.smoke_required is per pack_id, and the plan's 6 h saving never happens. Or an unreviewed loop patch lands mid-collection and itself trips a session.

judgments.reason: Time-boxing and dropping the cold gate when the seats agree are right. The fallback does not go far enough and may waste a session. M1 shows all ten thermal hits fall in the 23 s post-request tail, and no pre-member wait would have saved any unit (item 78). Three quads (b04-b06) also carried battery-excursion codes, so even a thermal-window fix caps that pass at about 7/10. The stronger fallback is a pre-declared, blind, dated amendment that confines the thermal exclusion to readings overlapping the member's decode span, with the registered rule printed beside it. It applies prospectively to s5-p2 and as a labelled alternative to s5-p1. Energies stay blind; only exclusion codes have been seen. s5-p2 is second in pass-2 order, after s6-p2, so the ruling has roughly one extra cycle of slack. Use it, without adding rounds.

missed_items: Every commit to the measurement checkout changes the fingerprint's code_commit, which forces a smoke for every pack still to run (fingerprint.py:42-43, 75-99; loop.py:318-320). Bundle C9 (pass-2 flip), any C8 s5-p2 procedure and any C6 zero-yield stop into ONE cherry-pick, landed in a desk window. Separate commits each cost a smoke cycle.

The smoke skip in C3 is not a lead ruling. smoke_required is computed per pack_id in code, so each new p2 pack_id smokes regardless of how §19 is read. The 30-minute notice already overlaps the smoke (loop.py:321-328, 489), so the 'overlap' saving in the map is zero.

The standing pointer (RUN_STATE item 78, step 1) says opening the p2 registrations is 'after the fit set'. C9's same-day flip needs an explicit lead override of that pointer, or it will not happen in time.

The A5/A11 session pool interacts with the 120 s wall deadline (powermetrics_fiducial.py:94). Block 5's firing was load-induced (item 77: 24 s isolated, fired in the loaded process). A4 must time the planned pool size on the Air, not serial runs only.

The idle measurement Mac after the last desk is a candidate machine for stage 1 and stage 2. It is faster, the calibration completed there, it is Ed's 6(c) rationale for block 5, and it needs no key or raw-archive copy. Choose between Mac and Air from A4's measurements, not by assumption.

User asked 'as much in the cloud as possible'. The blinded-export-only steps (A2 per-session runs, A3, A8) never read archives, keys or meter data (bytes_analysis.py:1124-1129; registration line 359), so they could run in cloud seats if Ed rules that blinded exports may leave his machines. Only raw-archive steps (A5, A6 meter, A11) and key releases need Ed's machines. The map never asks this narrower question.

The DST t0 blackout (10-31 16:30 PDT to 11-01 02:00 PST, item 69(e)) bars BYTES t0s, not other quiet-Mac work. It is a natural slot for the known-bytes hour (C13) or part of the block-5 dry run (ED-RULING 6a), so they need not pre-empt a BYTES session (INFERRED: depends on what is running at 16:30).

Block-5 dry-run Mac time (precedence under ED-RULING 6a) is not budgeted in the roughly 80-120 h BYTES estimate. Its duration on the Mac is unmeasured, and that is a further reason for Ed to decide the C10 extension or priority today.

C8 fallback: 'run s5-p2 unchanged' likely reproduces about 2/10 quads, because M1 shows the hits are systematic in the post-request tail. The better pre-declared blind fallback is an exclusion-window amendment (thermal counted only when it overlaps the decode span), with the registered rule printed beside it. Battery-excursion quads still cap the pass at about 7/10.

A1 is stronger than stated. With s1 absent the CLI refuses at frozen_predictions (bytes_analyze.py:91), so no predictions.json exists and stage 2 (which requires --predictions) cannot run. A lost s1 therefore blocks H2 and the MoE answer too, not only H1. validate_manifest also only allows dropping Qwen3-8B-8bit (bytes_analysis.py:438-440).

map.segment: Process gates: reviews, cold gates, councils, CI, and where orchestration runs (measurement Mac, cloud, MacBook Air). Path prefixes used below: jw: = scratchpad/jw (main), l9: = scratchpad/wt/l9, bytes: = scratchpad/wt/bytes, scout: = scratchpad/wt/scout/.codex-report/BLIND-DRY-RUN-SCOUT.md. All read-only. Nothing was launched or edited.

steps.name: Seat brief and WRITE_SCOPE fence
steps.what: Every delegated seat gets an exhaustive write scope. The seat stops with NEEDS_SCOPE outside it, and the lead grants or refuses.
steps.protects: Protects the four pinned estimator files and the governed calibration pins from unreviewed edits. If they change silently, the digests that define the calibration change.
steps.cost: In L9, 12 of 47 seats stopped at a fence, at 30-60 min each (K22). In October FIX-416-A and FIX-416-B each stopped once for scope, and FIX-416-F stopped twice.
steps.caught_real_defects: No number-touching catch outside the estimator files (OP-11). FIX-416-B's request for joulewise/b5/driver.py was refused correctly, because an identity difference is a harvest flag, not an arm refusal.
steps.redundant_with: The estimator-file freeze test (MG-23) and repin's estimator pins already protect the files that matter.
steps.proposal: Keep exhaustive scopes, as the CLAUDE.md rule says. In build briefs, grant the module, its tests and every registry it joins up front (OP-11 proposal). Fence only the estimator and pinned files tightly. No rule text changes.
steps.saves: Most of 12 fence stops per lane at 30-60 min each, about 6-12 seat-hours per large lane (INFERRED from the L9 rate).

steps.name: Bridge return envelope (BRIDGE_REPORT_V1 / claude-codex-report/v1)
steps.what: A seat's final two lines must be a parseable JSON envelope. A missing or malformed envelope counts as protocol failure, never as success.
steps.protects: Protects against an orchestrator taking a hallucinated 'done' at face value.
steps.cost: rc=65 on every consult while the bodies were complete (K19). Reruns or manual recovery each time.
steps.caught_real_defects: None (OP-12).
steps.redundant_with: The lead's diff read and replayed checks (SKILL.md step 7; orchestration.md:242-246) are the real protection against a false 'done'.
steps.proposal: Bridge-protocol v1.2. A malformed envelope with a complete body is FLAGGED, and the lead accepts the work only after its own diff read and test replay. No rerun is required. A missing body is still a failure.
steps.saves: One rerun or manual parse per affected seat (K19: every consult in that period).

steps.name: Seat self-check: quick_suite --tier touched
steps.what: Before handing back, a seat runs the state and docs fences, the fast modules, and every module that names a changed path.
steps.protects: Catches a broken module before the lead's time is spent.
steps.cost: Minutes. The default is modules under 5 s plus the touched modules.
steps.caught_real_defects: Not separately tallied (unknown). It is the seat-side copy of CI's quick tier.
steps.redundant_with: CI quick tier (ci.yml:14-33).
steps.proposal: Keep it as is. Cheap, and it shortens fix loops.
steps.saves: n/a

steps.name: Independent executing review by a non-author (ledger row 1)
steps.what: A seat that did not write the code runs it, with probes and mutations, and reports findings. The lead dispositions every finding (row 5).
steps.protects: The main R mechanism. Catches arithmetic and selection defects that the author's tests share with the code.
steps.cost: 30-90 min per review (MG-4), serial before the cold pass.
steps.caught_real_defects: YES, W-class. Historically: SC C11, C12, C37 and L9 C59, C63 (MG-4). In October: the PR #500 review found MAJOR-1 (a running magistrate was never stood down for a block-6 plan, so an agent could load a window). The H Opus review confirmed that the reservation --plan binding would refuse at chain stage 1.
steps.redundant_with: The cold final pass (G06). On PR #501 the two blind cold passes were used as row 1 instead of adding a third seat.
steps.proposal: Merge with G06 into one stage: two blind executing seats from different families, launched in parallel. Both count as row 1 and row 4. This follows the precedent at pr501-gates.md:13-14. Change the ledger text so row 1 accepts 'cold pass N' evidence.
steps.saves: One serial seat per full-tier merge (30-90 min wall, one seat). Roughly 10-15 merges in October (INFERRED from items 40-78).

steps.name: Delta review of number-code fixes, and the final-head rule
steps.what: Each fix round on number-bearing code gets a fresh executing delta pass. A commit after review that touches number-bearing code is reviewed again.
steps.protects: Protects against a fix that introduces a new number defect, and against an unreviewed last commit.
steps.cost: About 25 min per cold delta seat (7209d1b0 item 15). #416 ran 7 rounds × 2 seats over about 2 days. #573 ran rounds a-i (9+), and #574 rounds b-e.
steps.caught_real_defects: YES in early rounds. #416 round 1: a reference dropped silently on a read failure. Round 2: storage faults, E_ref 37.121 → 37.089 J. Round 3: an unauthenticated roster, allowance +16 %. #573: twin silent divergence on .zst (185 fields), and the NEG-8 mint recording a good member as a drop. Rounds 4-7 of #416 found 'edge cases that cannot occur on the real records' and 'No number'. The round-6 HIGH was a smoke stop, not a number.
steps.redundant_with: Late rounds duplicate the lead's real-archive replay (25 archives, 0 stops), which is what showed the late findings cannot occur.
steps.proposal:
Write the stopping rule into orchestration.md 'round limits':
- (a) The same defect class twice goes immediately to a structural ruling (the #416 round-2 and #574 round-e precedents), not to another fix round or a consult.
- (b) A delta round ends the chain when every finding is LOW/INFO, or when replay over every real archive shows it cannot occur. The lead dispositions those with no fix round (7209d1b0 item 26).
- (c) Delta rounds use one family, alternating, unless a round returns a BLOCKER.
The final-head rule stays.
steps.saves: #416: rounds 4-7 took about 5 h wall (20:3x 10-24 to about 01:xx 10-25) and 8 seat runs, with no number. Similar savings on #573 rounds f-i.

steps.name: Cold final pass on measurement, calibration or claim code (ledger row 4), two families blind
steps.what: Fable 5.1 and Opus 5.5, each blind to the other, execute the merge candidate. Each finding is dispositioned.
steps.protects: Gives a second, independent family view on number-bearing code. Different families catch different defects.
steps.cost: 30-60 min each (MG-5), usually after G04.
steps.caught_real_defects: YES. On PR #501, Fable F1 MAJOR (the verdict writer's raw-CPU veto) and Opus F1 MAJOR (the wait-budget skip): each family caught one the other missed (d34bf254 tally). L9 C66 W (Opus, sign error). B2-NR1 M1 (C_j form). KB rule: two corrections that could give a wrong class. On the b6 stage-1 pin b9de23a2c the cold and delta passes found no refusal, yet machine test 1 then found the agent.presence defect (W-latent).
steps.redundant_with: G04, which is the same kind of seat.
steps.proposal: Merge with G04 as above. Keep two families for code that decides counting, exclusion, estimators or the claim path. Use one family for other full-tier code (watchdog, mailer, loop plumbing, notices). The ledger's 'N/A (no measurement, calibration or claim code)' text already allows that.
steps.saves: The same serial stage as G04, plus one seat per non-claim full-tier PR.

Code that runs on the measurement Mac (collector, driver, loop, harvest, hazards) also needs a macOS whole-suite run, done on the MacBook Air (same OS and architecture as the measurement Mac) and never on the measurement Mac. Quarantine or fix the load-sensitive modules (MG-3 'KEEP, but'). Update orchestration.md row 2 and the BYTES §19 'laptop' wording prospectively.

steps.name: GitHub CI test jobs (quick, 12 ordinary shards, 2 exclusive jobs, build, installed wheel)
steps.what: Required checks on main. The quick tier, the ordinary suite in 12 LPT-balanced shards, and the calibration-exit and crash-matrix exclusive jobs run in parallel. Docs-only ranges skip them.
steps.protects: Executing regression tests on every push. These are the R evidence for rows 2 and 3.

steps.proposal: Keep it blocking. Rebalance from current hosted timings: split the module that floors shard 10 using the existing split_modules or exclusive-job pattern (ci.yml:199-225, 252-320), so the wall time goes back toward the design figure. Regenerate scripts/test_timings.json on a schedule instead of by hand.
