steps.protects: repin's estimator pins and the strict mock smoke protect numbers. The rest are record-about-record checks (class X).
steps.cost: It blocks docs PRs. Item 58: main CI was red until 'executed-evidence sections on five dated rulings' were added. repin blocked every push including docs-only, and caused K20 and the S3/S10 fix rounds (MG-13). test_docs_freshness is also one of L9's six acceptance modules (ED-RULING item 1).
steps.caught_real_defects: None for MG-16 (docs freshness), MG-17 (state kernel), MG-18 (histsem) and MG-13 beyond the estimator files. The CLI strict smoke is not separately tallied.
steps.redundant_with: The estimator-file freeze test (l9 tests/b5_analysis/test_frozen_files.py, MG-23) covers the pins that protect numbers.
steps.proposal: Blocking: the CLI strict mock smoke, and repin limited to the estimator and governed calibration pins (ESTIMATOR_CODE_PATHS). Advisory (non-blocking job): docs freshness, gen_state, histsem. Delete the state kernel and TASK_QUEUE after the L9 merge, as 7a decision 6 already decided. Drop tests.test_docs_freshness from L9's acceptance list: it guards ruling formats, not L9 numbers.
steps.saves: The docs-PR red cycles (item 58 type) and one L9 acceptance module. No science protection is lost.

steps.name: Gate-ledger required check, Impact statement and TIER-01 tiering
steps.what: The PR body must hold a five-row ledger with RUN evidence and a six-line Impact statement. A light tier is refused if any Impact line says Yes. Required on main since 2026-09-24 (D-170). TIER-01 defines full and light tiers, and its revert trigger is the defect log.
steps.protects: The Impact statement routes anything that can change a number to the full tier (orchestration.md:132-133). The row-format checker targets forgotten rows.
steps.cost: A head-SHA edit to the PR body after every push. About 50 red ledger emails a night before drafts were exempted on 10-22. Minutes per PR.
steps.caught_real_defects: Format checker: never caught anything (MG-9). TIER-01: zero light-tier escapes (tier01_defect_log.md has no rows). Day-30 review: due 2026-10-25 and not recorded in the decision log, which ends at D-186 (09-29).
steps.redundant_with: The ledger rows record evidence that G04-G08 produce. The checker only checks the record's format (MG-8: class X).
steps.proposal: (1) Record the overdue TIER-01 day-30 decision now: light-tier merge count, escapes 0, continue. (2) Widen light tier to non-number tooling (mailer, notices, watcher text) once all six Impact lines read No. (3) Have a script fill the ledger rows from executing_reviews.json and the CI run, and make the format checker advisory. The Impact-statement Yes→full refusal stays blocking.
steps.saves: Per-PR body editing and the red-email noise. It also removes a formal lapse: TIER-01 'continues only by a recorded decision'.

steps.name: Integration review for merge waves
steps.what: One dedicated review hunts interaction defects when two or more PRs changing measurement code land together.
steps.protects: Protects against cross-PR interaction defects.
steps.cost: Small; it rarely triggers (MG-6).
steps.caught_real_defects: YES historically: two integration defects in the 07-07/08 merge session, and C20 W (MG-6). October: not triggered separately. The #515 wave (123-137 commits) was held for a decision instead (item 60, scout:41).
steps.redundant_with: The whole suite on the merged tree covers a single PR.
steps.proposal: Keep as is. Use it for the L9 plus block-6 stage-2 plus BYTES wave onto main after the block-5 release.
steps.saves: n/a

steps.name: Lead diff read and lead live gate (real programs, real archives)
steps.what: The lead reads the exact merge candidate and runs the real flow: it replays every real archive after a rule change and re-executes reviewers' probes.
steps.protects: Catches defects whose own tests encode the same wrong assumption. Catches over-refusal of real data.
steps.cost: Minutes to an hour per change.
steps.caught_real_defects: YES. Each rule change in #416 caught one over-refusal of real data ('H's uncollected references; the zero-run archive'), which touches which data count. Re-executing Fable's #416 round-1 blocker confirmed it. The lead rehearsal on H caught the git-through-symlink defect before arm.
steps.redundant_with: None. It is the only gate that runs on the real archives.
steps.proposal: Keep it. Run the replays on the MacBook Air against hash-verified copies of the non-claim archives (H, BY-H2, machine tests, smokes), so the measurement Mac stays quiet. Claim archives stay restricted to the Mac.
steps.saves: Measurement-Mac CPU during replays.

steps.name: Real-program rehearsal: machine test, smoke, first arm on committed bytes
steps.what: Runs the real loop, driver, harvest and desk over a short non-claim session before claim sessions.
steps.protects: Protects against defects that refuse or empty every session, or that admit agent-overlapping runs.
steps.cost: A machine test is about 40 min of Mac time plus desk time. Three MT runs on 10-16/17. Each H arm refusal cost about 1 h 10 min of Mac time.
steps.caught_real_defects:
YES, every S-class catch of October, all after reviews had passed:
- MT1: plan_tree.sha256 sidecar not rewritten, so round 1 could never arm; agent.presence flag rejected, so an agent-overlapping run could have counted (W-latent).
- MT2: the busy-fraction veto lost every busy-only run.
- H arm 1: no config inventory.
- H arm 2: ledger split.
- s1-p1: 143 runs refused on missing sidecars. The smoke passed because it writes its own sidecar into a staged copy.
steps.redundant_with: None. Reviews (G04-G06, G16) did not find any of these.
steps.proposal: Make it a required gate. Before a registered pack's first counting session, run one non-claim smoke through the real loop using the committed pack bytes, never a staged copy. The smoke harness must read the same files the chain reads; fixing the harness is a full-tier code change. Run it right after the registration commit, in parallel with the registration cold gate, not after it.
steps.saves: s1-p1's lost session: one 313-388 min chain slot, plus the 9 yield notices and the re-pin cycle.

steps.name: Two-seat blind council for design or science questions
steps.what: The default seat (Sol 6.1) and one seat from another family answer blind. A cold judge is added only when they split on a science question.
steps.protects: Gives independent diagnosis of physical causes and design choices.
steps.cost: 10-30 min each (OP-1). In October about 9 councils: block-6 design, L9 Q-RENDERER/LINEAGE/EXACTSTACK/CONSUMERID, BYTES held-out rows, B6 NR, B2 NR1, H-DISK, KB rule, and 70B thermal rounds 1 and 2.
steps.caught_real_defects: YES (S/W): SC C36, C39, C42, C44 and L9 C50, C68. October: H-DISK sized the disk rule to refuse 0 of 9 good sessions. 70B M1 showed the thermal hits are post-request tails, which turned the question into a science question.
steps.redundant_with: None.
steps.proposal: Keep as is. Run both seats in the cloud, in parallel (already done).
steps.saves: n/a

steps.name: Four-model council (D-184)
steps.what: Fable, Opus, Sol and Astra on every major change 'when usage allows'.
steps.protects: Gives a diverse read on important science.
steps.cost: 0. It never ran (OP-8).
steps.caught_real_defects: None (never run).
steps.redundant_with: G14, plus a cold judge on a split.
steps.proposal: Delete it from the council skill and the D-184 text. orchestration.md:105 already limits it to 'only when Ed asks', and D-186 replaced its team. Ed can still ask for one.
steps.saves: Removes a stale mandate that seats load from skills.

steps.name: Cold judge per rule change, and judge plus refuter erratum chain (charter v2)
steps.what: A fresh cold judge rules on a packet under the charter, paired with a refuter from another family. Outputs are sealed and hash-pinned, with a packet-hygiene duty and a charter digest check.
steps.protects: Gives a judge free of loop context for rules that decide data. It is the anti-sunk-cost check.
steps.cost: 10-60 min plus charge writing (OP-3). Block-5 errata took about 10 h, 3 h and 3.5 h (OP-5). October: the B6 Q2 judge, the B2-NR1 judge, and the L9-ruling cold passes (2), on top of their councils.
steps.caught_real_defects: No W in three periods. L9 judges missed two defects later found by running code, and ruled one question wrong (K27). The 10-13 audit found blind Opus re-rulings 'never worse and better in 2 to 4 of 10'.
steps.redundant_with: OP-2, an executing refuter, which has W catches (B3 C5, SC C31).
steps.proposal: Install 7a decision 3 (decided 2026-10-14, not yet in orchestration.md:83-94): a rule change gets one executing refuter plus a one-line orchestrator decision. A cold judge stays only (i) when a two-seat council splits on a science question, and the judge must execute the disputed arithmetic (OP-7), and (ii) where a registration's own text requires one (block-5 §10). Charter digest check: keep (seconds). Fold the 09-29 convening list into the charter at the next Ed-ratified byte change.
steps.saves: One judge seat plus packet assembly per rule change, roughly 1-3 h each (OP-3, OP-5).

steps.name: Registration and acceptance cold gate (two blind judges re-deriving from raw)
steps.what: Before a registration or calibration acceptance binds, two cold judges (Fable and Opus) re-derive the values from raw data and rule ADMIT/REJECT per slot.
steps.protects: Protects estimators and exclusion levels fixed before data, and the raw re-derivation of calibration constants (orchestration.md:129-131).
steps.cost: Hours per gate. In October: b6 acceptance (2 judges), b6 whole file (2 judges), the BYTES registration gate after #416 (2 judges), and KB cold passes (2).
steps.caught_real_defects: YES at the value level. The b6 acceptance judges kept S-8's exclusion as a flag (it would have removed 14 of 53 known-good runs) and moved c_q from 0.73 to 0.54. Whole-file b6 gate: text corrections only ('None of the defects found makes round 1's data unusable'). #416 registration gate: 'no number-touching defect'.
steps.redundant_with: The #416 audit (G18) already re-derived the same BYTES sizing rows three times before the registration gate.
steps.proposal: Two-judge raw re-derivation only for slots holding a measured value or an exclusion level (the b6 acceptance pattern, where catches occurred). Whole-file text gates become one judge plus one executing refuter. When a #416 audit has already re-derived the same values at the same head, the registration gate checks only the text and the diff since the audit.
steps.saves: One judge seat and several hours per whole-file gate. Avoids re-deriving the BYTES rows a 4th and 5th time.

steps.name: Pre-arm triple audit, directive #416
steps.what: Three blind seats (Astra 6, Fable 5.1, Opus 5.5 at the highest effort) re-derive the calibration and sizing from raw files at the frozen head before any claim-bearing run. It runs once per frozen code or protocol change.
steps.protects: Protects the claim-bearing calibration and sizing, checked against raw bytes.
steps.cost: About 2 days for the BYTES pass-1 instance: audit on 10-23/24, then 7 cold delta rounds into 10-25 (7209d1b0). Three seats at the highest effort for several hours each (MG-7).
steps.caught_real_defects: YES, W. The NEG-8 reference span was the measured_run stage, 6.5-6.9× the request, so the DC drift term was 52 % low. Fable and Opus found it; Astra missed it. It also found the numeric predictors unbound (doubling W moved BW from 266 to 475 GB/s with no flag) and cell.below_minimum wrongly excluding a whole session. It MISSED the plan_tree.sha256 sidecar defect that emptied s1-p1.
steps.redundant_with: G17 (same rows re-derived at the registration gate) and G13 (the escape class it missed).
steps.proposal: Two seats (Fable and Opus, executing) instead of three, since the third family missed the key blocker. Pair it with the required real-loop smoke (G13) at the same head, in parallel, so the audit covers numbers and the smoke covers the plumbing that refuses sessions. Delta rounds follow G05's stopping rule.
steps.saves: One highest-effort seat (several hours) per audit. About 5 h and 8 seats of late delta rounds. The s1-p1 class of loss.

steps.name: Battery float, directive #421
steps.what: A physical predicate on battery current at arm, publication and t0, plus per-slot ioreg observations. Excursions exclude the run or unit, with disclosure.
steps.protects: A real physical hazard: battery assist hides DC-input energy from the meter.
steps.cost: Near zero in the loop (automatic).
steps.caught_real_defects: YES (P-protective). r1-alpha's battery flags met #421 (lowest SMC readings -22/-20 mA). s5-p1 lost 3 units to battery excursions in the 70B cell.
steps.redundant_with: None.
steps.proposal: Keep it as a physical check. Not ceremony.
steps.saves: n/a

steps.name: Quiet-Mac agent census, stand-down fence, arm notice and STOP
steps.what: Before t0 and during a session, the census refuses or pauses while any agent process is alive. The watchdog stands the magistrate down before spans. The arm notice lets Ed answer NO.
steps.protects: A real physical hazard: an agent on the measurement Mac adds measured joules (orchestration.md:117-120).
steps.cost:
October losses:
- BY-H2 refused at t0 because interactive 8a9fb7fe was open: one 9.5 h idle Mac interval.
- s6-p1 aborted by a leftover Codex 0.164.0 app-server daemon: 2 h pause, then the session lost and needing a retry.
- Two machine-test installs withdrawn or refused while an interactive session was alive.
- Activations must exit 'at once, quietly' whenever the loop is in PRECHECK..SESSION_RUN.
steps.caught_real_defects: YES (P-protective) every time. Each hit was a real contender, and the cause was always an agent or tool on the measurement Mac itself.
steps.redundant_with: None.
steps.proposal: Keep the fence. Remove the hazard source instead: move orchestration, interactive sessions and Codex CLI or app use off the measurement Mac to the MacBook Air (see G21). On the measurement Mac, disable the Codex auto-updater and app-server daemon (a setting, per 'one setting or one command'). The census already catches it before t0.
steps.saves: October: at least 9.5 h idle + about 2 h pause + one lost session slot (313-388 min chain + 88-101 min harvest) ≈ 17-19 h of Mac time.

steps.name: Magistrate activations (headless orchestrator on the measurement Mac)
steps.what: A launchd watchdog on the Mac starts headless Opus sessions that read RUN_STATE, rule, launch seats, arm, harvest, email and write records. 33 activations and 2 loop wakes in items 41-78.
steps.protects: Keeps the work going between Ed's sessions. It holds merge and arm authority under the rules.
steps.cost: Each activation must fit between sessions and exit before PRECHECK. Work waits for session boundaries ('A hand-off between models waits for a session boundary; continuous coordination would need the orchestrator off the Mac'). Usage-limit exits and 2 h background caps killed seats (7209d1b0 item 12). L9 lost its pointer from item 68 to item 77 after the 10-23 Codex Cloud outage.
steps.caught_real_defects: n/a (coordination role). Its records carry the pruning tallies.
steps.redundant_with: Interactive sessions with Ed (items 65, 66, 77).
steps.proposal: Run the orchestrator, magistrate loop and interactive sessions on the MacBook Air, continuously. The Air holds Ed's ChatGPT login for codex-cloud-run.mjs, so no credential goes into a cloud seat. On the measurement Mac keep only the launchd loop, harvest and desk scripts, and the block-5 dry run. The Air does Mac-touching steps (launchctl bootstrap, desk, notice ack) as short scripted calls at SESSION_DESK or DONE. Before that, confirm the census treats the remote-execution path as quiet (OPEN). Seats stay in the cloud.
steps.saves: Removes the session-boundary latency for every hand-off (items 39, 54-56: launches deferred to SESSION_DESK) and the G20 agent losses.

steps.name: Local Sol seats on the measurement Mac (fallback executor)
steps.what: When Codex Cloud has no executors, fix and review seats run locally on the Mac via codex-run-v3, in jw-wt worktrees, only while the Mac is idle.
steps.protects: Keeps the work going during cloud outages.
steps.cost: Competes with measurement for the Mac. Local seat scratch pinned 53 GiB of APFS clones (7209d1b0 item 34), and Codex scope snapshots took 24 GiB (item 70). Disk is the Mac's scarce resource.
steps.caught_real_defects: n/a (executor).
steps.redundant_with: Codex Cloud seats (item 39).
steps.proposal: Move the fallback executor to the MacBook Air (24 GB RAM, Codex CLI installed). Up to 2 concurrent local Sol seats there when Codex Cloud is down (INFERRED capacity). Keep the measurement Mac free of seat scratch.
steps.saves: Tens of GiB of measurement-Mac disk churn and the risk of a seat running into a PRECHECK. Seats keep running through outages like the one on 10-22/23.
evidence_refs: jw:RUN_STATE.md:259 (item 68: 'never got executors; its work runs as local Sol seats')

steps.name: L9 acceptance gates (ED-RULING items 1 and 3)
steps.what: L9 merges after six short modules, a shared physics_cache with a byte-identity test, one full-size cached test_dry_run, one executing review, and CI. The cold Fable and Opus passes move to 'before the release event'.
steps.protects: Protects blind-written analysis code that turns archives into printed numbers.
steps.cost: Full-size test_dry_run about 6 h on a 5-vCPU VM (22,170 s), test_release_equality about 13 h. The six short modules take about 830 s in total (mint_kept_units 739 s). L9-2 runs one long module at a time on 4 vCPU.
steps.caught_real_defects: The joined full-size run exposed the step-9b wall-deadline firing (host speed, not arithmetic) and the 82 identical refits (63 % of wall time). Earlier L9 cold passes: C66 W (Opus, sign error).
steps.redundant_with: Item 1's 'one executing review' and item 3's two cold passes are three seats on the same code at two different times.
steps.proposal: Launch the two blind executing cold passes (Fable and Opus, cloud) as soon as L9-2's modules are green, and count them as item 1's executing review (G04+G06 merge). Then nothing remains between the Mac dry run and release except the recompute agreement. Drop tests.test_docs_freshness from the item-1 list (G09).
steps.saves: One serial seat at merge, and one cold-pass cycle (about 1-2 h plus dispositions) off the dry-run-to-release path.

steps.name: Block-5 analysis plan §3.1 step 12: results cold gate
steps.what: A judge and a refuter re-derive every printed number from the artifacts of steps 3-11 before any paper sentence is filled.
steps.protects: Gives a second derivation of printed numbers.
steps.cost: 'Days per gate round' (cadence plan §1), on the critical path after release.
steps.caught_real_defects: Never run (block 5 not released).
steps.redundant_with: The independent recompute (scripts/independent_recompute_b5.py, which shares no code with L9) re-derives every printed quantity and must agree within registered bars. 7a decision 2 already made recompute agreement the release condition.
steps.proposal: Replace step 12 with one reviewer who reads the recompute's comparison table, and the renderer check that every row of the validated fill input prints. Done as a dated seal-record addendum, written before release while blind. No arithmetic, exclusion or blinding change.
steps.saves: Days on the release-to-paper path. Two seats.

steps.name: Block-6 §13 code gate: full-size synthetic chain plus two cold passes before the blind dry run
steps.what: The block-6 additions must be tested on full-size production-shaped synthetic archives through the real stage chain, independently reviewed, and given one blind executing cold pass each by Fable and Opus, before the S-14 pin.
steps.protects: Protects blind-written block-6 additions: pairing, between-session summary, replication word.
steps.cost: A full-size synthetic chain is about 6 h per run on cloud VMs (ED-RULING). Plus 2 cold passes.
steps.caught_real_defects: Not yet run. The B6-AN-1 driver is still being built (the scout calls analysis_lane.py a stub).
steps.redundant_with: The real blind dry run over the nine sessions, which reads real immutable archives with numbers closed. Per ED-RULING, a full-size synthetic run before it 'rehearses a rehearsal'.
steps.proposal: Apply the ED-RULING pattern: a cached full-size run once per release candidate, one gate stage of two parallel blind executing seats (G04+G06), and the real blind dry run as the end-to-end test. Needs a dated §17 entry checked by one executing refuter, written now while blinded.
steps.saves: About 6-12 h of full-size synthetic runs per fix round, plus one serial seat.

steps.name: Release cold gate added by the blind-dry-run scout
steps.what: The scout's plan adds a cold release packet and gate before the block-5 and block-6 releases.
steps.protects: Nothing beyond what the recompute agreement and the dry-run digest equality already protect.
steps.cost: One cold-gate cycle per release (packet assembly plus judge plus refuter).
steps.caught_real_defects: n/a (not yet run).
steps.redundant_with: Block-6 §12.3 already rules it out: 'There is no separate cold gate (pruning list 7a decision 2 ...)'. Also block-5 7a decision 2, and release_digest_differs_from_dry_run.
steps.proposal: Record a lead line that the release condition is dry run plus recompute agreement plus digest equality, as registered. The scout's step 3 'cold release packet' and step 5 'cold release record' become the dated release record only.
steps.saves: One cold-gate cycle per release (two releases).

steps.name: Independent recompute agreement
steps.what: Code that shares nothing with L9 recomputes the headline numbers from raw power records. They must agree within registered bars: 1 mJ per phase energy, and half a unit of the last printed digit.
steps.protects: The one independent check that numbers are computed right. It is the release condition.
steps.cost: Not yet run on real data. Same Mac bytes as the dry run.
steps.caught_real_defects: Pre-data: #571 scoped trace stops and exact bars. Block-6 derivation: 154 of 154 phase energies within 7e-15 J on rehearsals.
steps.redundant_with: Makes step 12 (G24) redundant.
steps.proposal: Keep it. Run it on the Mac right after the dry run in the same quiet window, or alongside it if the deadline-sensitive step 9b is not running (INFERRED: both are CPU-bound, so concurrent runs could trip the 120 s deadline; prefer sequential within one hold).
steps.saves: n/a

steps.name: Session-end pruning tally (the one pruning rule)
steps.what: At session end the orchestrator lists each gate that ran and what it caught that touched a number. A mechanism with no catch in its last three sessions is proposed to Ed for deletion.
steps.protects: Keeps ceremony from accumulating.
steps.cost: Minutes. Present in about 16 of the 30 October records (grep).
steps.caught_real_defects: Meta. It produced the evidence used here (for example the 7209d1b0 tally: rounds 4-7 'No number'; registration gate 'no number-touching defect').
steps.redundant_with: None.
steps.proposal: Write the tally as a fixed table (gate, ran, caught_number y/n, evidence) in each record, and let a short script collect the last three sessions per gate, so deletion proposals reach Ed automatically. This report is such a proposal.
steps.saves: It ends the drift that left the 10-14 deletions (MG-9, MG-16, OP-3, OP-8) unapplied for 13 days.

steps.name: Two-writer rule and session-end fixture census
steps.what: At most one writer per working tree. A ps census of orphaned test fixtures runs at session end.
steps.protects: Protects against lost work. Orphan fixtures add load on the measurement Mac (pid 43816, a leaked hazard_monitor, ran from 10-15 to 10-17).
steps.cost: Seconds.
steps.caught_real_defects: Operational. An orphaned fixture inflated c_q (item 42). The stall watcher prevented a repeat of the 6.5 h stall (OP-13).
steps.redundant_with: None.
steps.proposal: Keep both. The census matters most on the measurement Mac. Once seats move to the Air and cloud, run it there too.
steps.saves: n/a

parallelism: Merge the review stage: launch the non-author executing review and the cold final pass together, as two blind seats from different families. The PR #501 precedent counted the two cold passes as row 1 (jw:docs/process_traces/2026-10-17-magistrate-d34bf254/pr501-gates.md:13-14). This removes one serial 30-90 min stage per full-tier merge (MG-4, jw:docs/process/pruning_list_2026-10-14.md:341).

L9: start the Fable and Opus cold passes in the cloud as soon as lane/2026-10-27-l9-2's modules are green. They then run in parallel with the single full-size cached test_dry_run and with the BYTES loop, instead of at release time (jw:docs/process_traces/2026-10-27-l9-restart/ED-RULING.md:48-49 already allows running them in parallel with the dry run).

Fix seats start on the first delta report that arrives rather than waiting for both families. #416 rounds launched fix seats only after both reports (jw:docs/process_traces/2026-10-24-magistrate-7209d1b0/RECORD.md:18,31,42). INFERRED gain of about 20-30 min per round.

Run the real-loop smoke (G13) and the registration cold gate (G17) on the same head in parallel. The smoke needs only the committed packs, not the gate's verdict (bytes:docs/registrations/bytes_pack_v1.md:450 orders them serially).

Run the #416 audit seats in parallel with the registration text work. Its findings are already reproduced row by row, so the registration gate need only check the diff (jw:docs/process_traces/2026-10-24-magistrate-7209d1b0/DISPOSITIONS-416.md:3).

CI: split the module that floors shard 10 (about 150 min, jw:docs/process_traces/2026-10-25-magistrate-8b6b2b12/RECORD.md:30) using the existing split_modules or exclusive-job pattern (jw:.github/workflows/ci.yml:199-225,252-320). Run the macOS whole suite on the Air at the same time as Linux CI, not after it.
Councils: both seats already launch in parallel in the cloud (jw:RUN_STATE.md item 76/78). Keep the cold judge conditional on a science split only.

Block-6 §13 build (B6-AN-1) and its review run in the cloud while the Mac runs the block-5 dry run. Block-6's analysis is a two-level DAG: six ALPHA/BETA sessions are independent, and each GAMMA waits on its pair (jw:docs/design/analysis_cadence_plan.md:30-33).

The dry run and independent recompute run sequentially within one Mac hold. Seats, reviews and the release-record drafting run in parallel in the cloud and on the Air. Only structure leaves the restricted folder.
map.amendment_rules:
Governing texts, quoted:

**1. jw:docs/orchestration.md:83-90**
"When a cold gate is convened. Only for: (a) a registration, analysis plan or estimator constant; (b) a claim-bearing result (a calibration issued for claim use, a number the paper will print); (c) an irreversible action: deleting evidence, committing a measurement window, publishing; (d) a choice Ed has reserved to himself or to a cold gate. Fixture repair, scope grants, reading a ruling's own clause, process wording and "waiting" turn ends are the orchestrator's calls, recorded in the session record."

**2. jw:docs/orchestration.md:97-101**
"Any clause that limits rounds must name where the question goes when the limit is reached ("escalate to a consult", "to a cold gate", "to Ed")". D-186 (jw:docs/decision_log.md:12230) adds: "a round-limit clause says where the question goes when the limit is reached ... never 'stop for good'."

**3. jw:docs/orchestration.md:157-160 (pruning rule)**
"Any mechanism with no such catch in its last three sessions is proposed for deletion to Ed."

**4. TIER-01 items 4-5, jw:docs/orchestration.md:267-268**
"If any defect that changes a recorded, reduced or published number entered under LIGHT-TIER, TIER-01 is suspended at once ... and may be reinstated only by a new cold gate." "Day-30 review 2026-10-25: the orchestrator records the light-tier merge count and escape count in the decision log; the rule continues only by a recorded decision." This record is missing: jw:docs/decision_log.md ends at D-186.

**5. Charter, jw:docs/process/coldgate_charter_registry.md:43-48**
"Promotion requires Ed to re-ratify these exact candidate bytes." Lines 23-30: the 09-29 convening list is to be folded in "at the next byte change that Ed ratifies".

**6. Block-5 registration §10, jw:configs/campaigns/v5_claim_25g83/registration_block5.md:5144-5145**
"None to §§3–9 for an armed or completed attempt. A rule, threshold, catalog effect, roster or blinding change is a prospective cold erratum (one judge, one refuter), settled in one erratum."

**7. Block-5 plan §3.2 item 3, jw:configs/campaigns/v5_claim_25g83/analysis_plan_block5.md:196-199**
"A repair needed after the release is allowed only if it is written and reviewed by seats that have read no released number ... Any other change goes to a cold gate before it runs, and its outputs are labelled as produced after unblinding."

**8. Block-6 §12.4, jw:docs/registrations/block6_replication_DRAFT.md:1170-1173**
"No change to registered arithmetic after any block-6 data exists. A rule of §8 found wrong may be changed while block 6 is blinded, by a dated entry in §17 checked by one executing refuter; it then applies to every session, and the result under the original rule is printed beside it."

**9. ED-RULING item 7, jw:docs/process_traces/2026-10-27-l9-restart/ED-RULING.md:75-77**
"Where the block-6 registration itself requires a synthetic stage chain before its blind run, that requirement stands until amended by a dated entry under its §17 rules."

**10. Codex effort tiers, jw:.claude/skills/codex/SKILL.md:24-32**
"The lead may not raise or lower a ruled tier on its own authority."

**11. D-184 addendum, jw:docs/decision_log.md:12177**
"Only hardware, sudo, a notice NO, and publishing claims remain Ed's." So moving orchestration to new hardware (the Air) is Ed's call, already offered by him.

**12. Bridge contract**
jw:docs/contracts/bridge_protocol.md:1-25 has no separate amendment clause. Versions are co-designed by the lead and Sol and adjudicated by the lead (v1 → v1.1). Changing it is a process_rule_change under item 1's 'process wording'.

**13. BYTES**
No general amendment clause was found by reading. bytes:docs/registrations/bytes_pack_v1.md:450 fixes the pre-session gate order (whole suite on the laptop, then the registration cold gate, then commit, then smoke). Changing that order is a dated addendum (INFERRED from the Addendum 1-9 pattern, RUN_STATE item 58).
