science.segment: Process gates: reviews, cold gates, councils, CI, and placement (measurement Mac / cloud / MacBook Air)
science.lens: SCIENCE-PROTECTION SKEPTIC: for each non-KEEP verdict, a realistic path from adopting the proposal to a wrong, unsupported or non-reproducible printed number or claim

judgments.reason: Granting the module, its tests and every registry it joins up front is reasonable. The redundancy claim is too narrow, though. The freeze test (MG-23) covers only block-5 sealed files: registration, plan, catalog, identity pins, sizing, and the run_campaign/reduce/fiducial/adapter/harvest singles. ESTIMATOR_CODE_PATHS is four files. Neither covers BYTES pack flag_effects (registered 10-25) or block-6 catalogs and packs. G09 also proposes shrinking blocking repin to ESTIMATOR_CODE_PATHS. With both changes, nothing blocks a granted build seat from editing a registered exclusion effect.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: A BYTES build seat is granted 'every registry it joins', which includes a pack's flag_effects. It changes a code from DISCLOSE to EXCLUDE_WINDOW, or back. This is the same kind of effect as cell.below_minimum's EXCLUDE_WINDOW that #416 had to correct. Under G09, repin is advisory for non-estimator pins, and the block-5 freeze test does not list BYTES packs. The plan_tree sidecar is written from the current bytes, so it does not catch the change either (INFERRED). The registered exclusion changes after registration with no blocking check. Condition: the tight fence must explicitly list every registered pack, catalog, flag_effects, sizing and registration file of BYTES and block 6, not only the estimator files.

judgments.reason: A malformed envelope that still sits at the end of the output already shows the body was not truncated. The proposal keeps a missing body or missing envelope as failure, and it adds the lead's own diff read and replay. I cannot find a number-changing path, provided 'complete body' is defined mechanically: an envelope-shaped final line is present and only its JSON is malformed.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: Only if 'complete body' is judged by eye: a truncated reviewer report with no diff to replay (findings 4-6 cut off) could be accepted as 'no further findings'. That is closed if FLAGGED status requires the envelope line to be present as the final line.

judgments.reason: Merging the review with the cold pass has precedent (pr501-gates.md:13-14), and the parallel launch is sound. However, the merge cuts the claim-code seat count from three (one review plus two cold passes) to two. MG-4 lists W catches made by review seats (C11, C12, C37, C59, C63). MG-5 lists W catches made by a cold pass after review (C66, an Opus sign error). So different seats caught different W defects. Nothing shows that two blind cold passes cover what the mutation-probing review caught. 7a decision 2 also explicitly kept 'the two-model final look on the L9 code at merge'.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: On estimator or counting code, the two merged seats both miss a defect that a mutation-probing review would have found, of the C59/C63 kind. The dropped seat was the only one that ran mutations. Condition: the merged seats' brief must carry row 1's probe-and-mutation mandate. Any fix commit after the parallel launch still gets a final-head delta pass.

judgments.reason: Rule (b), 'replay over every real archive shows it cannot occur', would have discarded a real, session-killing HIGH in the very chain cited as waste. In #416 round 4, Opus found that 'every BYTES smoke stops at export', and the dispositions state: 'The 25-archive replay missed it because no BYTES smoke exists on disk yet'. Round 6's Opus HIGH (the smoke depends on the results-clone, so the packs are held) was also a stop of every smoke. Both are the same S-class as the s1-p1 loss that the auditor values in G13. A stopping rule (item 26: no finding above LOW) was already applied at rounds 6-7, so 'rounds 4-7 found no number' overstates what the late rounds produced. Rule (b) also ends the chain without naming where the question goes, which orchestration.md:97-101 and D-186 forbid.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: A delta finding concerns an input class that no existing archive contains: smoke archives, a future pack, a storage fault. Replay over the 25 archives shows 0 stops, so the chain ends. The first BYTES smoke, or the first counting session, then stops or silently drops references. With the round-2/3 class (unauthenticated roster: allowance 0.8726 to 1.0123 J, nothing printed), that is a printed-number change. Keep the existing rule ('same class twice goes to a consult'; stop at no finding above LOW). Treat 'cannot occur on real records' as a valid reason only when every input class the finding names exists among the replayed archives.
evidence_refs: jw:docs/process_traces/2026-10-24-magistrate-7209d1b0/DISPOSITIONS-416.md (Round-4 table: Opus 1 HIGH, '25-archive replay missed it')

judgments.reason: Keeping two families for counting, exclusion, estimator and claim code is right. The proposed single-family category, 'watchdog, mailer, loop plumbing, notices', includes code whose defects contaminate measured joules. PR #500 MAJOR-1 was a watchdog defect: a running magistrate was never stood down for an installed-only block-6 plan, so an agent could load a window. PR #501's two-family split, where each family caught a MAJOR the other missed, was on loop and verdict-writer code. The auditor also says the ledger's 'N/A' text already allows a lighter row 4. That is wrong: orchestration.md TIER-01 item 3 allows row-4 N/A only when every Impact line is No, and a full-tier PR with any Yes needs row 4.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: A watchdog or loop change is classed as 'plumbing' and gets one family. That family misses a stand-down gap of the MAJOR-1 kind. An agent then runs during a span, and the session's phase energies include agent load. The census may catch it (P-protective), or the run may count. Condition: two families for anything that touches the census, stand-down, arm checks or admission. Single family only for the mailer, notices and text.

judgments.reason: CI runs on pull_request with actions/checkout@v5 and no ref override, so it tests the merge ref, as the auditor inferred (ci.yml:3-5,19-21). But every job is ubuntu-latest. The proposal sends only 'collector, driver, loop, harvest, hazards' to the macOS run. It leaves out analysis code that runs on the measurement Mac: the L9 dry run, the independent recompute, and the parallel steps 1-2 that the cadence plan proposes with a spawn-context pool. Linux CI exercises fork defaults and its own filesystem and plistlib paths. The Air is also not shown to match the measurement Mac's pinned macOS and Python environment (b5-fixed-env.zsh).
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: Cadence-plan item 2.2 lands a process pool in dry_run.py. Linux CI is green under fork semantics. The macOS spawn path is first exercised in the real blind dry run, where it either refuses (costing a Mac hold) or reorders the record assembly in a way the serial-equals-parallel digest test on Linux never saw. Condition: macOS whole-suite rows also cover Mac-run analysis code, and the Air's Python and macOS are pinned to the measurement environment.

judgments.reason: Rebalancing shards and regenerating timings leaves CI blocking and the test content unchanged. I find no path to a wrong number.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: None found. The only risk is a split that silently drops a module from every shard. A shard-coverage assertion (the union of shards equals the module list) closes it.

judgments.reason: Making docs freshness, gen_state and histsem advisory is safe. Restricting blocking repin to ESTIMATOR_CODE_PATHS (four files) is not. The MG-13 analysis dates from 2026-10-14, before the block-6 registration (10-17) and the BYTES registration (10-25), whose pack, catalog and sizing digests are pinned artifacts. The cited redundancy, the L9 freeze test, covers block-5 files only.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: A later lane edits a registered BYTES pack config or a block-6 catalog. Repin is advisory, so CI is green and the merge goes through. The registered exclusion or estimator input differs from its registered digest, and nothing blocks before the next counting session uses it. Condition: blocking repin keeps every registered-artifact digest (block-5 seal, block-6 S-1 pin artifacts, BYTES registration and packs), not only the four estimator files.

judgments.reason: Auto-filling the ledger and making the format checker advisory is safe. Renewing TIER-01 'on a recorded escape count of zero' is not supported. tier01_defect_log.md has a header and no rows, and it was last touched by the 09-29 prune commit. Yet October had several material post-merge defects: the MT1 sidecar and agent.presence defects, the MT2 busy veto, s1-p1's sidecars, and cell.below_minimum on main. None was logged with its PR's tier. So the zero is an unmaintained log, not a measured count. 'Watcher' in the widened light tier is also ambiguous: watchdog code is hazard code (see G06).
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: TIER-01 is renewed on the empty log. One of October's unlogged defects actually entered through a light-tier PR, so the rule's own suspension trigger was met and missed. Later number-touching changes keep merging with no review. Condition: before renewal, attribute each October post-merge defect to its PR's tier. Keep watchdog, census and arm code out of the light tier.

judgments.reason: Making the real-loop smoke on committed bytes mandatory is right. But running it 'right after the registration commit, in parallel with the registration cold gate' contradicts 'committed pack bytes, never a staged copy'. Registration gates return ADMIT-WITH-CORRECTIONS, and the corrections create a new commit: BYTES was registered at 6731d5249 after its gate's corrections. A smoke on the pre-correction commit has the same escape class as s1-p1, a smoke on bytes other than the ones the chain reads.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: The smoke passes on the pre-gate commit. The gate's corrections change a pack file or sidecar. The first counting session reads the corrected bytes and refuses or empties, which is the s1-p1 loss again. Condition: the smoke is bound to the exact final registered pin's digest, and it reruns if any pack byte changes after it.

judgments.reason: The four-model council never ran, and orchestration.md:105 already limits it to when Ed asks. Deleting stale text changes no number.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: None found.

judgments.reason: The executing refuter does have the W catches, while cold judges have none in three periods. But the same OP-3 row records that 'blind Opus re-rulings were never worse and better in 2 to 4 of 10'. That is evidence that a blind second ruler improves rulings, and the proposal hands the ruling to the orchestrator's one line. The orchestrator carries loop context, so the anti-sunk-cost property is gone. A refuter attacks; it does not rule. The proposal convenes a judge only on a council split, not when the refuter and the orchestrator disagree.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: A rule change that decides which BYTES references count (like the #416 'uncollected' exception) is ruled by the orchestrator, who wants the session to run. The refuter's executed objection is overruled in one line, with no blind ruler to break the tie, and a counted-set rule is adopted that a blind ruler would have rejected. Condition: when the refuter's executed result contradicts the orchestrator's line on a counting or exclusion rule, a blind executing judge rules.

judgments.reason: Two-judge raw re-derivation stays where the catches occurred, which is good. But turning whole-file gates into one judge plus one refuter loses family diversity on text that defines estimators and exclusions. Text-code divergence (cell.below_minimum, where §6 said 'never stops a stage' and the code excluded the session; the NEG-8 'request' span) is a number class. The 'diff since the #416 audit' shortcut is unsafe because the audit head (c84bb34c2) and the registered head (6731d5249) are separated by seven fix rounds that changed number code (span, meter gap, bars). The auditor's own record says those rows were re-derived at c84bb34c2, not at the registered head.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: The registration gate reviews only the text plus the diff. A fix-round change between the audit head and the registered head alters a sizing input, for example the meter-gap rule or an agreement bar. The diff is reviewed as code, not re-derived against the registered rows, so a registered value no longer matches what the code computes. Condition: a diff-only gate is allowed when the audit's re-derived values are re-executed (a script, not a seat) at the registered head. Keep two families on sections that define estimators, exclusions or sizing.
evidence_refs: jw:docs/process/pruning_list_2026-10-14.md (MG-27: 73 text/code mismatches, one reached a number)

judgments.reason: The reason given for dropping the third seat, that Astra missed the key blocker, ignores what only Astra found. The dispositions credit two number-touching fixes to Astra alone. A3: numeric predictors were not bound to the manifest, and doubling W moved BW from 266 to 475 GB/s with no flag. A4: agreement bars were looser than §12, and mutations passed under the bar. The auditor's own summary lists A3 among the audit's catches.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: With only Fable and Opus at the next frozen-head audit, a defect of the A3 or A4 class goes unseen. Unbound predictors let a wrong model block silently change printed bandwidth, and loose agreement bars let a recompute disagreement pass as agreement. Keep three seats. Pairing with the G13 smoke and applying G05's existing stopping rule are fine.

judgments.reason: The fence is kept, and disabling the Codex daemon and auto-updater on the measurement Mac removes a known contender (item 78). This adds protection.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: None from this step itself. See G21 for the off-Mac orchestration gap.

judgments.reason: Today the span fence works because the magistrate runs on the Mac under a watchdog that refuses its launch during spans and stands down its process tree (MAGISTRATE_WATCHDOG.md:34-36,103,149). An orchestrator running continuously on the Air is outside that supervision. The watchdog cannot stand it down. Its ssh, rsync or scripted 'short calls' on the Mac are not agent processes, so the agent census may not see them (INFERRED: the census is agent-targeted). The auditor's open question asks only whether the census will wrongly refuse remote execution, not whether it will fail to detect it.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: During SESSION_RUN, the Air orchestrator runs a desk script, a git fetch, or the G12 archive copy (33-36 GiB of H read through rsync) on the Mac. No agent process exists, so the census stays empty and the session continues. The measured phase energies include I/O and CPU load from the transfer, with no flag. Condition: a Mac-side span lock owned by launchd that refuses every remote command, and a census pattern for sshd children and rsync, before the move.

judgments.reason: Real-archive replays stay, and running them on the Air on hash-verified non-claim copies is fine.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: Only through placement: copying the archives off the Mac is heavy I/O and must be scheduled outside PRECHECK..SESSION_RUN (see G21). Also, a replay set without smoke-shaped archives missed #416's round-4 HIGH.

judgments.reason: Moving the fallback seats off the measurement Mac removes disk churn and the risk of a seat overlapping PRECHECK. Seats touch no measured bytes.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: None found that touches a number.

judgments.reason: Launching the Fable and Opus passes early and in parallel is allowed (ED-RULING item 3). Counting them as item 1's executing review drops a seat on the code that prints the numbers, and it changes Ed's binding ruling, which lists 'one executing review' as a merge condition. L9's history has W catches from both seat types: C59 and C63 by review, C66 (a sign error) by a cold pass after review. The downstream check does not fully cover this code either: the recompute takes 'selection, anchors, timing bounds and calibration fits' as input judgments (independent_recompute_b5.py:4-5). L9 code also keeps changing after 'modules green': the physics_cache wiring, parallel steps 1-2, the evidence for the step-9b condition, and blind dry-run cures.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: The early cold passes review the L9-2 head. A later number-bearing change, such as the step-1/2 process pool or a dry-run R3 cure, lands with only CI. No seat probes how it assembles kept-unit records, so an ordering or selection defect reaches the release. The recompute treats the selection as input and does not flag it. Condition: keep a separate executing review, or a final-head delta pass on every later number-bearing commit.

judgments.reason: 'The recompute re-derives every printed quantity' is not verified, and parts of it are false. (1) Some printed lines are computed only by the recompute, so the recompute is their only computation: 7a decision 1's 'including three BETA sessions' line (BETA_INCLUSIVE_LABEL), the scaled-allowance sensitivity, and the F5 reconstruction diagnostic. A grep of l9:joulewise/b5_analysis finds none of them. Step 12 would be their only second derivation. (2) Neither the L9 nor the recompute worktree contains a program that compares L9 outputs to recompute outputs. The recompute's agrees() checks only against stored archive values, so the 'comparison table' a reviewer would read does not exist yet. (3) The sealed block-5 plan never names the recompute; its bars come from the FIX-571 docstring and from block-6 S-13. (4) Step 12 covers rendered paper fills, which the recompute does not produce.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: After release, the recompute alone prints the BETA-inclusive floor line, or the scaled-allowance sensitivity. A defect in that recompute-only code, for example the extra-session pooling, prints a wrong labelled number. Step 12 has been cut, and the reviewer reads a comparison table with no row for that line. Condition: replace step 12 with one executing seat that runs a blind-written mechanical comparator mapping every placement to an agreeing recompute row or issued field, and that independently computes the recompute-only lines.
evidence_refs: jw:docs/process/pruning_list_2026-10-14.md:539 (7a decision 1: computed by the recompute only)

judgments.reason: §13 requires full-size production-shaped synthetic testing, an executing review, and Fable plus Opus cold passes. The proposal keeps a full-size known-answer run (once per release candidate) and both families, and it changes only frequency and seriality, through the §17 route that ED-RULING item 7 names. Silent mis-pairing or a wrong replication word is still caught by the full-size known-answer run. The blind dry run catches only refusals.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: None found, provided the full-size run and the two cold passes are on the exact S-14 analysis pin. Block-6 §12.3's 'no separate cold gate' rests on these passes ('has had its two executing cold passes at merge (§13)'), so the §17 entry must keep them.

judgments.reason: Block-6 §12.3 explicitly says there is no separate cold gate. The block-5 sealed §8 item 3 asks only that 'the lead records a release event'. The RUN_STATE history that says the release is 'taken only through a cold gate (registration section 8 item 3)' misreads that clause. I cannot construct a number path from removing the scout's added gate.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: No number path. Authority caveat: the scout attributes the gate to 'the current user's' instruction. If that was Ed, cutting it needs his ruling (his 10-27 principle likely covers it), not a lead line. It also depends on G25 keeping the §13 cold passes.

judgments.reason: The proposal runs the recompute and the dry run sequentially within one hold, which avoids tripping L9's 120 s wall deadline. The recompute is stdlib-only and reads the same bytes. Nothing changes what is computed.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: None if the runs are sequential. Concurrent runs could fire the step-9b deadline, which ED-RULING item 6 treats as a tooling refusal, so they cost time, not a wrong number.

judgments.reason: A fixed tally table and a collector script only produce proposals to Ed. They delete nothing.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: Indirect: if the table has only 'caught_number y/n', it will mark session-killing catches as 'no', for example #416's round-4 and round-6 HIGHs and the machine-test catches, and so propose deleting the gates that make them. Add a 'caught_session_refusal' column.

missed_items: Some printed lines have no second derivation at all. The BETA-inclusive line (7a decision 1), the scaled-allowance sensitivity and the F5 reconstruction diagnostic are computed only in scripts/independent_recompute_b5.py. Grep finds none of them in l9:joulewise/b5_analysis. Whatever replaces step 12 must re-derive them.

No program comparing L9 outputs with recompute outputs exists in the L9 or recompute worktrees (grep), and the sealed block-5 plan never names the recompute. The block-5 release condition (7a decision 2: agreement 'within a tolerance fixed before release') needs a blind-written, reviewed comparator, and its bars fixed in a dated record, before the dry run. The scout also found no block-6 comparison (scout:31).

jw:docs/process/tier01_defect_log.md was never updated after 09-29, although October had material post-merge defects (the MT1 and s1-p1 sidecars, the MT2 busy veto, cell.below_minimum on main). The empty log is non-maintenance, not zero escapes. Each October defect needs its PR's tier attributed before TIER-01 is renewed.

Moving orchestration off the Mac moves remote commands outside the watchdog's stand-down and the agent census (ssh, rsync, archive copies for Air replays). A Mac-side span lock is needed that refuses remote work during PRECHECK..SESSION_RUN.

The pruning list's MG-13 and MG-23 analysis (10-14) predates the block-6 (10-17) and BYTES (10-25) registrations. 'Keep only the estimator pins' leaves their registered packs, catalogs and flag_effects without a blocking digest check.

#416 rounds 4 and 6 each found a HIGH that would stop every BYTES smoke. Round 4's was missed by the 25-archive real replay because no smoke archive existed. 'Real replay shows it cannot occur' is valid only when the replay set contains every input class the finding names.

Astra found number-touching defects in #416 that Fable and Opus missed (A3, unbound predictors; A4, loose agreement bars). That is evidence for family diversity in pre-arm audits, against the 'third family missed the blocker' argument.

Linux-only CI (ubuntu-latest) plus the cadence plan's macOS spawn-context pool for dry-run steps 1-2: the serial-equals-parallel digest test must also run on macOS, on the Air pinned to the measurement environment, before the real dry run.

cadence.segment: Process gates: reviews, cold gates, councils, CI, and where orchestration runs (measurement Mac, cloud, MacBook Air). Read-only verification. Paths: jw: = scratchpad/jw, l9:, bytes:, recompute: = scratchpad/wt/recompute, scout: = scratchpad/wt/scout/.codex-report/BLIND-DRY-RUN-SCOUT.md.
cadence.lens: CADENCE SKEPTIC. Each KEEP was checked against two questions: does it protect a printed number, and does a cheaper form exist that gives the same protection (a script, one round, parallel, earlier, off the measurement Mac, cloud first)? Every proposal was also checked for whether it goes far enough. agree=true means the auditor's verdict stands.

judgments.reason: Verified against OP-11. It is R only on the estimator files, has no number catch elsewhere, and cost 12 of 47 L9 seats a stop of 30-60 min each. Granting the module, its tests and its registries up front is the right cheaper form. The tight fence on ESTIMATOR_CODE_PATHS is what protects numbers. The ED-RULING item 6 shows why: the last edit to powermetrics_fiducial.py forced a calibration reissue.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: Without the tight estimator fence, a build seat could edit powermetrics_fiducial.py or reduce.py. That changes the governed pins and silently changes the calibration digests.

judgments.reason: OP-12 shows no catch, and K19 shows rc=65 on every consult while the bodies were complete. The lead's diff read and replay are the real protection. Flagging a malformed envelope with a complete body is enough. Accepting the work should still require the lead's executed replay, as proposed.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: If even a missing body were accepted, a truncated seat run could be read as 'done'. The proposal keeps that case a failure.

judgments.reason: It does not protect a printed number directly. It protects cadence: a broken module is caught in minutes on the seat instead of after a CI round that takes up to ~150 min because of shard 10 (8b6b2b12 item 9). Nothing cheaper exists, since it is already a script on the seat's own VM.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: Without it, a seat hands back a tree that fails the quick tier. The lead then spends a full CI cycle of about 150 min before the fix loop restarts.

judgments.reason: MG-4 is the main R mechanism and has W catches. Merging it with G06 into one parallel stage of two blind executing seats keeps both family views. PR #501 had each family catch a different MAJOR, and two seats still do. Block-6 §12.3 justifies having no release cold gate by the 'two executing cold passes at merge (§13)', and the merged stage still provides exactly that.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: Two serial stages add 30-90 min per full-tier merge with no added protection. The seats are the same kind, so the second sees what the first would have seen.

judgments.reason: The 7209d1b0 tally confirms it: rounds 1-3 touched numbers, and later rounds were 'edge cases ... No number'. The proposal should go further in two ways. (1) Rule (a) already exists: orchestration.md:97-99 sends the same defect class failing twice to a consult. The gap is that nobody applied it on #416, so (a) needs enforcement, not new text. (2) Turn every delta-round probe into a committed regression test. The next round's check is then 'tests plus the scripted archive replay (G12)', and a fresh seat is launched only when a fix touches a new code path. Under D-186 and orchestration.md:99-101, rule (b) must name where the question goes when it fires (the lead's disposition, or Ed). A clause that just says 'stop' is not valid.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: Without a written stop, #416-style chains run 4 or more extra rounds: about 5 h wall time and 8 seats, with no number changed. That sits on the critical path to the first counting session.

judgments.reason: Same as G04. Two families for counting, exclusion, estimator and claim code is supported by #501 (each family caught a MAJOR the other missed) and by L9 C66 (Opus only). One family for non-claim full-tier code is allowed by the ledger's row-4 N/A text.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: With only one family on claim code, a sign error like L9 C66 or a #501-type MAJOR goes uncaught into counting code.

judgments.reason: Row 2 can be met by green PR CI. The proposal does not go far enough on 'cloud first', though. Every CI job runs on ubuntu-latest and there is no macOS job, so the macOS parity leg can be a GitHub-hosted Apple Silicon macOS runner job in ci.yml, run in the cloud and in parallel with Linux CI. The Air then becomes the fallback (for example, for tests needing sudo or powermetrics). Merge-ref testing is plausible: the pull_request trigger and actions/checkout with no ref override give the merge commit by default. That is INFERRED from GitHub's default behaviour, not from repo text. The cost of macOS runner minutes on a private repo is INFERRED to be higher.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: A macOS-only failure (zsh path, launchd plist, APFS clone behaviour) passes Linux CI and first shows up on the measurement Mac at arm. That costs an arm cycle of about 1 h 10 min, as in the H arm refusals.

judgments.reason: Shard 10 at about 150 min is confirmed. CI rounds sit on every fix loop, so rebalancing is the largest single wall-time saving in this segment. It stays blocking because it is the R evidence for rows 2 and 3.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: Every fix round on a PR waits about 2.5 h for one shard. Over a 7-round chain like #416, that is most of a day.

judgments.reason: MG-13, 16, 17 and 18 have no catches. Keeping only the estimator pins and the strict mock smoke as blocking checks keeps the number protection. Dropping test_docs_freshness from L9's list changes an Ed-ruled list (ED-RULING:30-32). The lead already amended item 1 the same day under Ed's principle (ED-RULING:35), so the same route works. Record it in one line.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: Docs-only PRs stay red until format sections are added (item 58). That blocks unrelated merges and the L9 acceptance on a check that guards ruling formats, not numbers.

judgments.reason: The lapse is verified. tier01_defect_log.md has a header and no rows, and the last decision-log entry is D-186 at line 12228 (09-29). TIER-01 item 5 makes continuation depend on a recorded decision. Recording it takes one line. The Yes-to-full refusal is the only part that routes number changes, and it stays blocking.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: Read literally, TIER-01 is not continued, so every PR since 10-25 is full tier. That forces audit rounds onto docs and record PRs.

judgments.reason: It is cheap and rare, and it has W catches historically (MG-6: C20). One condition matters for cadence: it must not sit on either release path. Block 5 releases from the tagged L9 merge (7a decision 5), and block 6 from the S-14 pin (§13). So the later L9 + block-6 + BYTES wave onto main changes no Paper A number. Run it as one seat in parallel with merged-tree CI, never as a release precondition.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: If it is placed before the block-5 or block-6 release, a merge-topology question (the #515 hold) delays printed numbers that do not depend on main.

judgments.reason: The protection stays, because only real-archive replays caught over-refusal of real data (7209d1b0 tally). The cheaper form is a fixed-manifest 'replay every non-claim archive' command, not a lead-performed step. The Air placement is also out of date. H and BY-H2 are already off the Mac, offloaded to iCloud with per-member SHA-256 manifests (7209d1b0 items 33-34). They are non-claim, so blinding does not restrict them, and they compress about 70x (cadence plan §3). The replay can therefore run in a cloud seat as part of every delta round. That makes G05's stopping rule (b) cheap and continuous. Use the Air only if the restored size exceeds cloud disk (H is 33 GiB raw against about 30 GB for a Claude seat).
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: If the replay stays a manual lead step, each rule change waits for the lead and restored disk. Rounds then either skip the replay, so over-refusals like 'H's uncollected references' reach a session, or serialize behind it.

judgments.reason: Right direction, but it does not go far enough. (1) The fix for s1-p1 (991358f73) added a test that reads every loop pack through _plan_tree (item 71). Extended to load every registered pack exactly as the chain does, it puts the s1-p1 class into CI continuously, for free. (2) The 8b6b2b12 record itself says the controller refusing on a missing sidecar is a records check that 'should be a flag' under the 10-05 doctrine. Making it a flag removes the session-emptying outcome for this whole class. (3) The non-claim smoke on committed bytes can run first on the Air (same OS and architecture; INFERRED that driver, loop and harvest run there without the USB-C meter). Only the short arm rehearsal then needs the measurement Mac.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: A registered-pack bytes defect empties a 313-388 min chain slot, as s1-p1 did with 143 refused runs, after every review passed.

judgments.reason: It touches numbers: the 70B thermal question decides which units count, and H-DISK sized a rule to refuse 0 of 9 good sessions. Councils are already two parallel cloud seats of 10-30 min each. The only lighter form is to require executed evidence for every factual premise, as M1 did on s5-p1 in item 78, which is mostly current practice.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: Without a council, an exclusion question like the post-request thermal tail is decided by one seat. That could drop 10 units of a 70B cell on a wrong physical reading.

judgments.reason: It never ran. orchestration.md:104-105 already limits it to 'only when Ed asks', so cutting it only removes stale skill text. Do it with the next skill edit. It costs nothing on the critical path.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: Seats loading the stale skill text may convene four models on major changes and burn usage.

judgments.reason: 7a decision 3 (pruning_list:541) was decided on 10-14 and is still not reflected in orchestration.md:83-94. Install it as one edit. OP-3 has no W catch, and only the executing form (OP-2) has W catches.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: Rule changes keep paying 1-3 h judge cycles (OP-3, OP-5) that produce no W catch.

judgments.reason: Value-level catches (S-8, c_q) came only from the acceptance judges' raw re-derivation. Whole-file gates gave text only. Limiting the two-judge raw re-derivation to measured-value and exclusion slots keeps the protection.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: The BYTES sizing rows are re-derived a 4th time at the registration gate after #416 had already done so, adding hours before the first t0.

judgments.reason: Two executing seats keep the families that found NEG-8, since Astra missed it (7209d1b0 tally). Pairing it with the real-loop smoke covers the escape class it missed. ed_ruling is the correct authority because it is owner directive #416.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: A third highest-effort seat that adds no catch, plus serial late delta rounds, delays the first BYTES session by about 2 days.

judgments.reason: It is a physical hazard (battery assist hides DC input from the meter) and an automatic in-loop check. Nothing about it is cheaper or more parallel. The recompute also flags meter_battery_activity independently (independent_recompute_b5.py:53, 1490).
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: Battery-assisted runs undercount DC-input energy, and the measured joules for those runs are wrong.

judgments.reason: It is a real physical hazard and was correct every time. Go further. Item 78 shows the s6-p1 contender came from an interactive `codex update` run on the measurement Mac at 09:35 during a session, and the fence then waited 2 h before ending. Two one-command mitigations: (a) a wrapper on the Mac that refuses to launch codex or claude while the loop is in PRECHECK..SESSION_RUN; (b) INFERRED, a governed collection change: classify a contender that is reparented to launchd and persistent so the session ends at once instead of after a 2 h pause. Then the Mac is freed for the retry sooner. The Air move removes the source.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: A human or agent runs Codex on the measurement Mac mid-session. The session idles 2 h and is then lost, as s6-p1 was on 10-27.

judgments.reason: Moving the orchestrator off the Mac is right, but the Air is not the cloud-first choice. Item 77 shows the orchestrator already ran as a cloud Claude session (015ASG1T, 'off the Mac') and launched the L9-2 cloud seat. Item 39 names only one blocker to off-Mac orchestration: Ed's ChatGPT login for the Codex Cloud launcher. So the orchestrator should run in Claude cloud, with continuity INFERRED from scheduled cloud routines. The Air's role narrows to (1) holding the ChatGPT login and relaying Sol launches through codex-cloud-run.mjs, and (2) running local Sol fallback seats. For Mac-touching steps, use a pull model, not inbound ssh: the Mac's existing launchd watchdog polls a git ref or flag for 'arm', 'desk' or 'ack'. That avoids the open question of whether the census counts sshd children, and puts no agent process on the Mac.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: With the magistrate on the Air plus ssh into the Mac, either the census counts the remote session as an agent and refuses arms, or it is taught to ignore ssh and weakens the quiet-Mac protection. The Air also has a single point of failure (lid closed, sleep).

judgments.reason: Verified that seat scratch on the Mac pinned 53 GiB of APFS clones while free disk was 33 GiB (7209d1b0 item 34). Disk is the Mac's binding constraint, given about 43 GiB per collected session (cadence plan §1), so moving the fallback to the Air is justified. The 2-seat capacity is INFERRED.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: Local seat scratch fills the Mac's disk ahead of a session or the dry run's fresh custody root, and that refuses the dry run or the session.

judgments.reason: ED-RULING:48-49 already allows the cold passes to run in parallel with the dry run. Launching them as soon as L9-2's modules are green, and counting them as item 1's executing review, removes a serial seat and takes the cold passes off the dry-run-to-release path. It is consistent with Ed's 'asap'. Pair this with launching the recompute early (see G27).
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: If the cold passes run only after the dry run, a blocker they find forces a fix, a new pin and a rerun of the Mac dry run (hours of Mac time) that an earlier pass would have avoided.

judgments.reason: The proposal can go further. The 'one reviewer reading the recompute's comparison table' is itself a model step with no added protection. The comparison is a script with registered bars, and step 11's --validate-rendered already checks rendering. The recompute covers descriptive estimates and disclosures, not only phase energies (independent_recompute_b5.py:1187, 1860, 2386-2495), so step 12 has no unique coverage. The amendment must also change plan §1 item 4 (lines 63-64, 'handed to the results cold gate before any paper sentence is filled'), not only the step-12 row.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: If only row 12 is amended, §1 item 4 still requires a results cold gate. That leaves a 'days per round' gate on the release-to-paper path.

judgments.reason: Agreed. One coupling: §12.3 justifies having no release cold gate by the cold passes being 'at merge (§13)'. The auditor's version keeps them at merge, as one parallel stage, so it stays consistent. The cadence plan's variant (§5, cold passes moved to before release) would also need a §17 change to the §12.3 sentence. Write both together in one dated §17 entry with one executing refuter.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: If §13 is amended but §12.3 is not, the registration contradicts itself on the release condition. That invites a later gate or an erratum at release time.

judgments.reason: The substance holds: block-6 §12.3 and 7a decision 2 both rule out a release cold gate. The authority does not. scout:206 says the gate follows 'the current user's release cold-gate requirement'. If that user was Ed, a lead_ruling cannot cut it. It needs Ed's one-line confirmation, which is cheap and can ride the next email. Until then, block-5 and block-6 releases risk an extra gate cycle each.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: The lead cuts a gate Ed asked for, and the release record is later disputed. Or nobody cuts it, and two releases each wait for a packet, a judge and a refuter.

judgments.reason: Keep it: it is the one independent check. But the placement does not go far enough. The recompute uses only the standard library, takes the calibration fits as inputs instead of refitting (header, lines 1-6), and a grep found no wall deadline or timeout. So the 120 s step-9b deadline does not apply to it, and it shares no code with L9. Its CLI takes per-pack archives, exclusions and claim/bound run lists (lines 2591-2603). INFERRED, not verified: those are harvest-side artifacts, not L9 outputs. If so, the real recompute can run now, in restricted custody on the Mac during a collection gap, before L9 even merges. When the dry run finishes, release is then a comparison and not another Mac compute. Running it concurrently with the dry run is still unwise because step 9b is load-sensitive.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: If the recompute runs serially after the dry run, it adds its full runtime to the Mac hold that pauses BYTES. That pushes s1-p1 toward the 2026-11-02 registered end (ED-RULING 6a).

judgments.reason: A fixed tally table plus a script fits the evidence: the 10-14 deletions went unapplied for 13 days (7a decisions 3 and 6 are still not installed). The script is cheap and closes that drift.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: Decided deletions keep imposing cost because nobody applies them. G16 and G10 are current examples.

judgments.reason: It takes seconds. Orphan fixtures add measured load, and a leaked hazard_monitor inflated c_q (item 42). No cheaper form exists. Extending it to the Air is fine.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: An orphaned fixture runs during a session and adds joules or contention flags. c_q is biased.

missed_items: CI has no macOS job: every runs-on in ci.yml is ubuntu-latest (lines 17,37,99,135,235,273,323,342). A GitHub-hosted Apple Silicon macOS runner job would give row-2 platform parity in the cloud, in parallel with Linux CI, per Ed's 'as much in the cloud as possible'. The Air is the fallback. macOS minute cost is INFERRED.

The independent recompute is off L9's critical path. It uses only the standard library, has no wall deadline found by grep, and takes calibration fits as inputs (recompute:scripts/independent_recompute_b5.py:1-17,2591-2603). Its real run can be done now in restricted custody during a collection gap. Release then waits only on the dry run plus a comparison. Whether its inputs are harvest-side artifacts and not L9 outputs is INFERRED.

The non-claim archives H and BY-H2 are already off the Mac, in iCloud with per-member SHA-256 manifests (jw:docs/process_traces/2026-10-24-magistrate-7209d1b0/RECORD.md:100-104). Lead replays (G12) should therefore run in a cloud seat or on the Air from those copies, as a scripted step of every delta round, not on the Mac.

Records-check refusals: the 8b6b2b12 record (line 28) says the controller refusing on a missing sidecar 'should be a flag' under the 10-05 doctrine. Making records checks flag rather than refuse removes the session-emptying failure mode at its source. It is a governed collection change, best done blind before the s1-p1 retry if cheap.

Continuous rehearsal: fix 991358f73 added a CI test reading every loop pack through _plan_tree (jw:RUN_STATE.md:265). Generalize it to 'load every registered pack exactly as the chain does', so the s1-p1 class is caught on every push, not by a Mac smoke.

Orchestrator placement should be cloud first. Item 77 shows a cloud Claude session already orchestrating off the Mac. Item 39's only stated blocker is the ChatGPT login for Sol launches, which the Air can hold as a relay.
Mac-touching steps from off the Mac should use a pull model: the Mac's launchd watchdog polls a git ref or flag. Inbound ssh is avoided, so the open census question disappears.

A launch guard on the measurement Mac: a wrapper that refuses to run codex or claude while the loop is in PRECHECK..SESSION_RUN. Item 78's loss came from an interactive `codex update` run mid-session.

Mac disk is a cadence gate that nobody owns. Free disk was 33 GiB pending eviction (7209d1b0 item 34) against about 43 GiB per collected session (cadence plan line 15). A dry-run tooling refusal restarts in a fresh custody root (ED-RULING:64). Budget disk before holding the BYTES loop for the dry run.
G05 rule (b) must name where the question goes when it fires (orchestration.md:99-101; D-186), or under Ed's own 09-29 decision it reads as an invalid 'stop for good' clause.
Turn delta-round probes into committed regression tests, so a re-check after a fix is a test run plus the archive-replay script. A fresh seat is needed only when a fix reaches a new code path.
Authority for G26: scout:206 attributes the release cold gate to 'the current user'. If that was Ed, cutting it needs Ed's one-line confirmation, not a lead ruling.
G24's amendment must also change analysis_plan_block5.md §1 item 4 (lines 63-64), not only the step-12 table row (line 177).
If the cadence plan's §13 variant moves block-6 cold passes from merge to before release, then §12.3's justification for no release gate (lines 1164-1166) must be amended in the same §17 entry.

map.segment: Empirical ledger: what each check, gate, review round, machine test, smoke, cold pass, council and audit actually caught in October 2026 (block-5 tail, block-6 collection, BYTES H/BY-H2/pass 1, L9, #416)
map.summary:
Path prefixes: jw = scratchpad/jw (main); l9 = scratchpad/wt/l9; bytes = scratchpad/wt/bytes. "RS n" is RUN_STATE item n. "PL" is jw:docs/process/pruning_list_2026-10-14.md, the ledger to 10-14 with case IDs C##/K##. I could not read the HISTORY.md behind those IDs (it is in night-archive), so they are cited as PL states them.

Outcome classes: (A) a defect that would have changed a printed number or which data count; (B) would have lost a session or crashed collection or analysis; (C) cosmetic or process only; (D) caught nothing. A check that itself destroyed good data is marked NEG.

Headline, by check type (A/B/C/D, counted over instances I read):
- Executing review by a non-author: A>=8, B>=5. A: 3 from L9 S0-S3 (RS 33), plus C11, C12, C37, C59 and C63 before 10-14 (PL MG-4). B: PR500 MAJOR-1; the BYTES H reservation `--plan` binding; H members sharing the split ledger; mt-fix F1/F2.
- Blind executing cold passes (first rounds): A about 10. Delta cold passes with the same defect class repeating: A falls to 0 after round 3. The #416 tally: rounds 1-3 A, rounds 4-7 B or edge cases only (jw:docs/process_traces/2026-10-24-magistrate-7209d1b0/RECORD.md:106-116).
- Live machine test: 3 runs, A2, B2, C2, D1 (RS 41, 43, 44).
- Real-program rehearsal and real-archive replay: A2, B4 or more, plus the nine S10 defects (PL OP-9 C65). It missed one defect, which cost H's second arm.
- Harvest member exclusions: A on 7 or more sessions.
- Registration cold gates: A2, C2.
- Two-seat councils: one blinding leak (A), one refusal avoided (B), the rest decisions.
- Triple audit: A1, and its third seat added D.

Zero A in October, from the records I read:
- CI whole suite: B1, the rest C.
- Process censuses in CI: C only.
- Physical arm checks: D on 44 frequency reads.
- Smoke: 0 catches, 1 false hold, and it hid the s1-p1 defect.
- Lone cold judges: PL OP-3 says "No W in any period".
- Errata chain, watcher, yield-alert noise.

Checks that destroyed good data or time:
- Stale calibration-acceptance rule: BETA a4 and a5, 12 h (RS 23-24).
- Prospective-only rule: kept BETA a1, a4 and a5 out, about 18 h (PL OP-6).
- Controller sidecar refusal: s1-p1, 265 min, "protected no number" (8b6b2b12 RECORD:40).
- Wrong smoke hold #509 (RS 52).
- Agent presence on the measurement Mac: BETA a2 (RS 16), BY-H2 refused at t0 then 9.5 h idle (0277c5ab RECORD:9), s6-p1 276 min (RS 78), and 2 machine-test installs (RS 40).

Rule the evidence supports: keep everything where a second party executes code or physics against real-shaped data; make every first-round number check two-family and every delta check single-seat with a stopping rule; turn records and census gates into advisory flags. Get agents off the measurement Mac: the MacBook Air should host every interactive and orchestrator session. That alone removes the biggest non-physics cause of lost collection time in October.

steps.name: Physical arm checks (battery and charging, keep-awake and sleep, thermal, disk free-space line, clock and frequency gate, arm-time instrument cadence, pre-arm bracket helper)
steps.what: Seconds-to-minutes checks run before every arm: pmset and caffeinate assertions (RS 19), the battery current limit (#421), the P disk rule (H-DISK-RULING), the frequency word and measured clock rate (7209d1b0 RECORD:7), and the 2-min b5_prearm_bracket helper (RS 26).
steps.protects: Running a session on battery, asleep, thermally limited or with too little disk to finish; clock drift corrupting edges. Real physical hazards.
steps.cost: Seconds; bracket helper about 2 min (RS 26). Over about 40 arms in October (22 block-6 arm records with 44 frequency reads, 7209d1b0 RECORD:7; plus H x3, BY-H2 x2, BYTES x6, block-5 BETA a2-a6 and GAMMA a1).
steps.caught_real_defects: A0. B about 2: the lead's pre-arm physical look found a runaway fseventsd at 100% CPU and a fileproviderd reclaim at 165% (f18a96e1 RECORD:62); both would have held the pre-check. D: the frequency gate never refused in 44 reads and 'never changed a number' (7209d1b0 RECORD:7). All checks PASS and caught nothing at c5a1d8fd RECORD:61-62 and a69c5394 RECORD:34. Miss: the 10-12 iCloud eviction was not caught by the disk check (PL CA-4; RS 34). The sleep check flagged attempt 4, but sleep was later shown not to be the cause (RS 23).
steps.redundant_with: The loop pre-check (E03) re-measures contention and cadence at PRECHECK.
steps.proposal: Keep every check. Fold the hand steps (pmset, ioreg battery, df, caffeinate pid, eviction scan of ledger locators per RS 34) into the loop's pre-arm script so no agent has to be on the Mac to run them. Keep the frequency gate as a recorded value; it already became the measured-rate rule in FIX-416-B (7647bf11a).
steps.saves: About 5-10 min of agent time per arm, and removes one reason an agent is alive on the Mac near t0.

steps.name: Agent census at arm and t0, plus the live agent-pause fence (2 h pause limit)
steps.what: Refuses an arm or pauses a running chain while any `[c]odex|[c]laude` process is alive (joulewise/hazards/arm.py AGENT_CENSUS_ARGV, a46602ae RECORD:5). Members that overlapped an agent are excluded at harvest (agent.presence).
steps.protects: Agent CPU and GPU load inside a measured phase, which outside-CPU flags cannot fully attribute (PL CA-7: HV-17 measures outside CPU only). A real physical contamination.
steps.cost:
Each catch cost the session it caught:
- BETA a2: stopped 2 h 32 min after t0 by a `claude` session at the keyboard (RS 16).
- BY-H2: refused at t0 by open interactive session 8a9fb7fe, then 9.5 h of idle Mac (0277c5ab RECORD:3,9).
- s6-p1: a leftover Codex 0.164 app-server daemon kept the census non-empty, so a 2 h pause, then an abort at 276 min (RS 78; a46602ae RECORD:4,7).
- 2 machine-test installs withdrawn (RS 40 line 85).
- 3 harmless census hits on the courier and watcher (RS 31; a69c5394 RECORD:14).
steps.caught_real_defects: B5. Each was a real contender, and the census was right every time. A: the harvest's member exclusions dropped the agent-overlap units of s6 (a46602ae RECORD:7,16). Root cause in every case: an agent process on the measurement Mac (Ed at the keyboard, an interactive session left open, a `codex update` daemon).
steps.redundant_with: None. The harvest's agent.presence exclusion is the after-the-fact half of the same protection.
steps.proposal:
Keep the check unchanged. Remove the cause:
1. Run every interactive session (Ed's and Claude's), every orchestrator and magistrate activation, and every `codex update` or Codex app session on the MacBook Air or in the cloud, never on the measurement Mac.
2. Add a pre-arm reaper for known daemons, `codex app-server daemon stop` plus SIGTERM to pid-update-loop (RS 78 pointer step 1), to the loop's pre-arm script.
The remaining Mac-side agent is the magistrate wake. Once the Air hosts the orchestrator, the Mac needs only launchd jobs (cf. RS 39 bullet 3: 'continuous coordination would need the orchestrator off the Mac').
steps.saves: In October this would have saved BY-H2's 9.5 h idle interval, s6-p1's 276-min chain plus 35-min harvest, BETA a2's window and 2 machine-test reinstalls: roughly 15-20 h of quiet-Mac time in one month (sum of the cited figures; the overlap with other holds is INFERRED).

steps.name: Loop PRECHECK (180 s clean contention run within 600 s; instrument probe: 300 powermetrics frames, median at most 150 ms)
steps.what: Runs before each block-6 or BYTES session; holds in WAIT_PHYSICS until physics is clean.
steps.protects: Collecting under a background CPU hog or a throttled sampler cadence (250 ms frames instead of 130 ms). Either one corrupts phase edges and energy.
steps.cost: Minutes per session. On 10-17 it held for about 1 h (WAIT_PHYSICS 18:21-19:22) until the causes were fixed (RS 46-47).
steps.caught_real_defects:
B2, physical:
- mediaanalysisd at 1.86-1.91 CPU-s/s against a 0.05 limit (RS 46; 6789ef94 RECORD:8). Without the check this would have been an A, contaminated data.
- The loop's launchd job was `ProcessType Background`, giving 178-237 of 300 frames at a 218-299 ms median on 5 consecutive pre-checks (f4db0072 RECORD:7-19). The machine test never ran the loop, so only this check could catch it.
No false refusals recorded.
steps.redundant_with: Partly with E01; arm-time cadence is the same measurement.
steps.proposal: No change.
steps.saves: n/a

steps.name: Per-pack smoke (one member per stage in a staged clone, run by fingerprint)
steps.what: A non-claim mini-session before a pack's first session, or whenever the session fingerprint changes (block-6 registration line 358; BYTES registration line 450 'for each sub-pack's first session').
steps.protects: Intended to catch collection-path breakage before a 5-6 h session.
steps.cost: About 50 min per smoke (c634f6f3 RECORD:41). About 13 block-6 smokes (FIX-416-G replay count, 7209d1b0 RECORD:57) plus 6 BYTES pass-1 smokes. Each also sends about 4 false yield.stage_low notices (57e84ae6 RECORD:7-18; 52d50d1f RECORD:15).
steps.caught_real_defects:
A0, B0: no October record credits a smoke with a catch.
- NEG (missed a defect): it passed on r1-bytes-s1-p1 because it writes its own fresh plan_tree.sha256 into its staged copy and skips the bound stage. The real session then collected zero data, losing 265 min (8b6b2b12 RECORD:11,39-40).
- NEG (false hold): smoke_hold #509 on r2-alpha for anchor_fallback_member_unusable, a chance member event that full sessions handle. Judged wrong and resumed; the r2-alpha slot was lost (RS 52; c634f6f3 RECORD:41).
- C: false yield alerts every smoke, because the yield plan carries unreduced counts (RS 48).
Ed's impression that smoke testing improved the loop's success rate (c634f6f3 RECORD:20) is not supported by any recorded catch (INFERRED from absence).
steps.redundant_with: The live machine test (E05) for code changes; first-stage yield (E07) for pack-data defects; CI test test_every_loop_pack_tree_authenticates_through_its_sidecar for the sidecar class (8b6b2b12 RECORD:19,26).
steps.proposal:
1. Make the smoke run the committed pack bytes. It must not write its own sidecar, and it must include the first member of the bound-collection stage, so it tests what the session will read.
2. A smoke never holds a pack on a non-physical member event: physics refuses, everything else is a flag (RS 52).
3. Drop smoke yield alerts, or compute them from the kept counts (RS 48 queued fix).
4. Skip the smoke for a pack whose plan-tree digest and code pin equal a pack that already passed a smoke or a counting session at that pin, and rely on E07's first-stage abort instead.
steps.saves: About 50 min x 6 BYTES pass-2 sub-packs, about 5 h of quiet Mac per pass, plus the avoided false holds (one rotation slot in October).

steps.name: Live machine test (installs a full night job at a pin and injects faults; about 40-70 min)
steps.what: Exercises the night driver, agent pause, idle admission and cap, samplers, keep-awake, smoke desk and harvest on the real Mac at the candidate pin.
steps.protects: Collection-path and desk defects that only show on the real Mac with real launchd and real archives.
steps.cost: About 1 h 10 min of Mac time per live run (d34bf254 RECORD:48), plus a fix round and re-pin after each failure. 3 runs, 10-16 to 10-17.
steps.caught_real_defects:
Run 1, MT-20261016T2114Z (RS 41):
- B: smoke `prepare` left a stale plan_tree sidecar, so 'round 1 could never have armed'.
- A: the `agent.presence` flag was built without monotonic_raw_ns and rejected, so 'round 1 could have counted' an agent-overlapping run.
- C: courier stub, 34 min lost; classify called a crash 'physics'.
Run 2, MT-20261017T1735Z (RS 43; d34bf254 RECORD:27-38):
- A: block 5's busy-fraction veto silently excluded busy-only runs and references, which 'changes the survivor set and the drift bound'.
- B: a cap-skip read as missing_stage_bundles, and smoke.classify would hold the loop.
Run 3, MT-20261017T2215Z: PASS, D (RS 44).
Miss: it never ran the loop's own launchd job, so the ProcessType Background defect slipped (f4db0072 RECORD:18).
steps.redundant_with: Nothing else exercises the live path. The pr501 cold passes found the same busy-veto class on the archive the machine test produced.
steps.proposal: Keep it as the gate for any collection-path code change. Extend it to install the loop's own rendered plist, so the ProcessType class is caught. Also run one BYTES-pack variant through the real controller with committed pack bytes, which would have caught the s1-p1 sidecar before a 265-min session. Run it only at pin changes, never per fix commit.
steps.saves: Protective: each of runs 1-2 prevented at least one full round (about 3 sessions x 5-6 h) of non-counting or wrongly counted data.

steps.name: Lead rehearsal of real programs (dry prepare, driving the chain's own commands on a staged pack, trial re-harvest, throwaway-clone re-proof) and real-archive replay old vs new
steps.what: Runs the real programs over real-shaped data before an arm or a merge. For #416: replay of all 25 real desk archives after every rule change. For L9: the S10 joined chain on synthetic windows.
steps.protects: Plumbing and guard code that refuses or misreads real data: wrong ledger file, symlink pins, over-refusal of real archives.
steps.cost: Minutes to an hour each. L9 S10 rounds took hours (PL OP-9 'rounds of hours').
steps.caught_real_defects:
A2:
- The #416 replays 'caught one over-refusal of real data each time a rule changed' (H's uncollected references; the zero-run archive): 'these touch which data count' (7209d1b0 RECORD:116, items 22, 29).
B at least 5:
- The H rehearsal caught the git-through-symlink INPUTS_ONLY defect in the first fix (f1f6b9f1 RECORD:39).
- A trial re-harvest caught the uncommitted-pin refusal (df31cb27 RECORD:91).
- The clone re-proof caught 2 freeze blockers (desk-day-v5 00-session-record:327).
- The S10 joined chain found nine guard defects refusing real data (PL OP-9 C65).
- The full-size synthetic dry run exposed the step 9b wall-deadline refusal (RS 77).
Miss: the a69c5394 rehearsal did not drive the reservation or the capture, so H's second arm stopped at the pre-calibration capture, 0 runs, about 1 h 10 min (f1f6b9f1 RECORD:8,38).
steps.redundant_with: E05 for the live path. CI never sees real archives.
steps.proposal:
1. Turn the two ad-hoc tools (`rehearse_real.py`, a69c5394; the 25-archive replay, 7209d1b0) into one committed harness. One mode drives every chain command of a staged pack in order, including reservation, capture, one member and verdict. The other replays every archive on disk under old and new code and diffs stops and columns, with structure-only output.
2. Make the harness mandatory for any change that touches refusal, membership or export code.
3. Run the archive replays per archive in a process pool.
steps.saves: The 1 h 10 min H second-arm loss in October. Each automated run replaces about 30-60 min of lead hand-work.

steps.name: Yield accounting and yield alerts (yield.json, yield.stage_zero / stage_low notices)
steps.what: The desk counts present, raw-valid and succeeded runs per stage; the watchdog mails stage-zero and stage-low alerts.
steps.protects: Accepting a session that silently collected nothing.
steps.cost: Seconds. But the catch arrives only at the desk, after the whole chain.
steps.caught_real_defects: B1, late: r1-bytes-s1-p1 had 143/143 members refused in about 0.4 s each, and the alert came after the chain. The session cost 265 min of quiet Mac (8b6b2b12 RECORD:7,38-40). It confirmed the fix on s2-s4, with 125/125 each (118cc6cb RECORD:13; abb6de94 RECORD:13). C: false smoke alerts (E04).
steps.redundant_with: None for zero-yield detection.
steps.proposal: Add a first-stage abort to the loop. If the first collection stage ends with succeeded = 0 and every member failed before reaching its idle baseline (a non-physical refusal), stop the chain, mark the attempt not counting with that cause, and hold the pack. This changes no estimator or exclusion, because the session would not count anyway.
steps.saves: About 4 h of quiet-Mac time per such incident; s1-p1 needed only about 30 min to show the defect (RS 71 pointer: 'about 30 min after t0').

steps.name: Collection-time records refusals in the controller and driver (plan-tree sidecar authentication, lineage config inventory, chain stop on a capture-ledger refusal)
steps.what: Integrity checks that refuse members or stop the chain when a records artifact is missing or mismatched.
steps.protects: Running members whose config bytes cannot be authenticated. The lineage inventory is what checks each config's bytes (a69c5394 RECORD:10).
steps.cost: s1-p1: 265 min (8b6b2b12 RECORD:40). H arm 1: refused at launch, 0 runs (a69c5394 RECORD:7). H arm 2: about 1 h 10 min (f1f6b9f1 RECORD:38).
steps.caught_real_defects:
A0. B3 or more, and in each case the refusal itself was the loss:
- The sidecar refusal 'cost one whole session ... and protected no number. It is a pruning candidate' (8b6b2b12 RECORD:40).
- The lineage inventory gap: the remedy was to supply the record, not weaken the check (a69c5394 RECORD:10,31).
- The ledger split: 'caught a real plumbing defect ... no number' (f1f6b9f1 RECORD:38).
steps.redundant_with: The new CI test that every loop pack authenticates through its sidecar (991358f73), and E06 rehearsals.
steps.proposal: Under the 10-05 doctrine ('physics refuses; everything else is a flag'), the sidecar refusal becomes a flag at collection. Its catch has moved to CI before the pin, per 8b6b2b12 RECORD:28 and the pruning note in RS 71. Keep the lineage config-byte identity check as a refusal, because it is the R core. Keep E06's chain-command rehearsal as the place these are caught before a session.
steps.saves: Up to one session (about 4-6 h) per records defect.

- r3-alpha: 2 (RS 56).
- r4-alpha: 2 (RS 59).

- a verdict-writer path removed BETA a1 (RS 15).
C: representation-only flags compared against block-5 references (code.executed_differs_from_sealed, whole_window.*) on every block-6 and BYTES session (6e0b27ca RECORD:12-14; abb6de94 RECORD:5).

Whether the harvest needs Mac-local ledger locators and historical captures (RS 34) is unverified, so mark that INFERRED.

steps.cost: About 25-60 min each, plus a fix round per round. #416 ran 7 delta rounds x 2 seats from 10-24 11:5x to 10-25 00:2x, about 12.5 h wall, before the registration gate (7209d1b0 RECORD:16-88). #573 ran about 9 rounds (a-i) over about 2 days (786c0858 RECORD:10-44).

A, about 10 first-round catches:

- B2 NR1: C_j not conservative (283e9802 RECORD:22-24).

- #573: the twin could not read .zst, 185 fields above the bar; a REFUSE because re-reduction degraded and the NEG-8 mint recorded a good member as an accepted drop (786c0858 RECORD:10,27).

- #577: the harvest copy kept the old rules (786c0858 RECORD:9).
- Seal: C66 sign error (PL MG-5).
B:

- #416 round 4: BYTES smokes would stop at export; round 6: smoke tree witness (7209d1b0 RECORD:55,73).
- #577: H2 could refuse an arm on missing evidence (786c0858 RECORD:9).

C/D:
- #416 rounds 4-7 'edge cases ... No number' (7209d1b0 RECORD:112).
- Fable PASS with no defect on #470-#473, #476, #477 (desk-day-v5:325-326).
- L9 ruling cold: ACCEPT WITH CHANGES, no refusal (RS 56).
- Recurrence pattern: the same defect class came back 3 times in #416 (reference drop), 3 in #573 (storage), 3 in #574 (parser), and was ended each time by a lead structural ruling, not another round (7209d1b0 RECORD:31; 786c0858 RECORD:28,34).
steps.redundant_with: E13 (one executing review) and E15 (the triple audit) on the same head. On data-path code, E06's real-archive replay caught over-refusals the passes missed.
steps.proposal:
1. First round on number-bearing code: two blind families, executing. Keep this, because it is where the A catches are.
2. Delta rounds: one seat, scoped to the fix diff, plus E06's real-archive replay as a deterministic check.
3. Stopping rule, already adopted ad hoc at 7209d1b0 RECORD:66: stop at the first delta with no HIGH that touches a number or which data count, and disposition the lows.
4. When the same defect class recurs twice, the lead writes a structural rule (as with StorageStop(BaseException)) instead of a third round.
5. Collection-path-only or records-only code: one executing review (E13), no cold pair.
6. For block-6 analysis code, §13 requires 'one blind executing cold pass by Fable and one by Opus'. Moving them to before the release, as in ED-RULING item 3, needs a §17 entry.
steps.saves: In #416, stopping after round 3 with structural rules would have cut about 4 rounds, about 6-8 h wall (7209d1b0 RECORD:41-88). Similar for #573 and #574 (INFERRED, about 1 day each).

steps.name: Block-5 seal machinery: erratum chain, prospective-only rule, harvest pins per erratum, calibration-acceptance staleness
steps.what: After the seal, any rule change was a prospective cold erratum (draft, refuter, judge, text gate, new harvest pin). Corrected rules never applied to completed attempts.
steps.protects: Rules fixed before data (the R core: pre-registration).
steps.cost: Three errata of about 10 h, 3 h and 3.5 h (PL OP-5). Four harvest pins, about 12-20 h (PL HV-29). Prospective-only kept BETA a1, a4 and a5 out, about 18 h of collected sessions (PL section 1, K13/K17; OP-6). The staleness trigger cost BETA a4 and a5, 12 h: 'each spent six hours on a session the harvest was bound to refuse' (RS 24).

steps.proposal: For future blocks this is already replaced: block 6 §12.4 uses a dated §17 entry plus one executing refuter, and prints the original rule's result beside the change. Apply the same form to BYTES pass 2 and DIFFICULTY. Block-5 collection is closed, so its §10 machinery now matters only if a block-5 rule is touched. map.amendment_rules:
Governing texts, quoted:

(1) Block-5 registration §10 (jw:configs/campaigns/v5_claim_25g83/registration_block5.md:5144-5146 and 5156-5157):
- "None to §§3–9 for an armed or completed attempt. A rule, threshold, catalog effect, roster or blinding change is a prospective cold erratum (one judge, one refuter), settled in one erratum."
- "A review finding that concerns only how something is recorded (receipts, naming, schema formality) is dispositioned "flag, not refuse" and never sent to a fix round."
So E22's change to plan step 12 is a change to how the result is checked, not to what is computed. It needs a dated blind amendment to B5-PLAN made before release (b5_plan_amendment). The cadence plan header (jw:docs/design/analysis_cadence_plan.md:4-6) agrees: "Items marked **amend** change *how* a number is computed, and need a dated, blind amendment before the data they apply to are opened."

(2) Block-6 registration §12.4 (jw:docs/registrations/block6_replication_DRAFT.md:1168-1173):
- "No change to registered arithmetic after any block-6 data exists. A rule of §8 found wrong may be changed while block 6 is blinded, by a dated entry in §17 checked by one executing refuter; it then applies to every session, and the result under the original rule is printed beside it."
§13 (lines 1183-1186) requires the analysis code be "independently reviewed by executing them, and given one blind executing cold pass by Fable and one by Opus." Moving or merging those cold passes (E14) is therefore a b6_s17_entry. §12.3 (line 1161) already states "There is no separate cold gate".

(3) ED-RULING item 7 (jw:docs/process_traces/2026-10-27-l9-restart/ED-RULING.md:84-86): "Where the block-6 registration itself requires a synthetic stage chain before its blind run, that requirement stands until amended by a dated entry under its §17 rules."

(4) BYTES registration, order of gates (bytes:docs/registrations/bytes_pack_v1.md:450):
- "the whole test suite run on the laptop on the final integrated pass-1 tree before the registration gate, and not while measuring (Addendum 2; P0 ruling 11); this registration's cold gate ...; then, for each sub-pack's first session, the smoke by fingerprint"
Moving the suite to the Air (E11) or lightening the smoke (E04) for pass 2 is a bytes_registration_amendment made while BYTES is blinded.

(5) Ed's standing principle (2026-10-27, verbatim in the task): "meta rules be damned, the only real rule is good science at a speedy cadence".
Process-only rules (E10, E12, E14 deltas, E15, E16, E17, E24) carry no registration text, so they change by process_rule_change. The two exceptions are §13 above and the BYTES order line.
