science.segment: Empirical ledger: what each check actually caught (October 2026), verified under the science-protection skeptic lens

judgments.reason: The proposal keeps every physical check and only changes who runs it: the loop's pre-arm script instead of an agent. The clock hold already moved to the measured-rate rule (7209d1b0 RECORD item 4: 'the arm clock hold by measured rate'), and the frequency word never refused in 44 reads (RECORD item 2). Automating it removes one reason for an agent to be on the Mac. It does not remove a protection.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: None that reaches a number, provided the script still refuses on the physical criteria (battery, AC, sleep assertion, disk P) and records each value in arm.json. The only risk is that the automated version reports PASS when a probe fails, for example a pmset call that errors. Unmeasured must stay a refusal, as the hazard census does.
evidence_refs: jw:docs/process_traces/2026-10-24-magistrate-7209d1b0/RECORD.md item 4 (arm clock hold by measured rate)

judgments.reason: The check is unchanged and the proposal removes its cause. A daemon reaper and moving agents to the Air add protection; they take none away.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: None for numbers. Caveat: if the orchestrator on the Air reads the Mac over ssh, the census pattern ([c]odex|[c]laude) does not match sshd, so that is safe. Any helper it starts on the Mac must not be named codex or claude, or it will be counted as an agent (INFERRED).

judgments.reason: It made a real physical catch (mediaanalysisd), and it was the only check that caught the ProcessType Background cadence defect.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: n/a (kept).

judgments.reason: The smoke protects sessions, not numbers. But the proposal contradicts itself, and it relies on a check that does not exist yet. Item 1 wants the smoke to catch the s1-p1 sidecar class. Item 2 says a smoke never holds on a non-physical member event. The s1-p1 failure was exactly that: 143 of 143 members raised ArmReadinessError, a records refusal, not physics (8b6b2b12 RECORD:7). Under item 2, the fixed smoke would see the defect, flag it, and let the 265-minute session run anyway. Item 4 (skip by digest) falls back on E07's first-stage abort, which is unbuilt. The BYTES order line also requires the smoke 'for each sub-pack's first session' (bytes_pack_v1.md:450).
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: A repeat of the s1-p1 class: a pack defect that makes every member refuse for a non-physical reason. The smoke runs the committed bytes and reproduces the refusal, but under item 2 it only flags it. The pack is not held, and a full 4.5-6 h session collects zero. If item 4 has also skipped the smoke and E07 is not yet live, nothing catches it before the desk. Fix: the smoke holds when every member of a stage refuses with the same error (systematic), whatever its class, and flags only isolated member events such as #509's anchor_fallback. Do not adopt item 4 until E07 is merged and machine-tested.

judgments.reason: Runs 1 and 2 each caught a defect that would have changed a number or which data count (agent.presence rejected; busy-veto survivor set). The two extensions, installing the loop's own plist and adding a BYTES variant with the committed bytes, add coverage.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: n/a (kept, extended).

judgments.reason: This turns ad-hoc replays that caught over-refusals of real data into a committed, mandatory harness. That is a net gain in protection (7209d1b0 RECORD:116).
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: Blinding, not numbers. The #416 replays ran on H and BY-H2, which are non-claim archives, and printed value-level diffs. If the committed harness diffs 'columns' on blinded claim archives (block 6, BYTES pass 1), an energy column in the diff would unblind. The harness must make structure-only output a hard mode for any archive under withheld/ custody, not leave it to the brief.

judgments.reason: Detecting a zero yield earlier is right. But the claim that the abort 'changes no estimator or exclusion, because the session would not count anyway' is unverified. In BYTES, cell.below_minimum is cell-level and 'never stops a stage' (7209d1b0 RECORD item 3, citing §6). So a session whose first collection stage yields zero can still count for its other cells, unless that stage is the NEG-8 reference corpus that every bound needs (8b6b2b12 RECORD:7). A new controller stop rule is also new collection-path code. It needs the machine test (E05), and it may need BYTES registration text, because the registration defines stop conditions.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: Example: the first collection stage is one model's claim cell, and its members all fail before the idle baseline for a cause local to that stage (one model's weights path or config missing). The abort ends the session, and the other cells, which would have met their minimum and counted, are never collected. That changes which data exist and unbalances the pass. Fix: abort only when the refusal is session-global (the same error on the first member of stage 1 and of the next stage), or when stage 1 is the reference corpus stage.

judgments.reason: plan_tree.sha256 is a self-sidecar: the hash of plan_tree.json, stored next to it (bytes:joulewise/arm_readiness.py:4549-4573). The pack registrations already map lineage.plan_tree_digest_differs to DISCLOSE (bytes:configs/b6/packs/*/registration.json, e.g. line 172). So the registration itself treats a tree-digest difference as disclose-only. In hazard mode the controller keeps 'every session/slot/plan/custody/digest/T1 term' as a refusal (bytes:joulewise/controller.py:888-896), and the lineage config-byte check stays a refusal.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: Narrow: if a byte MISMATCH (not a missing sidecar) also became a flag, a plan tree edited locally on the measurement checkout would run. That checkout is cherry-picked onto a local pin and not exactly CI'd (8b6b2b12 RECORD item 10), and the edited tree would only be disclosed. Condition: flag only an absent sidecar; keep readiness_pack_digest_mismatch a refusal.

judgments.reason: Retargeting the representation-only block-6 flags is fine (6e0b27ca RECORD:12-14). Three parts are unsafe or rest on a false premise. (1) The stated redundancy is false. The independent recompute does NOT re-derive member exclusions from raw monitors. It reads the harvest's derived/exclusions.json (recompute:544-551), and its docstring says 'Selection, anchors, timing bounds and calibration fits are input judgments' (recompute:4-5). PL AN-18's widened scope is not implemented on lane/2026-10-14-independent-recompute (head 9ca87bce). So the harvest is the single source of which members count. (2) Off-Mac harvest: the harvest runs the same calibration replay under the frozen 120 s wall deadline (cadence plan §2.1 says the harvest uses physics_cache; ED-RULING item 6 relies on 'the same calibration completed at harvest' on the quiet Mac). That deadline fired at about 5.6x on a shared VM (RS 77). (3) code.executed_differs_from_sealed is representation-only in block 6, but in block 5 a difference removes the next window (registration_block5.md §10, ~5151). Retargeting must not touch block-5 catalogs.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: (a) The harvest runs on the Air or a cloud VM, the calibration replay hits the 120 s wall deadline, and the window's acceptance or member set differs from what the Mac would produce. Re-running the same session on another host then gives a different verdict, which a reviewer can rightly call non-reproducible. (b) Because nothing independently re-derives exclusions, a harvest exclusion bug, like the busy-veto silent exclusion (RS 43), is not caught by the recompute agreement, though the map claims it would be. Keep the harvest on the Mac until the governed deadline fix (cadence plan §2.4) lands. Change flag code only at a pass or pin boundary, never mid-pass, since BYTES pass 1 collects from one frozen pin (7209d1b0 item 9).

judgments.reason: CI stays the one whole-suite run. Measurement checkouts are cut from CI-green heads (8b6b2b12 RECORD decisions). Splitting shard 10 and skipping CI on WIP pushes does not reduce what the merged or pinned head is tested against.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: Only if the quarantined contention-sensitive job becomes non-required, or if a measurement pin is taken from a head that skipped CI. Condition: the quarantine job stays a required status, and every pin head must have green CI. #573's preflight-refusal catch came from CI (786c0858 RECORD:19).
evidence_refs: jw:docs/process_traces/2026-10-25-magistrate-8b6b2b12/RECORD.md (Decisions: measurement checkouts cut from CI-green heads)

judgments.reason: Recorded catches: A0, B0 (786c0858 RECORD:40,47; 7209d1b0 RECORD:115). The proposal keeps the full laptop suite once per registration, so the registered order is not dropped.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: Weak path: the Air's macOS version, chip and Python differ from the measurement venv (ci.yml marks 3.13 at /opt/homebrew/bin/python3.13 as the production nights interpreter). A macOS-only hazard regression could then pass on the Air and fail on the Mac. Condition: match the Air's macOS major version and Python, and keep the once-per-registration full run on the measurement Mac's own venv.

judgments.reason: 'Keep only the frozen estimator-file check' goes further than the evidence. (1) L9's test_frozen_files.py freezes only block-5 sealed inputs (the v5_claim_25g83 files, d117 v5 packs and block-5 seal pins; l9:tests/b5_analysis/test_frozen_files.py:10-30). Required CI step 'Hard-coded pins that protect a number are current' (repin --check, bytes:.github/workflows/ci.yml:109-112) covers kind-P families, which are by definition the ones that protect numbers: estimator_code ('an acceptance or floor was issued against it'), calibration_issued, floor_artifact and pack_config_bytes for block 6 and BYTES (bytes:configs/pins/registry.json). Making it advisory leaves the block-6 and BYTES issued pins without a merge fence. (2) The executing_reviews review-row test enforces that E13 actually happened on a head. E12's 'redundant with E13' is circular. (3) PL MG-22 explicitly keeps the orphan-process census (OP-24). An orphaned test hazard monitor (pid 43816) ran through the quiet kit and inflated c_q, corrected 0.73 to 0.54 (1a1261a5 RECORD:20,26).
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: A BYTES pass-2 or block-6 analysis seat changes an estimator_code or pack_config_bytes file that an acceptance was issued against. repin is now advisory and test_frozen_files does not list that file, so it merges green. The analysis runs on code that differs from what the acceptance was issued against, unless a runtime SHA binding refuses. That binding is unverified here for every consumer. Separately: a leaked fixture process runs during a quiet capture and biases a registered constant, as c_q was. Keep repin --check required for kind-P only, keep OP-24, and make the rest advisory.

judgments.reason: It is the main source of A catches (PL MG-4, :454). Letting first-round cold passes serve as the review, as pr501 did, keeps at least one executing non-author seat.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: n/a (kept). Only risk: if a cold pass that is not executing (read-only) is counted as 'the review', the executing property is lost. Require execution.

judgments.reason: The map calls #416 rounds 1-3 'first-round catches', but they were DELTA rounds. They ran after the triple audit and fix seats, on the fix range (7209d1b0 RECORD items 10, 12). Each A in them was found by only one of the two families. Round 1: Fable REFUSE (a reference silently dropped on a read failure) while Opus said ADMIT-WITH-CORRECTIONS. Round 2: Opus (E_ref 37.121 to 37.089 J). Round 3: Fable (an unauthenticated roster; allowance +16%) (RECORD:106-111). 'Delta rounds: one seat, scoped to the fix diff' would therefore have missed about half of the A catches in the very rounds cited. The real-archive replay (E06) found over-refusals, not these silent drops or wrong allowances, so it does not cover the same failure.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: #416 delta round 1 run as one Opus seat: ADMIT-WITH-CORRECTIONS, no HIGH touching a number. The stopping rule fires and the silent reference drop on a read failure ships. A BYTES reference whose trace fails to read disappears from the NEG-8 corpus, and E_ref and the allowance are printed from the reduced set. Keep two blind families on every delta round of number-bearing code until a delta round is clean in both; use one seat only for collection-path or records-only deltas. The stopping rule and the structural-rule-after-two-recurrences parts are fine.

judgments.reason: 'Drop the third seat' rests on #416 alone, where Astra missed the reference span. In the seal campaign's triple audit (Fable, Astra, Opus at a434e363d), Astra's A1, 'Excluded NEG-8 references retain influence over claim uncertainty' (EXECUTED), is C18 W: 30 J of contamination passed the screen (PL :456). Fable's report has no reference or allowance finding (30-triple-audit-fable.md: no match for reference, allowance or contamination), and its verdict was 'ARM-READY (no BLOCKER)'. The Opus report was never found (00-seal-and-arm-record.md:236). So in one of the two recorded triple audits, the third seat alone made an A catch. It is not shown that Fable and Opus would have found it.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: The next frozen head (for example BYTES pass 2) has a defect of the C18 class: an excluded reference still feeding the drift allowance. Under the merge, only Fable and Opus audit. In the seal run Fable missed exactly this, and Opus's result is unknown. cadence.segment: Empirical ledger: what each check, gate, review round, machine test, smoke, cold pass, council and audit actually caught in October 2026
cadence.lens: CADENCE SKEPTIC: challenge every KEEP (does it protect a printed number; is there a cheaper, parallel, earlier or off-Mac form with the same protection), check that proposals go far enough, and list missed parallelism

judgments.reason: The census protects a printed number. Agent load inside a measured phase is physical contamination, and the harvest's agent.presence exclusion is the after-the-fact half of it. Verified: s6-p1 dropped agent-overlap units (a46602ae RECORD:5). The census itself is already a cheap script (AGENT_CENSUS_ARGV, a46602ae RECORD:4). The cost was its cause plus slow recovery, not the check. The proposal stops short in two places. (1) Of the ~15-20 h claimed, BY-H2's 9.5 h was not the census's cost. It was notice latency: the refusal came at t0 22:22 PDT 10-22, and no magistrate acted until 07:43 the next morning (0277c5ab RECORD:1). The re-arm was routine (0277c5ab RECORD:5). Add automatic re-arm or retry by the loop when the census clears, or have the watchdog wake an Air-hosted orchestrator at once. Either cuts that class of loss whatever the cause. (2) The reaper should stop only named daemons (the codex app-server daemon and pid-update-loop, a46602ae RECORD:4). It must never SIGTERM an interactive session, because 0277c5ab RECORD:4 shows killing Ed's session needs his standing permission. Moving the orchestrator to the Air is right (RS 39 bullet 3, RUN_STATE.md:81). Whether it can reach the Mac over ssh without argv matching `[c]odex|[c]laude` (for example, paths under ~/.claude) is INFERRED and should be tested once with the arm census in dry mode.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: Unchanged recovery path: an agent census refusal at night idles the quiet Mac until the next scheduled activation, as with BY-H2 (9.5 h). An overbroad reaper kills Ed's live session mid-work.

judgments.reason: PRECHECK is already the cheapest form: a scripted, launchd-run physical measurement with no model in the loop. It caught a CPU hog (mediaanalysisd 1.86-1.91 CPU-s/s against a 0.05 limit; 6789ef94 RECORD:8). It also caught a throttled sampler (median 218-299 ms against 150 ms; f4db0072 RECORD:7-14). Both would contaminate phase energies, so it protects a printed number. One cheap addition moves part of it earlier: a static CI assertion that every rendered launchd template carries ProcessType Interactive. The fix 1706257c4 changed the test's assertion for the loop plist only (f4db0072 RECORD:22); extend it to all night or loop templates. Cost on 10-17 was about 1 h of WAIT_PHYSICS. That was a true positive, not ceremony.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: Without it, a session collects under a background hog or a 250-300 ms sampler cadence, and phase edges and energies are corrupted.

judgments.reason: Keep the live machine test for collection-path changes only. The auditor's trigger, 'only at pin changes', is too broad, because desk-only fixes also re-pin. Evidence: run 2's three number-touching defects were all desk side ('All three defects are on the desk side; there is no collection fault', d34bf254 RECORD:25-26). The pr501 cold passes reproduced and verified them by running the code on the stored MT-20261017T1735Z archive (pr501-gates.md:8-9), with no live Mac time. So for a change that touches only desk, harvest or verdict code, the gate can be a replay of the stored machine-test archive or real archives (E06 harness). That replay can run on the Air or in the cloud on copies. Spend the live 70-min run (d34bf254 RECORD:47-49) only when controller, driver, smoke-prepare or launchd code changes. Run 1's collection-side catches would also have been caught earlier and cheaper: the agent.presence flag schema defect (a driver test used build_flag, which skips the schema; RS 41) and the stale sidecar (now a CI test, 991358f73). Both are now unit-test classes. The lead chose a live rerun on 10-17 partly because the Mac was idle anyway (d34bf254 RECORD:46-49). That is not true while BYTES is collecting.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: With 'every pin' as the trigger, each desk-only fix costs about 70 min of quiet-Mac time plus a re-pin cycle. That time competes with BYTES sessions and the block-5 dry run (ED-RULING 6a gives the Mac to analysis first). The protection is the same as a stored-archive replay.

judgments.reason: A non-author executing review is the one check that repeatedly caught defects that changed which data count. Verified: in the L9 S0-S3 catches in RS 33/35, one archive was indexed as another's. The pr501 writer veto touched survivors. ED-RULING item 1 keeps exactly one such review for L9 (ED-RULING.md:46). A cheaper form with equal protection does not exist; a script cannot be independent of its author. Two refinements make it faster. (1) Run it in the cloud concurrently with CI and the E06 replay on the same head, not after CI goes green. In pr501 the review, CI and local runs were separate serial steps (pr501-gates.md:8-16). (2) Adopt the pr501 rule generally: when a blind cold pair runs on the same head, it is the review (pr501-gates.md:13-14). The auditor already proposes that.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: Dropping it lets author-blind defects through, such as an archive indexed as another pack's (RS 33) or busy-only runs silently excluded (d34bf254 RECORD:27-34), each changing the survivor set.

judgments.reason: Councils already run in the cloud while the Mac measures (a46602ae RECORD:7; RS 78). They produced one real blinding-leak catch and one avoided over-strict rule. Their cost is wall time, not Mac time. The M1 structural run on s5-p1 reframed the thermal question cheaply before round 2 (a46602ae RECORD:6). That supports a stronger rule than the auditor's: before convening a council on a physical cause, run the deterministic structural locate first (a script over structure only). Then convene only if the result leaves a science question. In thermal70, round 1 asked for M1 and then needed round 2 (a46602ae RECORD:6-7). With M1 first, one round could suffice.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: Two-round councils, where the first round's main output is a request for a measurement the lead could have run beforehand. Each round adds about 30-60 min of wall time and holds a pack, as with s5-p2 held until the ruling passes its gate (a46602ae RECORD:11).

judgments.reason: Both halves protect printed numbers: the blind dry run and the independent recompute agreement. Keep both. The proposal does not go far enough on when the recompute runs. The recompute shares no code with L9 (RS 37). Its lane is merged through PR #571 (recompute git log 9ca87bce), and the scout says only 'pin the reviewed version; run comparison in restricted custody' (BLIND-DRY-RUN-SCOUT.md:36). Block-5 archives are complete and immutable. So the recompute's restricted output for ALPHA, BETA and GAMMA can be produced now, before L9 lands, and the comparison waits only for the dry run's restricted output. That takes the recompute off the critical path entirely; running it beside the dry run is not enough. It is a single stdlib-only script (independent_recompute_b5.py imports: argparse..xml only, lines 18-32), so it is portable to the Air without a venv. Caveat, verified: it reads only uncompressed raw/powermetrics.plist; a .zst input gives trace_plist_missing / not_compared (lines 395-413). So off-Mac transfer needs decompression on arrival, and about 43 GiB per session uncompressed (cadence plan line 15) bounds what the Air can hold at once. Process per session, or add streaming .zst reading as a how-computed change. It is also a serial per-run loop with no pool (no multiprocessing import). A per-run process pool assembled in a fixed order is a cheap speedup, with a byte-equality test.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: As planned, the recompute starts only after L9 merges and the dry run begins. It then adds its own wall time, plus any build round it needs on real bytes, to the release critical path, though it could already have finished.

judgments.reason: Blinding is a science protection under Ed's own KEEP list, so it stays. The cheaper form is mechanical enforcement in place of brief prose. The cadence plan already says 'The machine should run the pipeline as a script, with nothing reading its restricted folder' (analysis_cadence_plan.md:52-54). Make the restricted directory unreadable to the agent's user, or put it on a host the agents cannot reach, and let the driver emit structure only. Then per-brief restricted-reading passages (PL OP-22) become unnecessary, because blinding no longer depends on each model obeying a paragraph. This matters more once seats run on the Air beside restricted copies of real archives.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: Analysis seats on the Air and an orchestrator with read access to restricted recompute or dry-run outputs would rely on prose alone to stay blind. One careless `cat` breaks blinding for a whole block.
evidence_refs: jw:docs/process/pruning_list_2026-10-14.md OP-22 (as cited by the auditor; INFERRED, not re-read)

judgments.reason: I agree with LIGHTEN, but not with placing the one remaining cached full-size synthetic run on the MacBook Air. ED-RULING item 6(c) keeps the 120 s wall deadline. Its stated safety argument is that the dry run runs 'on the quiet Mac, where the same calibration completed at harvest' (ED-RULING.md:63). The Air is a different, fanless machine (INFERRED: chip and cooling not stated anywhere read) and would also host interactive and orchestrator sessions. So it is a shared host, the condition that fired the deadline on the cloud VM (cadence plan:47-48). A deadline firing there is a host-dependent refusal: a wasted 6 h, with no information about the Mac. Put it either in the cloud, accepting a deadline firing as a known diagnostic, or on the Mac between sessions. Better, land the parallel steps 1-2 first (cadence plan §6 row 2), so the run is short wherever it goes.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: A cached full-size run on a passively cooled Air shared with agent sessions trips the 120 s step-9b deadline and is read as an L9 defect. That is the RS 77 misdiagnosis repeated.

judgments.reason: I agree, and the cut should go further. The scout report adds a release cold gate for block 6 that the registration does not require: 'B6 registration §12.3 ... says no separate cold gate ... I retain those merge passes and add the requested release gate' (BLIND-DRY-RUN-SCOUT.md:206). The scout also lists a 'cold gate under this user's instruction' among the block-6 release prerequisites (line 132). That is the same duplication as block-5 step 12. It needs the same fix: the recompute comparison table read by one reviewer. Otherwise the block-6 release reacquires a multi-day gate by scout drift. Whether the 'user's instruction' it cites is still Ed's current wish after 10-27 is INFERRED. Ask Ed in one line.
judgments.concrete_failure_mode: Block 5's step 12 is removed, but block 6's release still waits on a judge plus a refuter re-deriving every printed number. That costs days (cadence plan line 16) and gives no protection beyond the S-13 recompute comparison.

missed_items: Notice-latency loss is not a census cost. BY-H2 was refused at 22:22 PDT and the next magistrate came at 07:43 (0277c5ab RECORD:1). Add loop-level automatic re-arm when the census clears, or an immediate wake of an Air-hosted orchestrator. This recovers idle Mac hours for any refusal cause, not only agents.

The independent recompute can run NOW on block-5 archives into restricted custody. It shares no code with L9 (RS 37), its lane is merged (PR #571), and block 5 is closed. Only the comparison needs L9's dry-run output. That takes it off the release critical path rather than merely running it beside the dry run.

The recompute is serial, stdlib-only and plist-only. It refuses .zst inputs as not_compared (independent_recompute_b5.py:395-413). Off-Mac use needs decompression on arrival, or a blind how-computed amendment for streaming .zst. A per-run process pool with fixed-order assembly and a byte-equality test is a cheap speedup.

The live machine test should be split by what changed. Desk-only changes can be verified by replaying a stored machine-test archive or real archives off the Mac, as the pr501 passes did on MT-20261017T1735Z (pr501-gates.md:9). Live Mac time is only needed for controller, driver, smoke-prepare or launchd changes.

The scout report adds a block-6 release cold gate beyond the registration (BLIND-DRY-RUN-SCOUT.md:132,206). It should be merged into the S-13 recompute comparison, as E22 does for block 5. The same scout line 67 still lists the full pre-ED-RULING L9 gate sequence and should be marked superseded by ED-RULING item 1.

The block-6 identical-byte release replay (scout line 132) is a deterministic full rerun. Schedule it on whichever host is idle (Air or cloud, from verified copies) in parallel with the release record, not serially on the Mac.

Physical-cause councils should get a deterministic structural locate before round 1. M1 on s5-p1 (a46602ae RECORD:6) settled what round 1 left open. Running that kind of script first saves a council round.
A static CI assertion that every rendered launchd template (loop, night, after-jobs) has ProcessType Interactive. That moves the f4db0072 class from PRECHECK, at 1 h of WAIT_PHYSICS, to merge time.
Blinding should be enforced by filesystem permissions or host separation (cadence plan:52-54), not brief prose, before any seat on the Air sits beside restricted copies of real archives.

The Air should not host the cached full-size L9 synthetic run while the 120 s wall deadline stands (ED-RULING item 6c relies on the quiet Mac). It is a shared, likely fanless host (INFERRED), so a firing there is uninformative.
